author: lati-cooki
body:
Closes #63. Closes #64. Closes #51.

Three companion milestones on the engine-integrity spine: what the event log commits to (M37), what a continuity packet commits to (M38), and what the validator and projector agree exists (M39). All hold the M0 pruning discipline — no new protocol event types, no projection-semantics change, no validator reasoning change.

## M37 — Transitive Head Commitment (`event_hash.v2`, #63)

**Gap:** v1's hashed material excluded `previous_hash`, so an event's `content_hash` committed to its own fields but not its predecessor. The head hash was only a per-event checksum — head-only / suffix-only attestation was unsound.

**Fix:** Add `clista.event_hash.v2`, which retains `previous_hash` in the hashed material (excludes only `content_hash`). Each `content_hash` now commits to its predecessor, so the head becomes a rolling commitment to the whole prefix.

- `computeEventHash` already branches on `hash_version`, so v1/legacy events verify unchanged. Default append still stamps v1 — replay stays byte-identical; v2 is opt-in per event.
- New `verifyEventSuffix` + `clista integrity verify-suffix --anchor <head>`: verify an appended suffix against a trusted head alone — sound only under v2.

## M38 — Projector-Aware Continuity Verification (#64)

**Gap:** A continuity packet is verified later on a different checkout, but it stored a `projection_hash` with nothing identifying which projector computed it. A verifier whose projector differed recomputed a different hash and failed with a bare `projection_hash does not match recomputed value` — indistinguishable from a corrupt packet, even for byte-identical, valid events.

**Fix:** Declare `PROJECTION_VERSION` (the projector's output-contract identity) in `src/projector.js` and record it in every packet. On verify, a differing `projection_version` reports an honest `projector mismatch: … regenerate the packet or align the checkout` and skips the projector-dependent recompute comparisons. Events are still fully integrity/validity-checked; the packet's own `state_hash` must still commit to its `continuity_state`. `projection_version` is optional — legacy packets keep verifying against a matching projector.

## M39 — Event-Type Registry / drift guard (#51)

**Gap:** The validator and projector each dispatch on `event_type` through a large `switch` with no shared source of truth. The defaults are asymmetric — validator rejects unknown types loudly, projector falls through a silent `default: break` — so a type added to one switch but missed by the other slips through the silent side (the #40/#45 fail-open class). Four validated types reached the projector default.

**Fix:** `src/event-types.js` declares `PROTOCOL_EVENT_TYPES`, the single canonical registry. author: jsboige
body:
## What

Removes the dysfonctional `Microsoft.XmlSerializer.Generator` 8.0.0 NuGet package from the main project → **main project build goes from 2 warnings to 0**. Dispatch `3i1ie4` [SECONDAIRE] SGEN/XmlSerializer.

## Diagnosis

The main project emitted 2 `MSB3073`/SGEN warnings on every build:

```
dotnet Microsoft.XmlSerializer.Generator "...Argumentum.AssetConverter.dll" --force --quiet "...sgen.rsp"
La version du package 'Microsoft.XmlSerializer.Generator' n'a pas pu être résolue.
```

`Microsoft.XmlSerializer.Generator` is a **build-time pre-generator** for `System.Xml.Serialization.XmlSerializer`. It needs an `IXmlSerializerDescriptor` configuration to know which types to pre-generate. Grep across the project finds **zero** such descriptor (`XmlSerializerDescriptor` / `[XmlSerializer]` / `IXmlSerializerDescriptor` → 0 matches). The package's build target then tries to invoke itself as a `dotnet tool` and fails to resolve the package version → non-zero exit → `MSB3073`. **The package was already a silent no-op** (no pre-gen assembly produced) while spamming 2 warnings.

The 4 runtime call sites work by reflection without any pre-gen, independent of this package:
- `new XmlSerializer(typeof(FreemindMap))` × 3 (VirtueMindMapDocumentConfig.cs:519, MindMapDocumentConfig.cs:434, FallacyMindMapDocumentConfig.cs:1083)
- `new XmlSerializer(typeof(SexyContentData), new[]{ typeof(Entity) })` (Dnn2sxcConfig.cs:139)

## Fix

Drop the `PackageReference`. `<GenerateSerializationAssemblies>Off</...>` (L.11) stays as the guard that also disables classic .NET SGEN. The package was added in `6edf683c` (MindMap Virtues/Fallacies refactor) — a likely startup-perf attempt that was never wired (no descriptor), so it never worked.

## Validation (empirical)

- `dotnet build` main project: **0 warning / 0 error** (was 2 warnings).
- `dotnet test Argumentum.AssetConverter.Tests`: **587 pass / 1 fail (#133 OWL known-fail) / 5 skip / 593** — baseline intact, 0 regression.

## Discipline

- 0 write `Cards/`, 0 regen, 0 CSV/DB/OWL. Main csproj only (1-line deletion).
- Test counter = empirical `dotnet test`, not a reported figure.
- Net positive: build réellement 0-warning on the main project, tech debt removed (a package that resolved nothing and generated nothing).

body:
## Summary

Extracts the offline sync engine out of `packages/mobile` into a dedicated pure-TS package, **`@boardsesh/offline-sync`** (`packages/shared/offline-sync`), for maintainability. Pure relocation + mechanical seam changes — no engine logic rewrites.

**What moved:** the mutation outbox (`queue`/`drainer`/`handlers`/`error-classification`), the pull client, sync scheduler, checkpoints, `table-config`, the on-device SQLite DDL + migration runner, and the offline board-scope key helpers — plus their test suites (which already ran on `node:sqlite`; the adapter is now exported at `@boardsesh/offline-sync/testing`).

**Platform I/O is injected instead of imported.** The package has zero runtime dependencies:

- structural `SqlExecutor` / `OfflineDatabase` replace `expo-sqlite` types — the real `SQLiteDatabase` is structurally assignable, so mobile passes its handle with no wrapper
- `QueryInvalidator` (one-method slice) replaces the `@tanstack/react-query` dependency; `DrainOptions.isOnline` replaces `onlineManager`
- `SchedulerTriggers` replaces `AppState`/`NetInfo`; `onSchemaDrift` / `onCycleError` replace the Sentry and `__DEV__` console couplings

The mobile binding lives in `packages/mobile/src/offline/offline-sync-adapter.ts`. Rule (documented in the adapter + package docblock): mobile code never imports `drainMutationQueue`/`startSyncScheduler`/`triggerSync`/`pullSync` from the package directly — only via the adapter, so the real connectivity probe is always attached.

**Stays in mobile:** expo DB lifecycle (`connection.ts`, seed ATTACH), local read queries, the sync-status store, hooks, and the bridge component.

**Docs:** `sync-table-manifest.md` now points its DDL/table-config contract at the package paths; `offline-sync-plan.md` gains a "Why an outbox, not dirty flags on the data tables" section recording the design rationale, and CLAUDE.md lists the new package.

## What does this PR do?

Adds an observe-only smart model routing skeleton for Hermes turns. This does not switch the active provider/model, mutate the system prompt, change tool schemas, or affect prompt-cache stability. It only records a pre-turn route decision for later evaluation.

This is intentionally different from per-turn cheap-model swapping: the goal is to gather routing signals first, so future smart routing can become cache-aware instead of causing frequent model churn inside long sessions.

## Summary
- Converts `FileViewer`, `+page.svelte`, `+layout.svelte`, `settings/+page.svelte`, and `v/[code]/+page.svelte` from legacy Svelte syntax to runes, completing the incremental runes migration started after the Svelte 5/Vite 8/TypeScript 6 toolchain bump.

author: zenetusken
body:
## Summary
A DevSecOps pentest confirmed 4 real, independently-verified defects in the secrets
firewall — each reproduced directly (not just accepted from the pentest's votes)
before fixing, and each fix sabotage-verified against the pre-fix behavior.

- **`_entropy_blob` slash-density bypass**: a whole matched blob was exempted from the
  mixed-case/digit check once it held 3+ `/` anywhere. Reproduced: the real AWS example
  key was correctly flagged with 2 slashes, but flipped to unflagged with one more
  trailing `/` appended, and a synthetic slash-chunked keyword-less secret passed
  `extract()` end-to-end with `secrets_omitted:0`. Fixed to judge each `/`-separated
  segment independently.
- **Coverage gaps**: CLI-flag-style values (`--password hunter2`) and Stripe webhook
  secrets (`whsec_...`, under the 40-char entropy floor) bypassed the firewall entirely.
  Added a CLI-flag-shaped keyword arm and a `whsec_` vendor arm. Deliberately did **not**
  add a bare 32-hex arm, a generic `-p<value>` arm, or a scheme-less basic-auth arm —
  all three considered and rejected for false-positive risk (they'd collide with
  `docker run -p8080:80`, `tar -pxvf`, `docker run -u 1000:1000`) now that this firewall
  also gates real commit messages. A dedicated false-positive corpus asserts ordinary
  commits/prose/CLI flags stay unflagged.
- **ReDoS**: `_SECRET`'s unbounded prefix quantifier gave real O(n²) `re.search` blowup
  on attacker-influenceable text. Bounding just the repetition count wasn't sufficient —
  a separator-free payload still triggered an O(remaining-length) backtrack sweep per
  position. Fixed by bounding both the repetition count and each segment's length. The
  same investigation found two more, previously-unflagged instances of the identical bug
  in sibling arms (URI-creds, JWT via a repeated-anchor attack) and fixed both. Verified
  linear scaling to 256,000 chars across every adversarial shape found.
- **Unfirewalled git log**: commit subjects never passed through any secrets-shape
  check — only `_sane()`'s control-byte strip, a different concern. This was the one
  Phase-2 candidate source with no firewall despite SKILL.md framing it as the
  "strongest, highest-precision source." Fixed via a new pure `_scrub_commit_log`
  helper wired into `build_context`; SKILL.md updated.

Structural change: `_SECRET`/`_entropy_blob`/`_looks_secret` are relocated from
`extract_signals.py` to `memory_status.py` (the dependency root, mirroring the existing
`_is_mirror`/`_frontmatter` precedent) since `memory_status.py`'s own commit-log path
needs them and `extract_signals.py` already imports FROM `memory_status.py` (circular
import otherwise). Existing importers resolve them transitively; a smoke pin asserts
single-sourcing.

Independent of and does not overlap with #82 (evict/mirror/check-ignore fixes) — no
shared files touched by both changesets beyond `memory_status.py`/`tests/smoke.py` in
non-conflicting regions.

## Test plan
- [x] `python3 tests/smoke.py` — 747 passed, 0 failed
- [x] `mypy --config-file mypy.ini` — no issues
- [x] `python3 tests/validate_manifests.py` / `tests/simulate_accumulation.py` — pass
- [x] Every regex fix independently reproduced (bypass confirmed, then confirmed fixed)
  against the live code before landing — including two ReDoS instances the pentest
  itself didn't flag, found by extending its own methodology
- [x] A false-positive corpus (ordinary commits, docker flags, real paths, prose) is
  asserted to stay unflagged, since this firewall now also gates real commit messages
- [x] ReDoS guard: 3 adversarial payload shapes (up to 100,000 chars) must complete in
  <1s; sabotage-verified to fail (5-6s at 1/4 the size) against the pre-fix regex

author: mattrickslauer
body:
Turns the runtime-vision half of the Hearth thesis from 100% simulated into a real, verified pipeline: real camera → real Qwen-VL → family-vs-stranger recognition, plus the authoring agent asking for the context it needs.

## 1. Cloud brain: real Qwen-VL vision path (`backend/`)
`chatVisionJSON()` sends real image bytes (base64 or url) to `qwen-vl-plus`; `judge()` routes to vision when frames are attached. `npm run qwen-vl-check` → PASS.

## 2. Hub: a camera is just another sensor (`hub/`)
`hub/camera.mjs` ingests an **OBS RTMP** stream via ffmpeg `-listen` (no MediaMTX) and snaps a JPEG on a cadence — same DESCRIBE/READING path as an ESP node. Frames sampled, never streamed: pulled on demand from `GET /frame`; `GET/POST /camera` retune cadence + quality. `camera-selftest` → PASS.

## 3. Dashboard: live camera tile (`frontend/`)
Pulls the latest frame on the snap cadence with rate/quality sliders (`EXPO_PUBLIC_HUB_URL`).

## 4. Authoring: Qwen suggests the context it needs
Vision wishes return `contextSuggestions` — upload household photos, aim, cadence, quality, lighting — surfaced as a dashboard card. Verified live via `qwen-check`.

## 5. Household reference-photo whitelist — family vs strangers (`backend/`)
Upload a reference photo per household member; at judge time they go to Qwen-VL **before** the live frame so it recognises family by comparison — facial recognition **without a face-embedding model** (keeps Qwen load-bearing). `HouseholdMember` across MemoryStore + Tablestore (durable `hm#` rows); tools `add_household_member` / `list_household` / `remove_household_member`; `JudgeInput.references`. `npm run household-check` → PASS (store CRUD; Qwen-VL distinguished same-subject `same:true` from a different subject `same:false`; production judge returned a real verdict).

## 6. Alibaba OSS provisioner (`backend/scripts/oss-provision.ts`)
Idempotent bucket create + GET CORS + signed-URL round-trip for durable frames/reference images. **Currently blocked** by an account-standing issue (`403 UserDisable`); the vision loop runs on base64 without it, and this passes once the account is re-enabled.

## Remaining (this PR / follow-ups)
- Frontend household **upload UI** (the screen the suggestions point to).
- **Runtime wiring**: hub auto-pulls `/frame` + household references → Qwen-VL judge when a vision watch fires → act. (Closes the live loop.)
- **Metered Stripe billing**: local watches free, cloud reasoning metered per Qwen-VL call (test mode; judges can one-click upgrade). Reuses the account from `~/Code/aws-hackathon`.
- Move reference-image + frame storage to **OSS** once the account clears.

## Verified
`qwen-vl-check`, `camera-selftest`, `qwen-check`, `household-check` all PASS. Backend + frontend typecheck clean.

- Adds a thin `@anthropic-ai/sdk` wrapper (`ClaudeClientService`) that forces structured JSON output via `tool_choice`, plus a Redis-backed per-world daily token budget (`AiBudgetService`).
- `NpcStrategyService`: periodically generates a goal queue per NPC guild (AI or rule-based fallback), persisted to `Guild.aiStrategy`. `NpcService`'s investment executor now consults the highest-priority goal to pick a target port instead of pure home-region random — the executor's atomic action (invest) is unchanged, exactly as flagged in the M7 code comment.

Every attempt is recorded in `AiGenerationLog`.
- `AI_ENABLED=false` (the default dev/CI mode, no API key configured in this environment) keeps the game fully playable purely through the fallback path — this is what was actually exercised in live e2e testing below.

**Deliberately out of scope**, to keep this milestone shippable and fully testable without a live Anthropic API key: the DIALOGUE agent (SSE chat with tavern NPCs/officers) described in docs/06, and the doc's separate BullMQ `ai-gen` queue — both agents instead run as synchronous, fallback-guarded calls inside the existing tick processor, which satisfies the same "AI never stalls the game" invariant with far less moving parts.

author: nykefleym-pbi
body:
## Summary
The product owner noted "you don't see the effects of the abilities in the game." Two fixes:

### 1. Animated status-condition overlays on the affected Pokémon's sprite
New shared `StatusEffectOverlay({ statuses })` component (`src/components/game-ui.tsx`) rendering a visible animated effect directly on/around the sprite (in addition to the existing small status chip in the combat panel):
- **Burn** — flickering flames at the sprite's base
- **Freeze** — translucent icy-blue tint overlay
- **Paralysis** — irregular yellow electric sparks
- **Poison** — purple glow + rising, fading bubbles
- **Badly poisoned** — same as poison plus added purple/pink sparks
- **Sleep** — a floating, bobbing 💤 above the head
- **Confused** — two 💫 stars orbiting the head (counter-rotation trick), able to layer on top of any major status since confusion is the sole stacking volatile

All animations are hand-written `@keyframes` + matching CSS classes in `src/styles.css`, following the existing convention (like `animate-shake`). Emoji + pure CSS — no new assets. Wired into both Solo's sprite wrappers (`battle-screen.tsx`) and Nearby Battle/Training's `ArenaSprite` (`live-pvp-battle-screen.tsx`, both call sites). The separate "Frozen solid!" question-skip takeover UI is untouched.

Note: Solo only tracks confused/poisoned in its own local status state (a pre-existing, intentional scope from the Status Conditions feature), so only those two overlays surface in Solo today; the component handles all 7 generically for when/if Solo's set expands. Nearby Battle/Training shows the full set.

### 2. Toast the effect of previously-silent signature abilities
Pure `passive_damage`-only signature abilities (Freeze-Dry, Stone Edge, the Sacred Sword line, Sunsteel Strike, Collision Course, etc.) folded their bonus silently into the damage number with zero player feedback. Added `describeHitModifiers()` (`src/lib/signature-abilities.ts`) that turns the *actually-resolved* modifiers (ignore-Defense / bonus Attack / bonus Crit / extra hit) into plain text read straight off the ability's own effect payload — so the toast can never drift from the real catalog effect. In `live-pvp-battle-screen.tsx`'s `resolveQuestion`, when such an ability fires with no bundled sub-effect, the acting player now sees `✨ {move} — {effect}!`.

Scoped as a local-only toast for the acting player (no server round-trip): these abilities carry nothing (no stat/status) for the opponent to authoritatively receive, so adding a broadcast would mean touching the core signature RPC (out of scope). Bundled abilities and all other trigger families already toast via the existing `post_answer` / `pvp_live_effects` paths, so this covers only the one confirmed silent case.

## Test plan
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.
- `npx vitest run` — 159/159 passing.
- `eslint` clean on all changed files.
- `npm run build` succeeds.
- Browser-verified via Playwright Chromium: all 7 overlays render distinctly and confusion layers correctly over a major status (temporary preview routes, since removed); also captured confusion rendering live on a real Solo battle sprite, and PvP overlays on a real `ArenaSprite` via a synthetic-state harness (sandbox blocks live Supabase). No temporary route files or route-tree diff remain.

`src/components/game-ui.tsx`, `src/components/battle-screen.tsx`, `src/components/live-pvp-battle-screen.tsx`, `src/lib/signature-abilities.ts`, `src/styles.css`

author: privatejoel
body:
Closes the PO→SO loop with **no manual quote-picking**. You upload the PO; Anvil finds the corresponding quotes itself, matches each line, and runs the **quantitative (price/qty) + qualitative (part/description)** checks — surfacing only the exceptions.

## Why this shape
A real SO routinely draws lines from **multiple quotes** (part families quoted separately). So matching is **per-line against the whole pool** of the customer's quotes — not one hand-linked `quote_id`. Each enriched line is stamped with `source_quote_id`/`source_quote_number` (provenance), and duplicate parts across quotes resolve to the most-recent price and are flagged `ambiguous`.

## Pieces
- **`_lib/quote-reconcile.js`** (pure, 6 tests) — `reconcilePoAgainstQuotes()`: normalized part-no match, multi-quote pool, price-delta tolerance → `price_mismatch`, qty note, exact-vs-normalized + description-agreement, ambiguity. Returns enriched lines + `summary` + `flags`.
- **`POST /api/orders/reconcile_quotes` `{ order_id }`** — auto-pools the customer's non-cancelled quotes, reconciles, persists enriched `salesOrder.lineItems` + a `result.quoteReconciliation` report, links the primary quote (most lines matched). Enrichment is **quote-authoritative on price/HSN/tax** but keeps the PO's own `customer_part_number` (the SO "Cust Part No").
- **Auto-trigger** — `so-intake` runs it right after the PO draft is created (best-effort, non-blocking); the toast shows `quotes N/T matched, X price⚠, Y unmatched`. Large POs re-run once background extraction lands.
- **client** `orders.reconcileQuotes`.

## Safety
Automatic match, but **verification is visible**: price mismatches, unmatched lines, and ambiguous parts are flagged in the stored report and the toast, so a wrong auto-match can't silently mis-price an SO. `discounted_unit_price` is set to the **quoted** rate (authoritative), and the delta vs the PO's stated price is reported.

Feeds the SO voucher renderer (#215) → an ingested PO now yields a complete, priced, verified Sales Order end-to-end. Verify: 6 reconciler tests green; full suite = unchanged local-env baseline.

## Summary
Wires the 6 already-exported occt bindings flagged as Tier 1 "cheap shoulders" in `prompts/BONSAI_KERNEL_RESEARCH.md` §GAP-TO-COMPETITIVE, following the exact recipe `GEOM_LOFT` (#688) proved: worker case + LEAF-set entry + Outliner category + witness, no new math.

- **`GEOM_REVOLVE`** (`kernel.revolve`) — LEAF, fresh self-contained solid (profile+axis+angle, no parent). Highest-value op in this tier: first axisymmetric-solid authoring path (round columns/tanks/turned parts). Axis must lie IN the profile's own plane for a real solid.
- **`GEOM_SHELL`** (`kernel.shell`) — non-LEAF, parent-mutating. New `listFaces`/`queryFaces` §FACE-PICK device mirrors the existing edge-pick.
- **`GEOM_OFFSET`** (`kernel.offset`) — non-LEAF. Simpler than assumed: whole-solid distance+tolerance, no face list.
- **`GEOM_FILLET_VARIABLE`** (`kernel.filletVariable`) — non-LEAF. Real signature takes a SINGLE edge (not an array) + start/end radius.
- **`GEOM_CHAMFER_DIST_ANGLE`** (`kernel.chamferDistAngle`) — non-LEAF, edge array + distance + angleDeg (degrees).
- **`GEOM_DRAFT`** (`kernel.draft`) — non-LEAF, single face. Verified by direct probing: `direction` must be the picked face's own outward normal for a real taper; an unrelated direction is silently a no-op; horizontal faces throw. Documented in-code for the next caller.

**LEAF classification:** only `GEOM_REVOLVE` joins the optimistic-append whitelist (own solid, no parent ref — same class as `GEOM_SWEEP`/`GEOM_LOFT`). The other 5 mutate a referenced parent (same class as `GEOM_CUT`/`GEOM_FILLET`) and take the authoritative re-fold.

author: foxorama
body:
## Why

Off the fairway used to be mostly *light* `rough` (carry 0.9) with only a thin scatter of trees, so a sprayed ball bounced straight through it and paid no real price for missing the hole — it was "far too easy to play through the rough and ignore the actual golf holes."

## What

A new generator pass (**GS-rough-gradient**) fills the off-corridor rough with a distance-graded mix so the rough drives play back toward the fairway:

- a **heavy-rough band** (`deeprough`/`fescue`) hugs the fairway edge, near-continuous so a miss is actually caught;
- beyond it, the world's **trees thicken the further out you go** (measured: verdant at max wildness plants ~`15 / 30 / 48 / 48` trees across the 0–15 / 15–35 / 35–60 / 60+ yard bands off the edge).

Difficulty rides **only the shape**, not fairness (every kind is non-penalty):

- **calm stops** — a wide, recoverable heavy-rough buffer with trees pushed far out (a wild spray lands in deep rough it can hack out of, not the woods);
- **wild stops** (≥ `ROUGH_CHAR_MIN_WILDNESS` 0.45) — a per-hole character roll (tight tree chute / heavy-rough gauntlet / mixed) and the forest thickens with wildness, so hard stops read "a lot more random."

World identity is preserved via `treeDensity` (desert stays scrubby ~16–29 trees; jungle/parkland wall the fairway ~110–148); the ocean keeps a `fescue`-only dune band (its deep-rough is the sea). A `standoff` keeps every blob off the mown centreline route; a `maxLat` cap keeps `playBounds`/the OB box from ballooning.

## Determinism — terrain stays byte-for-byte identical

The pass draws from a **dedicated side stream** (`${seed}:rough:${holeIndex}`, the same pattern the pin/slope/contour use), **not** the main terrain `rng`. So it perturbs zero existing draws: every penalty crossing, green and grove — and `validateCrossings`/`validateFairness` — stay byte-for-byte identical; only the non-penalty rough is *added*. `GENERATOR_VERSION` 18 → 19.

## Balance is deliberately deferred

Per the request (rough/trees first, rebalance next), balance was **not** re-tuned — the course is meaningfully harder now (max-wildness to-par ~1.0–1.4, pick-up rate roughly doubled). Rather than soften the rough to sneak under the death-spiral bars, those fences are relaxed to the interim reality with a greppable `TODO(GS-rough-gradient)` in `tests/{biomes,themes,patches,characters}.test.ts`, and the follow-up (a smarter reach-AI that plays back to the fairway / richer starter bags) is logged as **GS-rough-gradient-rebalance** in `IDEAS.md`. Deep-rough/hazards2 placement assertions were retargeted to "the mown route stays clean."

## Tests

Full suite green — **1020 tests, 103 files** — and `tsc` clean.

body:
## Summary
- Some upstream (Philips) private DICOM elements carry a value whose byte length is incompatible with the VR pydicom infers (e.g. `(01F1,1026)` = 6 bytes read as an 8-byte double).
- On re-encode for the C-MOVE forward, pydicom raised `BytesLengthException`, silently dropping the whole C-STORE sub-operation for any instance carrying such an element.
- Sets `pydicom.config.convert_wrong_length_to_UN = True` so these elements are coerced to UN and relayed verbatim instead of failing to encode.

## Test plan
- [ ] Forward a study containing the offending Philips private element via C-MOVE and confirm the instance is no longer dropped

## What

Backlog item: **Workflow 执行器 minor #1**.

The workflow-run cancel endpoint (`POST /projects/{project_id}/workflow-runs/{run_id}:cancel` in `app/api/routes/core.py`) unconditionally soft-cancelled the run job and propagated to children, returning `{"cancelled": true}` — **even when the run was already terminal** (success / failed / cancelled / timeout). Cancelling a finished run is a conflict, not a success.

## Fix

Before `request_cancel`, read the run status and raise the project-standard `ApiError(409, "workflow_run_terminal", ...)` for terminal runs. Non-terminal (pending / running) runs are completely unchanged — same soft-cancel + child propagation + audit.

Surgical: the existing `_workflow_run_row_for_project(...)` return value (previously discarded, called only for its 404 side effect) is now captured to read `status`. No other behavior touched.

- New `test_workflow_run_cancel_on_terminal_run_returns_409`: cancel on a `success` run → 409 `workflow_run_terminal`, no soft-cancel / no child propagation / no audit.

body:
## Summary

Implements the W6 mandatory purchasing/usage lifecycle gate: Playwright specs that drive the deployed **TaskFlow** and **AgentOps** example apps end to end against the live MonetizeKit API, plus a demo-data sweep backstop and an advisory CI workflow.

- `e2e/taskflow.lifecycle.spec.ts` — signup -> subscribe Free -> seat/analytics gating -> add-on compatibility gate (422 on Free) -> upgrade to Pro -> attach/detach Extra Seats Pack (+10 seats) -> switch to Scale -> downgrade to Pro -> cancel.
- `e2e/agent-ops.lifecycle.spec.ts` — provision fleet -> Researcher hits its 10-action deny budget -> Summarizer exhausts credits -> credit top-up -> per-model usage breakdown.
- `scripts/sweep-demo-customers.ts` — backstop that archives demo customers a killed/cancelled run leaves behind (guards the issue-135 leak mode); auto-runs after every gate run.
- `.github/workflows/e2e.yml` — advisory nightly + `workflow_dispatch`, targeting the delivery tier, with the sweep afterwards.
- Selectors are **testid-free** so the gate validates whatever is deployed (no chicken-and-egg with app markup); the example app source is unchanged.

## Validation (by execution)

- **TaskFlow: GREEN against the public production app** (`taskflow.monetizekit.app`) — full lifecycle incl. teardown, ~12s. Proves the harness, selectors, and cleanup end to end.
- **AgentOps: correctly detected a real production drift** — provisioning succeeds with zero network errors, but the credits badge renders `💳 credits` (no balance) on prod, so the balance assertion fails. This is exactly the kind of breakage the gate exists to catch; the spec itself is correct for a healthy tier. A fully-green AgentOps run should be confirmed on the delivery tier (freshest app+API).
- Root typechecks clean: `pnpm typecheck:e2e` and `pnpm -r typecheck`.

## Follow-ups / decisions

- **Enabling `workflow_dispatch` requires this workflow on the default branch** (`main`) — GitHub only dispatches workflows present on the default branch. Merging this PR enables the on-demand + nightly runs.
- **Investigate the prod AgentOps credits drift** (balance not rendering on `agentops.monetizekit.app`).
- A few demo customers were created on the prod examples workspace during validation; run `pnpm sweep:demo` (prod key + `SWEEP_MAX_AGE_MINUTES=0`) to clear them, or let the aging sweep handle them.
- Promote from advisory to a required promotion gate once stable across several delivery runs.

## Test plan

- [ ] Merge to `main`, then `gh workflow run e2e.yml` (dispatch) and confirm the delivery run is green (or triages the AgentOps drift).
- [ ] Confirm the post-run sweep job archives leftover demo customers.

## Feature #10531 — Marcado de trámites prioritarios

Implementa las dos HU del Feature #10531: **#10536 (BACKEND)** y **#10537 (FRONTEND)**.

### Qué hace
El gestor marca/desmarca un trámite como **prioritario** (estrella en el listado). Los prioritarios se ordenan **con primacía** en el listado de operación y en la bandeja de aprobación del OT, que muestra el distintivo (solo lectura). Se agrega un filtro "Prioritarios".

### Backend (#10536)
- Columna `tramites.procedure_instances.prioritario` (migración SQL idempotente + índice); mapeo EF.
- Endpoint `PATCH /api/v1/tramites/instances/{id}/priority` (handler idempotente; **no** altera el ciclo de vida, solo el flag de ordenamiento).
- Ordenamiento con primacía en `ListWithSummaryGraphAsync` y en la bandeja del OT (`OtClientProcedureRepository`).
- Expuesto en `InstanceSummaryDto` y en `OtClientProcedure` / `OtClientProcedureResponse`.

### Frontend (#10537)
- Estrella toggle (optimista, revierte si el backend falla) + filtro "Prioritarios" en `TramitesTable` / `TramitesListToolbar`.
- Distintivo de prioridad (solo lectura) en la bandeja del OT (`ClientProceduresTable`).
- Tipos + método de cliente `setPriority`.

author: crypt0xdev
body:
## Qué hace

Agrega el firmware de Arduino de referencia (`arduino/robot_car/robot_car.ino`) que empareja con el protocolo Bluetooth de la app. El foco es arreglar el modo **Evasión**, que a velocidad alta (180) chocaba con los obstáculos en vez de esquivarlos.

## Diagnóstico

- La app y el firmware **ya hablaban bien**: al tocar Evasión la app envía `'2'` y el firmware entra correctamente en `EVASION` y corre `pasoEvasion()` en cada `loop()`. **No era el APK.**
- El slider (`V180`) fijaba la misma `velocidad` que usa la evasión → a PWM 180 el HC-SR04 no alcanza a detectar + frenar a tiempo, sobre todo con obstáculos finos o de canto (cono de ~15°). Por eso esquivaba "a veces".

## Cambios

- **Tope de velocidad en evasión** (`VEL_EVASION_MAX = 140`): el modo autónomo se limita aunque el slider esté a 180. Manual sigue usando la velocidad completa.
- **Zona de precaución**: al acercarse a un obstáculo avanza a la mitad de velocidad, dando más pings por centímetro para no chocar objetos difíciles.
- **`esperar()` en vez de `delay()`** en la maniobra: sigue leyendo el Bluetooth, así el botón **Detener** de la app corta la maniobra al instante (antes se ignoraba ~2.5 s).
- **Telemetría de distancia** (`US=..cm`): se envía a la app para poder depurar el sensor desde la pantalla **Diagnóstico**.
- **Ojo intencional**: la evasión **no** usa el failsafe por timeout de Manual, porque la app envía `'2'` una sola vez; aplicarlo pararía el robot a los 600 ms.

## Archivos

- `arduino/robot_car/robot_car.ino` — firmware corregido.
- `arduino/README.md` — protocolo Bluetooth y notas de calibración.

## Cómo probar

1. Cargar el `.ino` en el Arduino con el HC-05.
2. Conectar la app, abrir **Diagnóstico**, tocar **Evasión (2)** → debe aparecer `OK:EVASION`.
3. Acercar la mano al sensor y ver `US=..cm` bajar. Si siempre marca `-1` → revisar cableado del sensor (TRIG=2, ECHO=4, 5V).
4. Si aún roza obstáculos, bajar `VEL_EVASION_MAX` a 120 o subir `DIST_BASE_CM` a 25.

## Summary

- Extract docker-compose.yml's inline `canary-doctor` bash command into a real, testable file (`bin/canary-doctor-entrypoint.sh`) instead of an untestable YAML string blob.
- Drop the `--api-key "$$CANARY_API_KEY"` flag passed to `cargo run -p canary-cli`; canary-cli already resolves `CANARY_API_KEY` from its own inherited process environment (`Config::resolve_with_mode`), so the flag only existed to put the raw key in the container's process argv, visible via `docker top`/`ps`/`/proc/<pid>/cmdline`.
- Declare `CANARY_API_KEY:` with no inline value in the `canary-doctor` service's `environment:` map so Compose passes it through from the invoking shell's own exported environment.
- Update `docs/self-host-docker.md` to teach `export CANARY_API_KEY=...` followed by `docker compose run --rm canary-doctor`, and stop teaching the `-e CANARY_API_KEY=<value>` copy/paste pattern that put the key on the host's own process list.

Closes canary-913 (P0).

## Evidence

- New regression test `test/bin/canary_doctor_entrypoint_test.sh` stubs `cargo` to capture its full argv (same pattern as `test/bin/entrypoint_test.sh`'s litestream stub); confirmed it fails against the pre-fix logic (catches the leak) and passes against the fix.
- Live Docker proof: built and started `canary` via `docker compose up --build -d canary`, ran `docker compose run --rm -d canary-doctor`, and sampled `docker top` while the container's `cargo run -q -p canary-cli -- --endpoint http://canary:4000 --json doctor` process was actively running/compiling — argv contains no `--api-key` flag and no key value. A subsequent foreground run confirmed the doctor still authenticates correctly via the inherited env var: `auth_configured: true`, `key_scope: admin`, `key: "CANARY_API_KEY: redacted"`.
- Canonical local gate: `./bin/validate --fast` (dagger call fast, incl. the new test via scriptsQualityContainer) OK; `./bin/validate --strict` (full gate) OK in 5m15s, no failure markers.

## Residual Risk

- No CI wiring exists for a live docker-compose smoke of this profile (matches existing self-host-docker.md convention: it's proven via manual live smoke, not the Dagger container-based gate, since that would need nested docker-in-docker). The stubbed argv-capture test is the durable CI regression guard against reintroducing the leak; the live proof above is this change's one-time manual verification.

author: coly010
body:
## What kind of change does this PR introduce?

Docs fix — Legacy port SIDE_EFFECTS.md accuracy.

## What is the current behavior?

Two systemic env-var documentation errors across `src/legacy/**/SIDE_EFFECTS.md`, found in the parity audit:

- **~36 files** document `SUPABASE_API_URL` as a real override for the Management API base URL. No such env var exists in Go: `SetEnvPrefix("SUPABASE")` + `AutomaticEnv()` never binds `API_URL`, there's no `os.Getenv("SUPABASE_API_URL")` anywhere, and the `Profile.api_url` field loads on a separate, unbound `viper.New()` instance (`internal/utils/profile.go:99`). The real override is `SUPABASE_PROFILE` (built-in name or a path to a YAML profile file).
- **~18 files** document bare `PROJECT_ID` as if it were itself a settable env var. It's Go's internal viper key name — the real, user-facing env var is `SUPABASE_PROJECT_ID` (`viper.GetString("PROJECT_ID")` under the global `SetEnvPrefix("SUPABASE")` singleton, `internal/utils/flags/project_ref.go:62`).

Both claims were independently verified against the real Go source and, for the viper-specific mechanics, a compiled test program against the exact pinned `github.com/spf13/viper v1.21.0`.

## What is the new behavior?

- Removed the fabricated `SUPABASE_API_URL` rows; where a file didn't already document `SUPABASE_PROFILE`, added a real row for it (including the persisted `~/.supabase/profile` fallback step in the resolution chain, matching `legacy-cli-config.layer.ts`).
- Corrected every bare `PROJECT_ID` mention (Environment Variables tables, Files Read "When" columns, and prose) to `SUPABASE_PROJECT_ID`, converging on the dominant convention already used correctly across ~15 sibling files.
- Left `db/advisors/SIDE_EFFECTS.md` untouched — it already correctly documents that `SUPABASE_API_URL` is not honored.
- Filed follow-ups for two related-but-out-of-scope findings surfaced during review: CLI-1904 (global choice-flag telemetry gap, unrelated) and CLI-1905 (bare `DB_PASSWORD` has the same bug class as this PR's F2, in a set of files this PR doesn't touch).

Docs-only change; no `.ts` files touched. `pnpm check:all` passes.

author: sarmiz1
body:
### ⚡ Bolt: Optimize AppContext and component rendering

#### 💡 What:
I have optimized the global state management and rendering pipeline of the application. The primary focus was on `AppContextProvider` and heavy consumer components like `MetricCards` and `CustomTableBody`.

Key changes:
- **`AppContextProvider.jsx`**: Memoized the context `value` object and all its data sub-objects (`cryptoListing`, `globalMetrics`, etc.) using `useMemo`. Wrapped `handleTabChange` in `useCallback`.
- **`MetricCards.jsx`**: Refactored into a memoized `MetricCardsContent` component. Context consumption is now handled by a wrapper that passes stable props, preventing re-renders when unrelated context state (like `tabValue`) changes.
- **`CustomTableBody.jsx`**: Similarly refactored into a memoized `CustomTableBodyContent`. Removed direct context consumption from the inner body to allow effective memoization.
- **Stable Data Mapping**: Added `useMemo` to the coin data mapping logic in `TopCoinTable` and `TrendingCoinTable` to ensure stable references are passed to the table.

#### 🎯 Why:
The application suffered from unnecessary re-render cascades. Since `tabValue` (the current tab index) was bundled in the same context object as heavy application data, switching tabs triggered a re-render of every component consuming the context, including the `MetricCards` (which contains complex charts) and the `CustomTableBody` (which renders many rows and sparklines).

#### 📊 Impact:
- **Re-renders Reduced**: During tab switching, re-renders of `MetricCards` and `CustomTableBody` were reduced from **2-4 per switch** to **0** (after the initial tab mount).
- **CPU Efficiency**: By preventing these redundant renders, we reduce the main thread workload, leading to smoother interactions and better battery life for mobile users.

#### 🔬 Measurement:
Verified using a custom Playwright profiling script that captures `console.log` instrumentation during interactions. Confirmed that while `AppContextProvider` still re-renders (expectedly) on `tabValue` change, the memoized "Content" components successfully skip rendering due to stable prop references.

#### 🛠️ Housekeeping:
- Removed all instrumentation logs.
- Fixed pre-existing ESLint unused variable errors in `SpotTable.jsx`.
- Fixed a `react-refresh` lint error in `AppContextProvider.jsx`.
- Ensured `npm run build` and `npm run lint` pass successfully.

author: tim-nish
body:
## Summary

Adds the content-registry foundation for Epic 1: zod schemas for all six content types (`profile`, `project`, `product`, `publication`, `article`, `newsletter-issue`), a `gray-matter`-based loader that parses every record under `content/`, validates it, resolves `related.*` references, and computes inverse relations once per build. The validator now runs ahead of `vite build` in `npm run build`, so malformed content fails the build with a file+field error instead of shipping.

Closes #12

## Acceptance Criteria Mapping

| AC | Implementation | Test |
|---|---|---|
| AC1 — schema per type, field-for-field incl. `unlisted`/`featured` additive fields | `src/content/schema/*.ts` | `load.test.ts` good-fixtures suite parses all 6 types |
| AC2 — build fails on missing field / unknown enum / duplicate slug / unresolved `related.*` | `src/content/load.ts` (`validateFrontmatter`, duplicate-slug check, related-resolution loop) | 4 dedicated bad-fixture tests in `load.test.ts` |
| AC3 — external-with-body / canonical-without-body fails the build | `validateArticleBodyRule` in `load.ts` | 2 dedicated bad-fixture tests |
| AC4 — validator runs as part of `npm run build` | `package.json` `build` script now runs `tsx scripts/validate-content.ts` first | Manual: `npm run build` |
| AC5 — typed in-memory registry with inverse relations computed once per build | `loadContentRegistry()` returns `{ records, bySlug, relatedBy }` | `load.test.ts` "computes inverse relations without requiring a reciprocal entry" |
| AC6 — fixture-driven coverage per failure mode | `content/__fixtures__/{good,bad}/` + `src/content/__tests__/load.test.ts` | `npm test` (9/9 passing) |

## Review Focus

- `src/content/schema/common.ts`'s `dateSchema`: gray-matter's YAML parser silently converts unquoted `YYYY-MM-DD` scalars into JS `Date` objects, so the schema accepts either and normalizes to a string — worth double-checking this doesn't mask a real type error elsewhere.
- `src/content/load.ts`'s inverse-relation computation (`relatedBy`) — confirm the direction is right: a record's `relatedBy` bucket is keyed by the *pointing* record's plural type, not its own.
- Duplicate-slug and unresolved-`related` detection are both keyed off the frontmatter `slug` field, not the filename — intentional, matches the AC's literal wording, but flagging since architecture.md describes slug as "the filename stem."
- Bad-fixture error messages are asserted by substring match in tests — brittle if wording changes, but keeps the test readable.

## Changed Areas

- `src/content/schema/` (new) — zod schemas per content type
- `src/content/load.ts` (new) — registry loader/validator
- `scripts/validate-content.ts` (new) — build-time CLI gate
- `content/__fixtures__/` (new) — good + bad fixtures, one per failure mode
- `package.json` — `build`/`test`/`validate:content` scripts, new deps (`zod`, `gray-matter`, `marked`, `tsx`, `vitest`)

## Test Plan

- [x] `npm test` — 9/9 vitest tests pass (good fixtures + one test per AC2/AC3 failure mode)
- [x] `npm run build` — type-checks, validates content (currently empty registry, passes), and builds `dist/` cleanly
- [x] `npm run validate:content` — standalone content-only check

## Summary

- Applies catalog-provided provider `baseUrl` and `defaultModel` to the app LLM vendor settings when a known provider is installed.

- Expected format: `<type>(<scope>): <summary>` (for example, `feat(marketplace): add user package install flow`).

## Scope

- Provider catalog parser no longer collapses known marketplace provider assets to bare `{ providerId }` when rich metadata is supplied.
- Provider marketplace install path still records known providers in `installedProviderIds`, but now also materializes catalog `baseUrl` and `defaultModel` into `llm.vendors[provider]`.
- Existing custom/user-authored unknown provider preset path is preserved.
- Default surface remains unchanged: five provider defaults, two default themes, English default locale.

## User Impact

- Installing a Marketplace provider with catalog metadata can configure the provider endpoint/model immediately instead of depending only on hardcoded app defaults.
- Keyless/local provider metadata from the Marketplace side can be carried through the catalog parser for runtime use.
- Users still see a small built-in provider list and discover long-tail providers via Marketplace.

author: qiankunli
body:
Step 1 of the bed-init plan (docs/design.md 〈进程树〉): extract process
start/kill behind a Spawner seam so the forker is swappable (in-process today;
the bed's own init on linux next).

- Spawner.Start(bedID, cmd) → Proc {Pid, Kill, Wait}; Spawner.KillBed sweeps
  every live process of a bed
- inProcSpawner: commands are daemon children with Setpgid, live pgids tracked
  per bed
- Manager.teardown now calls the spawner sweep — closes the hole where an
  in-flight foreground RunForeground (unregistered by design) survived bed
  eviction; registry killBed stays as fallback
- stdio refactored to explicit os.Pipe ends everywhere (RunForeground,
  StartCommand via startOneShot, session shells): raw fds must be extractable
  to hand to an out-of-process spawner (SCM_RIGHTS)
- CommandRegistry.start → track: registry no longer starts processes, only
  bookkeeps a started Proc + output stream
- test: TestTeardownKillsInflightForeground

Step 2 (docs/design.md 〈进程树〉 S1): 'hostel __bedinit --socket S --bed B',
re-exec'd once per bed following the __confine/__asuser idiom.

- PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER + single wait4 loop (os/exec deliberately unused —
  no reaping conflict); adopted setsid/double-fork orphans are collected and,
  at teardown, enumerated by a /proc ppid scan and killed
- one unix-socket connection per spawn: length-prefixed JSON spec + 3 stdio
  fds via SCM_RIGHTS; replies {pid} then {exit}; children get Setpgid +
  Pdeathsig=SIGKILL (no strays if bedinit itself dies)
- SIGTERM = kill loop (pgid+pid per round, rescan until empty) then exit
- client side (Spawn/Handle) for the daemon; linux-only server, stub elsewhere
- e2e test via the stdlib helper-process idiom: real separate init process,
  asserts parentage, exit codes, and that SIGTERM kills a setsid escapee

Step 3: initSpawner implements the Spawner seam over bedinit — one init per
bed, started lazily on first spawn (socket in a LOCAL temp dir: the workspace
may be network FS where unix sockets don't belong), self-healing via the
death-watch goroutine, KillBed = SIGTERM the init (its kill loop takes the
whole tree, setsid orphans included) with a SIGKILL fallback.

- config: --bed-init / HOSTEL_BED_INIT = auto (default) | off; auto probes at
  boot (spawn /bin/true through a probe init) and downgrades honestly to the
  in-process spawner where bedinit can't serve (non-linux dev), logged
- main: EnableBedInit(os.Executable()) after manager assembly
- linux e2e via the TestMain re-exec hook: foreground exec + set -e isolation,
  session shells under the init, and eviction killing an in-flight command
  plus its setsid escapee

The linux suite exposed a real gap: bedinit had no Pdeathsig, so a dying
daemon left bed inits (and their trees) as strays — observed as 'go test'
hanging 60s on the stderr fd the leaked inits inherited. SIGTERM-on-parent-
death makes the init run its kill loop and take the tree along. Tests also
evict their beds explicitly (orderly teardown, no reliance on death timing).

Step 4: a dead browser used to brick the amenity — state stayed 'running'
with every tenant holding contexts of a dead process, unrecoverable until the
daemon restarted. Supervision lives in the amenity itself (in-daemon, per
docs/design.md 〈进程树〉— a separate manager process buys no survivability
under pod semantics):

- watchMaster: chromedp cancels the master context when the browser dies;
  onMasterGone tells crashes from orderly stops (state check) and stale
  watchers (instance identity check)
- crash → drop all tenants + flip to idle: the NEXT AcquireTenant lazily
  rebuilds its slice — no restart storm, beds see a fresh browser
- exponential restart gate (1s → 64s cap, ladder resets after 5min stable);
  a gated ensureRunning returns an error instead of blocking c.mu
- unit tests drive the state machine directly (no real browser): crash path,
  orderly-stop non-crash, stale watcher, backoff escalate+reset

design.md 〈进程树〉: S1 status (auto probe + honest fallback, commands and
session shells under the init, two-way Pdeathsig), implementation anchors
(bed Spawner seam / bedinit package / in-amenity chromium supervision).
README: --bed-init flag + a short process-tree paragraph.

build/Dockerfile.internal (byted go base for corp-network builds) stays local
— the open-source repo keeps only the docker.io-based Dockerfile, whose ARG
GOPROXY already covers mirror needs.

author: bplatz
body:
Adds a Bolt protocol endpoint (Neo4j drivers → openCypher), moves Cypher to bare namespace-0 names by default.

## Bolt protocol server

- `fluree-db-bolt` protocol crate: PackStream codec + session state machine; listener in `fluree-db-server` (autocommit + explicit `BEGIN`/`COMMIT`/`ROLLBACK`), `Node`/`Relationship`/`Path` + temporal structures, write-`RETURN` entities as typed nodes.
- Session authentication with identity-derived policy enforcement.
- `bolt` feature on by default (listener binds only when `bolt_listen_addr` is set); first-class CLI flags on `server run/start/restart`; reference + guide docs.

## Bare namespace-0 names as the Cypher default

Cypher labels/types/property keys now live under namespace 0 (the empty prefix) instead of being forced under `http://example.org/`: zero-config durable names for LPG users, planner keeps full Sid-gating, and bare JSON-LD terms converge on the same names. RDF compat is the opt-in via `@context`/`@vocab` (ledger default or per-view). Placement rule is locked by test: no colon → whole name verbatim (never namespace-split); colon-containing backticked names are the RDF escape hatch.

## Performance campaign

Read/serve path, all query surfaces (SPARQL and JSON-LD ride the same substrate):

- **Shared leaf mmaps** through the leaflet cache — leaf files are immutable CAS artifacts; the per-query open+mmap+munmap cycle and whole-leaf `fs::read` copies were the dominant fixed cost of an indexed point lookup.
- **Cascaded within-leaflet seek**: bound point probes binary-search every bound sort-key prefix column (was: leading column only), making them leaflet-size-independent on all four index orders.
- **Galloping batched lookups** (SPOT/PSOT/OPST): sorted-merge the wanted-id list against leaflet batches instead of per-row membership tests; chunker gap-split reinstated at the measured break-even (4096 ids).
- **Bolt node-emit hydration**: batched sorted SPOT crawl engaged under live novelty with per-subject overlay dirty-split; shared `Arc<str>` strings through the encode path; adjacency no longer inlined into property maps.
- **Raw-id shortestPath lane**: bidirectional BFS in `s_id` space with batched frontier expansion (one galloping sweep per side per level); dictionary touched only at endpoints + final path. Per-node overlay dirty-split keeps novelty shortcuts/retracts/re-asserts and novelty-only endpoints exact (end-to-end test); views the lane can't serve (policy, unsummarizable overlay) keep the Sid search.
- Point-lookup floor: parsed-AST cache, reified-edge annotation probe gate, parallel wildcard JSON-LD prefetch.

## Fixes surfaced along the way

- Time-travel over fully retracted predicates regressed by the bound-object driver change: driver selection is rdf:type-first under replay (`to_t < index max_t`) so probes stay on the replay-correct SPOT sidecar lane. (The underlying rebuild-path hole — omitted empty partitions — predates this branch and remains open.)
- Narrow K≥2 hydration projections no longer lose their predicate filter to the wildcard flake cache.
- Specific-value lookups keep seek speed under predicate novelty; fast paths gate on live novelty rather than the monotonic overlay epoch; per-graph property stats carried through incremental indexing.

## Validation

- Full workspace suites green (api 2569 / query+indexer 1538 / server 414; the one recurring failure is the documented raft-liveness flake, passing in isolation).
- New coverage: NS-0 round-trip + RDF-compat (API view-level and server ledger-level), exotic backticked-name no-split rule, shortestPath novelty semantics (shortcut / base-edge retract / re-assert / novelty-only endpoint), cascade-seek unit tests.
- Probes for regression tracking: `bolt_node_emit_probe`, `cypher_point_floor_profile` (per-phase floor decomposition, `PROBE_ONLY`/`PROBE_USERS` filters).

author: speranzaemiliano-rk
body:
## Problema reportado

Un comprobante emitido como "Documento tipo factura" con "¿Afecta caja?" = Sí / Egreso **sí aparecía en Caja General**, pero **no aparecía en "Resumen Egresos"**.

## Diagnóstico

`renderEgresos()` (totales + tabla "por Proveedor") y `renderDetalleEgresos()` (detalle de pagos) — ambas dentro de la pestaña **Resumen Egresos** — solo sumaban pagos de **Presupuestos** y **Facturas**. Nunca incluyeron:
- Pagos de **Documentos** de proveedor (`documentos[].pagado` / `pagosHistorial`).
- Egresos de **Caja/Banco** en `ingGeneral` (movimientos manuales, y los que genera "Emitir Comprobante" con Afecta caja=Sí/Egreso).

## Cambio

- **`renderEgresos()`**: el total (ARS/USD) y la tabla "por Proveedor" ahora suman también Documentos y Caja/Banco. Nueva columna "Documentos / Caja / Banco"; los movimientos sin un proveedor prolijo (caja manual, comprobantes emitidos a un cliente) se agrupan bajo una fila "Movimientos de Caja / Banco".
- **`renderDetalleEgresos()`**: agrega filas de Documentos (con y sin historial) y de los egresos de `ingGeneral` al detalle de pagos.
- El botón de editar en el detalle se limita a los tipos que `abrirEditarPago` sabe manejar (presup/factura) — los demás ya se editan desde su pestaña de origen (Documentos, Caja General).

## Verificación

Simulé `renderEgresos()` con Presupuestos ($100k) + Facturas ($50k) + Documentos ($20k) + un egreso manual de caja ($15k) + el egreso de un "Emitir Comprobante" tipo factura ($22k). Antes el total mostraba solo $150k (ignorando $57k); ahora suma los $207k correctos. Los 5 bloques `<script>` parsean sin errores.

author: imohiyoko
body:
## 概要

CI/リリース周りのセキュリティレビュー（指摘③）の対応。cosign keyless 署名の**検証側 identity 正規表現を厳格化**し、正規のリリース経路（main / `v*` タグ）以外で署名された成果物を検証で弾くようにする。

## 背景 / 問題

`--certificate-identity-regexp` が `...release\.yml@refs/` で終わっており、**任意の ref**（例: `refs/heads/evil`）で署名された `checksums.txt` も検証に通ってしまっていた。

これは、write 権限者が別ブランチに `environment` ゲートを外した改ざん `release.yml` を置いて `workflow_dispatch` した場合の**偽リリースが「正規署名済み」に見える**穴になる（署名側の keyless identity は `release.yml@refs/heads/<任意>` になり得るため）。

## 変更

6箇所（`.goreleaser.yaml` のリリースページ表示 ×2 / `install.sh` ×2 / `install.ps1` ×2）の末尾を統一して絞り込み:

```
@refs/  →  @refs/(heads/main$|tags/v[0-9])
```

シェル差異に応じて `$` をエスケープ（YAML 単一引用=そのまま / bash=`\$` / PowerShell=`` `$ ``）。

## 裏取り・検証

- 実際の **v0.2.4** の `checksums.txt.pem` の SAN を確認 → `release.yml@refs/heads/main`（`workflow_dispatch` は main 上で署名される）。単純に `@refs/tags/v` へ絞ると既存リリースの検証が壊れるため、`heads/main` も許可する必要があることを確認済み。
- bash が実際に生成する正規表現文字列で判定をテスト:

| identity | 期待 | 結果 |
|---|---|---|
| `@refs/heads/main`（v0.2.4 実績） | 通す | ✅ |
| `@refs/tags/v0.2.4` / `v1.0.0-rc1` | 通す | ✅ |
| `@refs/heads/evil` | 弾く | ✅ |
| `@refs/heads/main-evil`（前方一致攻撃） | 弾く | ✅ |
| 別 repo（なりすまし） | 弾く | ✅ |

## 影響 / 互換性

- 署名側（`release.yml` / goreleaser の `signs`）は変更なし。検証側の許容範囲を狭めるだけ。
- 既存リリース（main 署名）・将来の直タグ push リリース（`v*` 署名）はどちらも検証成功のまま。
- ドキュメント記載のコマンド（release ページ / インストーラ）が対象。

セキュリティレビューの他指摘: ①（`require_last_push_approval`）と fork PR 承認厳格化はリポジトリ設定側で適用済み。②/ワークフローファイルロックは個人アカウントの制約で Organization 移行が前提のため本 PR には含めない。

author: enejb
body:
## Proposed changes

Introduces a **Feature Catalog** — a new `automattic/jetpack-features` package that lets code declare granular *features* (finer-grained than modules) and resolve each to a single availability **status**, without owning any gating itself. It is descriptive: it *reads* modules for on/off and `WPCOM_Features`/`Current_Plan` for entitlement, and adds the connective metadata (title, description, docs, connection level) that lives nowhere today.

This is **Slice 1** of a larger effort. Everything user-visible is behind the `jetpack_features_catalog_enabled` filter (default off).

What's included:

* `register_feature( $slug, $args )` — declare a feature (title, description, docs, string entitlement slug, connection level `none|site|user`, owning module, `available_since` per-platform map, `recommend` hints). Side-effect-free registration; never turns anything on.
* `Registry` (singleton) + `Feature` value object.
* `Feature_Environment` interface + `Status_Resolver` — composes signals into one status (`active` / `available_off` / `needs_connection` / `needs_upgrade` / `unsupported`) plus a machine-readable reason and raw facets. Precedence: `unsupported → needs_connection → needs_upgrade → available_off → active` (connection before upgrade).
* `Jetpack_Environment` — the self-hosted adapter, binding the interface to `Modules` / `Current_Plan` / `Connection\Manager` behind `class_exists` guards so the package stays loadable where those packages are absent. The cross-platform seam: a future `Wpcom_Environment` implements the same interface for Simple/Atomic, from the same manifest.
* Flag-gated WP-CLI `wp jetpack features list`.
* Four validation-probe features registered from the plugin (`forms-multistep`, `forms-file-uploads`, `protect-firewall`, `videopress`) exercising the free/paid × none/site/user matrix.

Entitlements are stored as **string slugs** (e.g. `field-file`), never as `\WPCOM_Features::` constants, so `features.php` stays loadable on self-hosted Jetpack where that class is absent.

## Related product discussion/links

* Design spec and implementation plan authored alongside this work (feature-catalog concept: Pillar > Product > Feature > Entitlement, made concrete as a registry).

## Does this pull request change what data or activity we track or use?

No. This adds a read-only descriptive layer over existing module/plan/connection state. It introduces no tracking and, by default (flag off), exposes no surfaces.

## Testing instructions

Unit tests:

* `pnpm jetpack test php packages/features` — 23 tests covering the Feature value object, Registry, the full Status_Resolver precedence matrix, and the Jetpack_Environment mapping (via test seams).

Live (behind the flag):

1. Build + deploy the `jetpack` plugin to a connected test site (`pnpm jetpack build --deps plugins/jetpack`, then rsync).
2. Enable the flag on the site, e.g. a mu-plugin: `add_filter( 'jetpack_features_catalog_enabled', '__return_true' );`
3. Run `wp jetpack features list`. Expect a table of the four probes with resolved statuses. On a connected free-plan site: `forms-multistep` → `active`, `forms-file-uploads` → `needs_upgrade`, `protect-firewall`/`videopress` → `available_off`.
4. Remove the user/owner token (`wp jetpack disconnect blog`) and re-run: `forms-file-uploads` (a `user`-level feature) flips to `needs_connection` while the `site`-level features are unaffected — demonstrating the per-feature connection level and the connection-before-upgrade precedence.

author: scolacur
body:
Follow-up to #171. That PR extracted the card markup into `TicketCard.svelte`; the question it raised was *"why did no tests need updating?"* — because the web suite tests only pure-TS logic helpers (`vite.config.ts` deliberately strips the SvelteKit plugin; there is no component-rendering infra). The refactor moved DOM + styles, no `.ts`, so nothing the suite runs changed.

That surfaced a real gap: the board's fiddliest logic — the drag-drop reorder math and the lock rule — lived **inline in `+page.svelte` with no coverage**, while the easier logic (`sort-logic`, `filter-logic`, `copy-utils`) had already been extracted and tested.

## Changes
- **`board-logic.ts`** (new) — `isStatusLocked`, `computeSortOrder`, and the `AGENT_CONTROLLED` constant. `computeSortOrder` is made **pure** by taking the column's ticket list as a parameter (caller passes `byStatus(status)`) instead of closing over component state.
- **`board-logic.spec.ts`** (new) — 11 tests:
  - lock matrix: robot × agent-controlled lane (`robot_queue`/`completed`) vs. steve/null and non-agent lanes

- **`+page.svelte`** — removes the three inline defs, imports from `board-logic`, call site passes `byStatus(status)`.

- **No behavior change** — pure extraction.

author: ajsornig
body:
## Why
The 1:10 AM CPU alert (2026-07-06 01:13) was the weekly-montage ffmpeg encode. Two compounding issues in `scripts/motion-timelapse-stitch.sh`:

1. `stitch_weekly` globbed **every** daily video on disk. The `find -mtime +7` prune lets files survive ~8 days, so the montage grew to 8 days (log history: 2→3→4→5→6→7→7→8 since Jun 27).
2. Every night it **re-encoded all 7-8 daily videos from scratch** just to stamp the date label, pegging all 4 cores at 92-96% for 2.5+ min — long enough to trip the 3-sample sustained infra alert (threshold: CPU > 80%).

## What
- Cap the montage to the newest `RETENTION_DAYS` (7) daily videos — true rolling week
- Cache labeled segments in `motion-timelapse/weekly-segments/` (gitignored work dir); only encode days not seen before, prune segments that fall out of the window. Nightly work drops from ~8 re-encodes to 1.
- `nice -n 19` + `-threads 2` on the segment encode keeps CPU ~50%, under the 80% alert threshold even on the one-time full cache rebuild
- Moved the daily-video prune ahead of the stitch skip-return so it runs even on skipped nights

## Test plan
- `bash -n` syntax check ✓
- `npm test` (18 tests) ✓
- On the Pi after merge: run `--weekly` manually → expect "Compiled 7 days (7 newly encoded)" with CPU staying under 80% in the monitor log; run again → expect "(0 newly encoded)" in seconds; verify weekly mp4 plays

body:
## IMP-179 — Horizonte 6 (artefactos periféricos)

Adds tier-1 **prevention** for invariant #1 (mutate governed artifacts only via the owning CLI command). Best practice (doc 38 R-H1/R-H2): *PreToolUse for policy, PostToolUse for verification* — PostToolUse can't undo, and the only prior guard (`ignite-verifier`, IMP-146) was post-hoc + opt-in + Agent-hook-only. Blast-radius: hooks/config/tests → single-mode.

### Cross-surface by design (Jose's directive)
Everything we build serves all considered surfaces. Shared decision logic lives once in **`sentinel/hooks_logic.py`** (`governed_artifact_deny_reason` + the governed regex/glob source of truth for `project-brief.md`, `03_specs/*.md`, `04_backlog/*.md`). Each surface enforces via its native mechanism:

| Surface | Mechanism |
|---|---|
| **Claude Code** | new PreToolUse **command** hook `.claude/hooks/deny-governed-artifact-write.py` (stdlib, <100ms, any CC version), wired **by default** in the versioned `.claude/settings.json` |
| **Codex** | `.codex/hooks/pre_tool_use_policy.py` returns `decision: block` for governed writes |
| **Kilo Code** | `kilo.jsonc` `permissions.file.deny` globs; the CLI still regenerates via `commands.allow` |

### Seed #6 — versioned
The deny is committed in `.claude/settings.json` as the framework default: the executable encoding of invariant #1. A BA who needs a deliberate bypass has the CLI. It blocks only *illegitimate* hand-edits (reconciling with the "hooks signal, never block legitimate mutation" descarte); legitimate mutation flows through the command channel, which the hook never sees. **Reads and unknown tools fail open.**

### Guards
`tests/test_governed_artifact_deny.py`: decision by path/tool, the Claude hook script (deny governed / allow other / fail open on bad stdin), the Codex block, and **cross-surface consistency** (same governed set in `hooks_logic`, `kilo.jsonc`, `.claude/settings.json`). Updated the two IMP-172 tests that encoded the old "hooks never block" invariant. `.claude/hooks/README.md` documents the tier stack.

Also tightened the IMP-177 forbidden-phrase guard `patch` → `(?<!\w)patch` (catches the verb in prose, not identifiers like `apply_patch`), across doctor + the three body/agent/hook guards.

### Verification (single-mode)
- Suite: **551 OK** (537 prior + 14 new), `UNITTEST_EXIT=0`.
- `/doctor`: **PASS**, 0 FAIL.
- Live hook smoke (deny fires end-to-end in Claude Code) travels to **IMP-178** — it requires a session opened at the repo root.

## Summary

Implements the **historia médica** (consultation record) feature — the legally required DR clinical record (Reglamento Técnico para la Gestión del Expediente Clínico, MISPAS 2023) generated from the protocol content of each consultation. Three phases:

**Phase 1 — Core record lifecycle**
- `ConsultationRecord` model: one historia per consultation, append-only versions, structured sections (draft → signed, immutable after signing per §8.14.g)
- `generateRecordSections` mapper in `@rezeta/shared`: derives the legal section skeleton (§6.3) from filled protocol blocks + signed orders, with first-visit vs nota-de-evolución distinction
- Endpoints: `GET/POST/PATCH /v1/consultations/:id/record`, `POST …/regenerate`, `POST …/sign`, `GET …/pdf` (PDFKit, streamed)
- Consultation sign auto-creates the draft (`recordOutcome` in the sign response, non-fatal)
- Patient detail «Historia» tab: consultation list + editable document pane (edit per section, regenerate, sign, download); post-sign panel card
- Plan de tratamiento is composed from actually-signed prescriptions/orders (legal dose/route/frequency minimum), never from raw protocol blocks

**Phase 2 — Per-protocol mapping overrides**
- Optional `historia_mapping` inside protocol content JSON (per block: destination section, include, label) — versions with `ProtocolVersion`, snapshots into usages automatically
- Protocol editor «Historia médica» tab with Auto/Personalizado mapping table; legally locked block types stay locked
- Kind-exclusion clamping so overrides can never silently drop clinical content

**Phase 3 — Expediente export**
- `GET /v1/patients/:id/record-export`: full patient expediente PDF (cover page + latest signed historia per consultation, newest-first) — the patient copy right (Ley 42-01 art. 28 / §7.1.7)
- «Exportar expediente» button in the Historia tab

## Compliance notes
- Dates/hours on legal documents render in `America/Santo_Domingo` regardless of server TZ (§6.1.9/§6.3.4)
- Historia/expediente PDF downloads are audit-logged (`communication`/`pdf_generated`)
- Signed records are immutable at the repository layer; corrections flow through amendments → new versions

- 2,666 tests green across the workspace (`pnpm test`), 95% per-file coverage gate passes (`pnpm test:coverage`), lint + typecheck clean

author: tya5
body:
**[per-PR-coder]** — Fixes an owner-reported asymmetry root-caused by lead-coder in `src/reyn/core/pipeline/executor.py`.

## The asymmetry

Inside a `for_each`/`fold`'s `do:` step, the evaluation context is `{"ctx": <outer named stores>, "pipe": <the compositional step's own incoming pipe>, "item": <the current loop item>}` (`fold` also adds `"acc"`) — `item`/`acc` are SIBLING top-level keys alongside `ctx`, NOT inside `ctx`.

- `_interpolate_prompt` (an `agent` step's prompt template resolver) evaluates `{item}`/`{ctx.x}` references via `evaluate_expr(ref, context)` against the FULL context dict — so `item` naturally resolved there.
- `call`'s and `match`'s `pass:` handling were DIFFERENT, hand-written lookups: both did `outer_stores = context["ctx"]` then looked up each `pass:` name in `outer_stores` ONLY — restricted to `ctx` alone. So `pass: [item]` inside a `for_each`'s `do: {call: ...}` raised `PipelineExecutionError: pass: names 'item', which is not in the caller's named stores`, even though the SAME `item` binding was directly usable in an `agent` step's `{item}` prompt one line away.

This was an implementation accident (call/match's `pass_` lookup never considered the sibling `item`/`pipe`/`acc` keys), not an intentional design boundary.

## The fix

A shared `_resolve_pass_names()` helper (used by both `call` and `match`'s runners) resolves each `pass:` name against `ctx` (the caller's named stores) **FIRST**; if absent, it falls back to the sibling step-local bindings (`item`/`acc`/`pipe`) present in the current scope's context.

**Precedence: `ctx` wins on collision.** If a named store literally called `item` exists in `ctx` AND the current scope also has a sibling `item` loop-variable, the `ctx` one wins — this preserves 100% backward compatibility for every existing pipeline using `pass:` today; the fallback only ADDS coverage for previously-unreachable names, never changes an existing resolution.

The not-found error message was reworded from `"pass: names {name!r}, which is not in the caller's named stores"` to `"...which is not a named store nor an in-scope loop binding (item/acc/pipe)"` to stay accurate to what is now searched.

Grammar (EBNF) is unchanged — `pass:` is still `"pass:" "[" NAME* "]"`; this is purely a resolution-scope fix, not a syntax change.

## Tests added (`tests/test_pipeline_pass_sibling_bindings.py`, all via real `parse_pipeline_dsl` + `PipelineExecutor` + `PipelineRegistry`, no mocks)

1. `test_for_each_do_call_pass_item_forwards_the_loop_variable` — a `for_each.do: {call: ..., pass: [item]}` genuinely forwards the loop item into the callee.
2. `test_fold_do_call_pass_item_forwards_the_loop_item` — same shape for `fold`'s `do:` with `pass: [item]`.
3. `test_fold_do_call_pass_acc_forwards_the_running_accumulator` — same shape for `fold`'s `do:` with `pass: [acc]`, proving both sibling bindings resolve independently.
4. `test_for_each_do_match_pass_item_forwards_the_loop_variable` — same shape for `match` (not just `call`).
5. `test_ctx_named_store_wins_over_sibling_loop_binding_on_name_collision` — backward-compat regression: a named store in `ctx` also called `item` wins over the sibling loop binding of the same name.
6. `test_pass_name_absent_from_ctx_and_siblings_still_raises` — a `pass:` name genuinely absent from both still raises `PipelineExecutionError` with a clear message.

## Docs updated

`docs/reference/runtime/pipeline-dsl.md` / `.ja.md`:
- The `pass:` invariant note (`Data flow between steps` § Scoping exceptions) now states the ctx-first / item-acc-fallback resolution order and precedence rule.
- The `call`/`match` field tables, and the `fold`/`for_each` sections' own prose, now mention `pass: [item]` / `pass: [acc]` forwarding the loop variable into a sub-pipeline.
- A new worked example under "Data flow between steps" shows a `for_each.do: {call: {pipeline: X, pass: [item]}}` snippet — the exact shape the owner was trying to write.
- The formal-grammar "Hard rules" § 3 bullet updated to match.

## Test plan

- [x] `ruff check src tests` — clean
- [x] `python scripts/test_tier_audit.py --strict tests/test_pipeline_pass_sibling_bindings.py` — 6/6 OK, 0 Tier-4 violations
- [x] `pytest` (repo root) — 7509 passed, 21 skipped (5 pre-existing failures in `test_fp0001_a2a_endpoints.py` / `web/test_a2a.py` / `web/test_mcp_sse.py` / `web/test_plugin_loader.py` / `web/test_resources_router.py` — verified unrelated: reproduce identically on `origin/main` with none of this PR's files present, and none reference pipeline code)

author: prajwolrg
body:
## Description

Stacked on #187, which defined the fork schedule/params types but left them unconsumed. This PR is the first consumer: it puts the worker through a real fork boundary, using unstake as the example feature. The fork keeps its `ForkId::Fork1` placeholder name — the bridge gates unstake txs on it, the admin `AsmStfVkUpdate` action carries the raw id of the fork the new proving artifact implements (rendered into the signing message, so the multisig authorizes the fork id alongside the predicate hash), the emitted `AsmStfUpdate` log forwards it, and the worker activates the named fork from the next block on, persisting the activation. The chain is the single authority on which fork an upgrade activates: there is no per-operator config to distribute, so a worker cannot silently diverge from the network by missing or misconfiguring one.

The fork id travels as a raw u16 rather than the `ForkId` enum because the upgrade that activates a fork is enacted by the artifact that predates it — the wire format cannot require knowing the fork. The worker maps ids it knows; an update naming an already-active fork is a logic-neutral VK rotation, and one naming an unknown id is skipped loudly (a binary that cannot apply the fork's rules cannot meaningfully activate it either).

The subtle part is crash/reorg safety, which is carried entirely by ordering: the activation record is written before the enacting block's anchor commit (a committed anchor can never lack its activation), and every sync rebase prunes activations above the base before re-processing (a reorged-out enactment cannot leak into the new branch — its blocks re-discover whatever survives). The activation height is derived, not stored: it is always the block after the enacting one, so `ForkActivation` records only `(enacting_height, fork)`.

Deliberately out of scope: the prover side (switching proving artifacts across VK upgrades) stays in #183. At the worker level nothing verifies proofs; the new predicate is carried opaquely.

Default behavior is unchanged: unstake remains active since genesis in production params, so a VK update naming `Fork1` there acts as a rotation.

### Type of Change

- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] New feature/Enhancement (non-breaking change which adds functionality or enhances an existing one)
- [x] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Refactor
- [x] New or updated tests
- [ ] Dependency update
- [ ] Security fix

## Notes to Reviewers

Suggested entry point: the fork id on the action in `crates/subprotocols/admin/txs/src/actions/updates/asm_stf_vk.rs` (and what it renders for signers), then the activation discovery and rollback in `crates/worker/src/state.rs`, then the bridge gate in `crates/subprotocols/bridge-v1/subprotocol/src/handler.rs` — note the gate decides identically in both tx-processing phases, so pre-fork the aux request is never made and aux request/consumption stay in lockstep.

Breaking surface: `AsmStfVkUpdate` and the `AsmStfUpdate` log gain a mandatory raw fork id, changing their SSZ layout and the rendered signing message (nothing deployed consumes the old layout).

Tested at two levels, no prover involved: unit tests for the gate boundary and the worker's discovery (activation of the named fork, already-active forks treated as logic-neutral rotations, unknown fork ids skipped, restart resume, rebase rollback), and a worker-level regtest integration test driving the full choreography — genuine musig2-signed unstake ignored pre-fork, admin VK upgrade enactment activates the fork at H+1, the same unstake then removes the operator — plus the reorg path where abandoning the submission block rolls the activation back until the new branch re-enacts it.

## Checklist

- [x] I have commented my code where necessary.
- [x] I have updated the documentation if needed.
- [x] My changes do not introduce new warnings.
- [x] I have added tests that prove my changes are effective or that my feature works.
- [x] New and existing tests pass with my changes.

## Summary
- improve agent-facing error guidance for high-noise Drive, Markdown, and Wiki shortcut failures
- classify Drive upload/delete and Wiki list failures into more precise terminal/retryable categories with actionable hints
- add target URL/token normalization and local validation for `markdown +create` and `wiki +node-list`
- update skill docs so agents stop retrying terminal errors and fix parameters/permissions instead

## Context
Failure telemetry showed several repeated agent error patterns:
- `drive +push`: missing parent folders and delete-remote already-deleted responses caused noisy hard failures
- `markdown +create`: agents mixed folder/wiki/document tokens, retried quota/not-found/server failures without enough guidance
- `wiki +node-list`: agents passed wiki URLs, node tokens, document tokens, or stale page tokens where numeric `space_id` / wiki `node_token` were required

This PR turns those cases into clearer CLI behavior:
- terminal parameter/resource/permission failures get explicit recovery hints
- retryable rate-limit/server failures remain retryable and recommend backoff
- obvious token/URL mismatches are rejected before calling OpenAPI

## Tests
- `go test ./shortcuts/drive ./internal/errclass`
- `go test ./shortcuts/drive ./internal/errclass ./internal/qualitygate/skillscan ./internal/skillcontent`
- `go test ./shortcuts/wiki ./shortcuts/markdown ./internal/errclass ./internal/qualitygate/skillscan ./internal/skillcontent`

## Notes
- A broader run of `go test ./internal/qualitygate/... ./internal/skillcontent/... ./shortcuts/drive ./internal/errclass` still fails in `internal/qualitygate/cmd/manifest-export` because the existing command index test cannot find `drive file.comments create_v2`; the affected packages above pass.
