author: yosawed
body: ## Summary Completes JoyportU support (bus wiring + full command-mode protocol) and fixes a menu shortcut conflict. All protocol work follows the `ppi_8255.h` reference implementation (XM6 C8255 class). **Hardware verification with a real JoyportU device is planned as a follow-up debugging session.** ### 1. JoyportU bus wiring via PIA delegation `ppi.c` was compiled and exposed to the Swift menu, but `$E9A000` accesses were routed only to `PIA_Read`/`PIA_Write`, so command-mode port I/O never reached the device (notify mode worked because its receive thread feeds `X68000_Joystick_Set()` directly). - **Writes**: `PIA_Write` mirrors joyport register writes to `PPI_Write` in command mode. PIA remains authoritative for internal side effects (ADPCM pan via `ADPCM_SetPan`, strobes). Notify mode is not mirrored — its send path blocks awaiting an ack and must not stall high-frequency ADPCM pan writes. - **Reads**: `PIA_Read` delegates input-port reads to the new `PPI_JoyportU_CmdRead()` in command mode, falling back to the emulated joystick path on failure/output-direction/notify mode. Port C stays on the internal latch (`pia.PortC`) under the default control word `$92` (it is an output port), so ADPCM pan read-modify-write is unaffected. ### 2. Command-mode read protocol (device → host) Implemented per the reference `ExecCmd`: - **No receive thread in command mode** — every response is read synchronously, exactly like the reference (which stops its thread once command mode is confirmed). This removes the thread-vs-sync-response conflict by construction. - **Init handshake**: probe firmware with the `'v'` version query; v2+ uses the `0x37` command-mode init, older firmware falls back to `0x31` ("command(old) mode"). The end-mark echo is validated before activation. Notify mode keeps its historical permissive handshake to protect the known-working path. - **Port queries**: `0x3A`/`0x3B`/`0x3C` round-trips with 8255 direction checks (output ports are served from the internal latch). - **Port A burst prefetch**: length-prefixed responses are buffered and drained by subsequent port A reads (analog stick data streaming). - **REQ line handling**: port C bit 4 set/reset (`0x08`/`0x09`) reads back a status byte on v2 firmware; `0xFF` invalidates the prefetch (the reference's "STAT LUSTER" workaround). ### 3. Protocol bug fixes in `ppi.c` - Port C data was double-shifted (`>>4` at both call site and `SendJoyportUData`), sending zero to the device. - Control register writes (`$E9A007`) were never forwarded; both control-word and bit set/reset forms are now sent, with duplicate suppression for bit set/reset as in the reference. - `recv_end_mark` was never cleared: stale acks made every wait after the first pass immediately. Now cleared before send and consumed on observation. - `Finalize()` now calls `PPI_Cleanup()` (receive thread join + serial close on quit); `StopJoyportU` only joins the thread when one was started. When no JoyportU device is connected (the common case), behavior is completely unchanged. ### 4. ⌘⇧M shortcut conflict **System → Use X68000 Mouse** and **Debug → Machine Monitor** were both bound to ⌘⇧M; the System item resolved first, so the monitor shortcut never fired. Machine Monitor now uses ⌥⌘M. ## Testing - `make -C tests/core` passes (6/6). - `pia.c` and `ppi.c` pass host-side `gcc -Wall -fsyntax-only` checks (with minimal IOKit stubs for `ppi.c` on Linux). - Xcode build not run in this environment (Linux container). - **Not yet verified on real hardware.** Command-mode init handshake (`'v'` probe, `0x37`/`0x31` responses), query round-trip latency, burst prefetch, and REQ status behavior all need validation with an actual JoyportU device. Timeouts deactivate the device gracefully (falling back to emulated pads) rather than hanging emulation.

author: rinz0x0cruz
body:
## Summary
Puts the **whole site under a passphrase** while keeping a public portfolio view. The existing AES-256-GCM apps gate is extended to cover the **entire un-redacted dashboard**, so entering the passphrase reveals everything the public build redacts — job descriptions, match rationale, referral contacts, and applications — decrypted **in the browser**. No server, no new dependencies.

## Two-tier model
- **Public (unauthenticated):** the redacted dashboard as before (no JDs/rationale/contacts, `applications: []`, funnel stripped). The portfolio view is unchanged.
- **Full unlock (passphrase):** a **header lock button** (and the Applications tab gate) decrypts the full payload and swaps it into `App` state wholesale — JDs render in the drawer, rationale/contacts appear, the Applications board + funnel populate. Re-lock restores the public view. The unlock is cached in `sessionStorage` for the tab.

## Lean public bundle (lazy-load)
The un-redacted payload is ~710 KB (incompressible once encrypted). Instead of baking it into the JS bundle, the heavy ciphertext ships as a **separate `site.enc.json`** fetched **only on unlock**; the bundle bakes just a tiny `{v,url}` pointer. Public first-load stays lean.

## What changed
- **Crypto:** new `web/src/lib/unlock.ts` (`unlockDashboard` — lazy-fetch + PBKDF2-SHA256/AES-GCM decrypt, `isEncPointer`, sessionStorage cache). Shared `UnlockForm` + header `UnlockControl` (lock/unlock/re-lock dialog). `ApplicationsGate` slimmed to reuse the form.
- **App wiring:** `App.tsx` holds `unlocked: DashboardData | null`; `data = unlocked ?? dashboard` drives rows/overview/applications. `Header` gains the lock control.
- **Build/publish:** `build-secure-apps.mjs` encrypts the full dashboard; `publish.ps1` + `publish.sh` write the heavy blob to `dist/site.enc.json` and bake only the pointer.
- **Types/docs:** `schema.ts` adds `EncPointer`/`EncRef`; FEATURES/ARCHITECTURE/SECURITY updated.

## Testing
- Web: `tsc -b` + `vite build` green; Vitest **47 passed** incl. new `unlock.test.ts` (inline round-trip, wrong-passphrase rejection, pointer detection).
- Verified in a local replica of a published build: redacted public tier (0 descriptions, `Applications0`) → enter passphrase → lazy-fetch 950 KB blob → decrypt → **`Applications38`**, re-lock button, and the **Job description** section renders in the drawer.

author: vikasprogrammer
body:
## What

Refreshing the console used to drop you back to a page's default view — most visibly, an open session terminal would vanish and you'd land on the sessions list. Top-level pages were already in the hash (`#/sessions`), but **deeper selection state was component-only**, so it didn't survive a reload or back/forward.

This makes the **open terminal live in the URL** and lays the foundation for the same on other pages.

## Changes

- **Hash router gains an optional detail segment** — `#/sessions/<tmux>`. `useHashRoute` now returns `{ route, detail, nav }` and `nav(route, detail?)` encodes the detail. The detail is everything after the first slash, URL-decoded.
- **`selected` is derived from the URL** (single source of truth) instead of a separate `useState`. Opening a terminal calls `nav('sessions', tmux)`; closing/deleting the open one navigates back to `#/sessions`. Refresh and back/forward now reopen the same terminal.
- **Bug fix:** `audit` was missing from the router's parse allow-list, so reloading `#/audit` silently fell back to Inbox. The router now validates against a shared `ROUTES` constant (kept next to the `Route` type).

## Notes

- Title in a deep-linked terminal is best-effort from the loaded sessions list, falling back to the tmux id for the brief window before sessions load.
- The detail-segment machinery is generic — other pages (agent editor, artifact focus) can adopt `#/<page>/<id>` next.

## Test

- `cd web && npm run build` — passes (strict `tsc -b` clean).
- Manual: open a session → address bar shows `#/sessions/aos-…` → refresh reopens the terminal; back returns to the list; reload on `#/audit` stays on Audit.

author: nkwiatkowski
body:
Backport of #17262 to `releases/v1.0.x`.

## Context

A customer's `queues` table (MySQL) grew so large the executor's scheduled cleaner could no longer purge it — it hit `Lock wait timeout exceeded` and shut the server down. Because the executor is the component that runs the purge, once it can't boot it can never clean up.

## Root cause

`JdbcCleaner` batches MySQL deletes (`.limit(10_000)`) but ran the entire batch loop inside a **single** `dslContextWrapper.transaction(...)`, holding row locks on every deleted row until one final commit — always tripping `innodb_lock_wait_timeout` on large tables.

## Changes

- **`JdbcQueueCleaner`** (new) — server-type-agnostic bean holding the purge logic; the MySQL branch now **commits per batch**, so the purge can grind through millions of rows without lock contention. `JdbcCleaner` becomes a thin `@Scheduled` delegate and inherits the fix.
- **`sys purge-queue`** CLI command — purges the `queues` table without booting any server component, so an instance whose executor can't start can still be recovered. Uses the configured `kestra.jdbc.cleaner` retention, with an optional `--retention` override.

## Tests

`AbstractJdbcCleanerTest` passes on H2, MySQL and Postgres; new `PurgeQueueCommandTest` verifies the command resolves `JdbcQueueCleaner` and runs in a no-server-type context.

author: gonidelis
body:
fixes #9588 with a new design.

Adds `cub::detail::BlockPrefetch`, a standalone block-scope facility for cooperatively emitting global-memory tile-prefetch hints.

Design-only PR: it lands the facility and nothing else, no algorithm is wired to it yet (net diff is a single new header).

#### What this adds

- `cub::detail::LoadPrefetch` - enum of prefetch targets: `none`, `l2` (`prefetch.global.L2`), l1 (`prefetch.global.L1`, falls back to L2 where real L1 prefetch is unavailable), and `bulk_l2` (TMA `cp.async.bulk.prefetch` into L2; requires SM90+, no-op on older arch).
- `cub::detail::BlockPrefetch<T, ThreadsPerBlock, Prefetch, PrefetchStride>`- a collective with a single static `Prefetch(it, items_to_prefetch)`. The block's threads cooperatively stride the tile, one hint per cache line (or one TMA bulk prefetch for `bulk_l2`). _A no-op for none and for iterators that can't yield a raw address_ (e.g. `CacheModifiedInputIterator`), so call sites need no enablement check.

_Everything is under detail, no public-API or stability commitment._

## Issue
- `xTdhLoop` is timing out near the 15-minute Lambda ceiling while recalculating xTDH and rebuilding xTDH stats.

## Fix
- Increase the `xTdhLoop` Lambda memory from 512 MB to 3072 MB to give the function materially more CPU and network headroom without changing xTDH behavior.

## Changes
- Updated `src/xTdhLoop/serverless.yaml` provider memory size only.
- No API, entity, migration, queue, or workflow changes.
- No architecture-doc update needed because this only changes Lambda sizing, not system shape.

- `npm run lint` passed.
- `npm run build` passed after installing both root and nested `src/api-serverless` dependencies in the fresh worktree.
- First `npm run build` attempt failed because nested API dependencies were not installed in the new worktree; no code changes were made for that failure.

## Risk
- Level: Low
- Why: Deployment-only Lambda sizing change; behavior and data shape are unchanged. Cost per invocation can increase, but timeout/retry churn should decrease.
- Rollback: Revert the memory size to 512 MB and redeploy `xTdhLoop`.

## Deployment
- Redeploy backend service: `xTdhLoop`.
- Order: `xTdhLoop` only.

## Review Notes
- Please focus on whether 3072 MB is the desired emergency headroom for the current production timeout loop.

author: cxbasdev
body:
## What Problem This Solves

`addIgnoreRules` in `src/shared/ignore-rules.ts` reads `.gitignore`, `.ignore`, and `.fdignore` files with `readFileSync(..., "utf-8")` and no size limit. A malicious or runaway ignore file in a scanned workspace can be loaded entirely into memory, causing the CLI or agent workspace scan to OOM before any rules are applied.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ignore files are line-oriented pattern lists; even large monorepos rarely exceed a few hundred KiB. A 4 MiB byte cap lets legitimate ignore files pass through while preventing an unbounded read from exhausting process memory. When a file exceeds the cap the scanner cannot know which exclusions the user asked for, so it fails closed: it conservatively excludes that directory's whole subtree from the scan. The exclusion is terminal for the directory — processing stops there so a later ignore file cannot negate it and reopen a subtree whose policy could not be parsed. Symlinked ignore files are still followed to their final regular target, preserving legacy workspace behavior.

## User Impact

- Workspace scans (`openclaw agent`, skill loading, etc.) no longer buffer arbitrarily large ignore files.
- An oversized `.gitignore` / `.ignore` / `.fdignore` now hides its subtree from discovery (fail closed) instead of dropping all of its exclusions (fail open). Workspaces with ignore files over 4 MiB will see that subtree disappear from scans until the file is trimmed below the cap.
- Normal-sized ignore files work exactly as before.

## Evidence

- Replaced `readFileSync` with a bounded `readRegularFileSync({ maxBytes: IGNORE_FILE_MAX_BYTES })` read in `src/shared/ignore-rules.ts`, after a direct size check that signals oversize.
- On oversize, the matcher adds `<prefix>**` and the per-directory ignore-file loop stops, so no later file can re-include the excluded subtree.
- `src/shared/ignore-rules.test.ts` covers normal files, under-cap large files, oversized files, cross-file negation (oversized `.gitignore` + later `!pattern` in `.ignore`, and oversized `.fdignore` + earlier negation), and symlink chains.
- Local test run on the final head:
  ```
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/shared/ignore-rules.test.ts --run
  # 6 tests passed
  ```

## Real behavior proof (standalone, final head 01d3b33e2)

Standalone script driving the real `addIgnoreRules` / `loadSkillsFromDir` scan path in temp workspaces (no test-runner mocks):

```text
=== Normal .gitignore ===
  ignores node_modules/foo: true
  ignores dist/bar.js: true
  ignores src/main.ts: false
=== Large-but-under-cap .gitignore (~2.6 MB) ===
  file size: 2,600,000 bytes
  ignores ignored-file: true
=== Oversized .gitignore (~13 MB): fail-closed subtree exclusion ===
  file size: 13,000,000 bytes
  ignores ignored-file: true
  ignores anything/else.txt: true
=== Oversized .gitignore + later negating .ignore: exclusion stays terminal ===
  ignores ignored-file despite later negation: true
  ignores secret.txt despite later negation: true
=== Oversized .fdignore + negating .ignore: exclusion stays terminal ===
  ignores ignored-file despite earlier negation: true
=== Skill discovery: oversized .gitignore + negating .ignore hides the skill ===
  skills discovered: 0
=== Symlinked .gitignore still honored ===
  ignores node_modules/foo: true
=== All standalone proof checks passed ===
```

- A 2.6 MiB ignore file is still loaded normally.
- A 13 MiB ignore file now excludes its whole subtree (fail closed), and later `!` negations in other ignore files of the same directory cannot reopen it.
- A skill directory hidden by an oversized policy is not discovered even when a later ignore file explicitly negates it.
- Symlinked `.gitignore` files are resolved to their final regular target and honored, preserving the previous workspace-scan behavior.

author: lalalune
body:
## Problem

On a genuinely-fresh install, the server-only boot (`startEliza`, `packages/app-core/src/runtime/eliza.ts`) bound the API and then **always booted a full default agent runtime** — PGlite open (~503ms), migrations, plugin-sql registration, default character build, services — even though the GUI shows onboarding first and **discards that entire runtime** when it restarts the agent after onboarding commits. That work sat on the critical path before onboarding's first paint. It is pure waste on fresh installs, and worst on mobile + cloud-only onboarding (#13377, #14390) where the local runtime is never needed at all.

The pre-existing code already skipped the interactive first-run CLI prompt in GUI/headless mode ("the GUI will restart the agent after first-run setup") but still booted the throwaway runtime anyway (`preOnboarding` marker).

## What changed

`startEliza` (serverOnly) now consults a **fresh-install gate** right before its post-bind runtime boot. When the gate fires, the process binds **only** the API server (the first-run/status/options, auth, and config routes onboarding needs) and **defers the runtime**. The runtime boots on the real onboarding-commit signal — reusing the **same `onRestart` path the GUI already used** to restart the agent after first-run — funneled through a single-flight registry so no trigger can double-open PGlite.

### State machine (server-only boot)

```
bind API server (runtime = null, state "starting")
        │
        ▼
gate = shouldDeferRuntimeBootUntilOnboarding()
        │
        ├─ false  (returning user  |  provider env key set  |  cloud-provisioned)
        │     └─ boot runtime now ──────────────► state "running"     [unchanged today]
        │
        └─ true   (genuinely-fresh install)
              state "not_started", startup.phase "awaiting-onboarding"
              (API serves onboarding; NO agent runtime; canRespond=false)
                    │
                    │  boot triggers (single-flight, whichever comes first):
                    ├─ POST /api/first-run  with a LOCAL deployment target
                    ├─ POST /api/agent/start      (funnels via onRestart)
                    └─ POST /api/agent/restart    (funnels via onRestart)
                    │
                    ▼
              boot runtime ──► "starting" ──► "running"
                    │
                    ├─ cloud/remote onboarding target → NO local runtime ever boots (#13377):
                    │     the client binds the cloud/remote agent; this process stays runtime-less.
                    └─ boot failure → state "error" (client three-state error state), registration
                          kept so an explicit start/restart retries.
```

### The gate predicate

`shouldDeferRuntimeBootUntilOnboarding()` (`packages/app-core/src/api/deferred-runtime-boot.ts`) defers **iff all** hold:

- **not** cloud-provisioned (`isCloudProvisioned()`),
- **no** provider auto-enable env key set (`PROVIDER_PLUGIN_MAP` keys — `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OLLAMA_BASE_URL`, `ELIZA_CHAT_VIA_CLI`, …), and
- `!hasCompatPersistedFirstRunState(loadElizaConfig())` — **the exact predicate `GET /api/first-run/status` answers `complete` with.**

So env-configured contexts (CI with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OLLAMA` dev loops, provisioned cloud containers) and any returning user keep booting the runtime **immediately, exactly as today** — the gate is scoped to the genuinely-fresh no-config state, not to headless mode. Server-only/CLI `eliza start` with a completed config, CI, and scenario-runner are all unaffected.

### Honest `/api/agent/start`

`POST /api/agent/start` with a **null runtime** used to fake-flip the reported state to `running` with nothing behind it. It now **boots on demand** through the injected `onRestart` (503 when no boot path exists; 500 + reported state `"error"` when the boot fails; idempotent while a boot is already in progress). A live-but-stopped runtime keeps the flag-flip.

### Fail-fast

No swallowed errors: a failed deferred boot flips the reported agent state to `"error"` and rethrows; the client observes it via `/api/status` (three-state rule). The first-run-commit trigger is fire-and-forget with a `runtime.reportError`-adjacent server log, and the failure surfaces to the client through the reported state — the finish flow polls `/api/status` and early chat turns hold on the runtime-ready gate.

## Files

- `packages/app-core/src/api/deferred-runtime-boot.ts` (new) — gate + single-flight boot registry
- `packages/app-core/src/runtime/eliza.ts` — serverOnly branch: gate, register deferred boot, `awaiting-onboarding` state, onRestart funnels the first boot
- `packages/app-core/src/api/first-run-routes.ts` — local-target commit fires the deferred boot; cloud/remote targets do not
- `packages/agent/src/api/agent-lifecycle-routes.ts` — `/api/agent/start` boots on demand from a null runtime
- `packages/agent/src/api/server.ts` — passes `onRestart`/`onRuntimeSwapped` into the lifecycle route

## Verification (real, end-to-end — scratch STATE_DIR fresh-install simulation)

Booted `packages/app-core/src/entry.ts start` against fresh temp state dirs with **no provider env keys**, real HTTP probes, real model turn.

### 1) Fresh install → no runtime boots, onboarding-required status, fast API bind

```
[boot-profile] startEliza:serverOnly entry                                    +1138ms
[boot-profile] startEliza:before startApiServer (config/registry setup done)  +1140ms
[boot-profile] startEliza:API bound (webview can connect, ready:false)        +3836ms
[eliza] Fresh install — agent runtime boot deferred until onboarding commits (onboarding API routes are live)
[boot-profile] startEliza:runtime boot deferred (awaiting onboarding)         +3837ms
```

Runtime-boot work (PGlite + migrations + plugins) **entirely skipped** — `grep -c PLUGIN:SQL server.log` → `0`. Status probes:

```
GET /api/first-run/status → {"complete":false,"cloudProvisioned":false}
GET /api/status           → {"state":"not_started","canRespond":false,
                             "startup":{"phase":"awaiting-onboarding",...}}   ← designed awaiting state, not error, not fake-ready
GET /api/health           → {"ready":true,"runtime":"not_initialized","agentState":"not_started"}
GET /api/auth/status      → {"required":false,"localAccess":true,...}
```

The client startup coordinator (`startup-phase-poll.ts`) sees auth `required:false` + first-run `complete:false` → dispatches `BACKEND_REACHED { firstRunComplete:false }` → onboarding shows. Phases advance identically.

### 2) Onboarding commit → runtime boots + real chat turn

Deferred fresh server (`state=not_started`, 0 runtime), then:

```
POST /api/first-run  {name, deploymentTarget:{runtime:"local"}, serviceRouting:{llmText:{backend:"cli",...}}}  → {"ok":true}
[eliza] Booting the deferred agent runtime (first-run onboarding committed)

/api/status:  not_started → starting → running   (canRespond:false → true)
[eliza] Auto-enabled plugin: @elizaos/plugin-cli-inference
[eliza] Runtime initialised in headless mode

POST /v1/chat/completions {"model":"cli","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply with exactly the single word BOOTPROOF and nothing else."}]}
MODEL_REPLY: 'BOOTPROOF'          ← real model turn on the just-booted runtime
```

(Provider for the live turn: `ELIZA_CHAT_VIA_CLI=claude` persisted to config by the onboarding step — the keyless claude-CLI provider lane — so the booted runtime has a working `TEXT_GENERATION` handler. The cloud-key lane booted identically and wired the cloud-proxy provider; its live call returned the structured "cloud key not authorized" degrade because the saved dev key is expired — pipeline proven, external credential dead.)

### 3) Returning user → boots immediately, laps unchanged

State dir with a completed config (`meta.firstRunComplete`, deploymentTarget, serviceRouting):

```
grep -c "Fresh install" server.log → 0     ← gate did NOT defer
[boot-profile] startE

author: bongkokwei
body:
## Summary
This PR fixes phase error calculations to properly wrap errors to the (-π, π] range and ensures consistent phase reference frames throughout the calibration loop, particularly in probe mode correction.

## Key Changes

- **Phase error wrapping**: Updated `calculate_mzi_errors()` and `calculate_phase_shifter_errors()` to wrap phase errors using `np.angle(np.exp(1j * delta_phase))`, preventing spurious ~2π errors when target/measured phases straddle the ±π boundary.

- **Removed phi_init from error calculations**: Eliminated the unused `phi_init` (initial phase offset) parameter from phase error calculations. Phase errors are now consistently computed as `target - measured` without offset adjustments.

- **Fixed probe mode phase reference**: Updated `apply_probe_correction()` to use the same phase reference frame as the error that triggered probe mode, ensuring the probe correction targets the correct zero point. Changed the probe error calculation to match the standard `target - measured` convention.

- **Improved power wrapping margins**: Made wrap margins symmetric (±25% of P_2π) in `wrap_and_clip_power()` to prevent converged powers near boundaries from triggering spurious full-cycle jumps.

- **Probe mode cleanup**: Added logic to clear accumulated probe targets when exiting probe-mode range, preventing stale offsets from carrying forward on re-entry.

- **Phase reference consistency**: Modified `run_calibration_iteration()` to pass the stored reference measured phases (`all_errors["ps_measured_phases_ref"]`) to voltage adjustment, ensuring all downstream calculations use the same phase reference frame.

## Implementation Details

The phase wrapping uses the complex exponential method to map phase differences to (-π, π], which is more robust than simple modulo operations when dealing with phase discontinuities. This ensures that small phase errors near the ±π boundary are reported correctly rather than as large ~2π errors.

The removal of `phi_init` from error calculations simplifies the code and eliminates a potential source of inconsistency, as the initial phase offset should be handled at the measurement level, not in error computation.

author: lior-nis
body:
Closes #437.

Credits broker-paid dividend/cash activities to each strategy's virtual NAV so live/paper NAV matches the total-return \`adj_close\` the backtest reinvests on — otherwise NAV understates the sizing denominator and the drawdown breaker trips on a phantom dividend drawdown.

Attribution is signed and per-side: each \`DIV\` row is attributed to the entitled side from each strategy's OWN signed position (long credit split by long shares, short debit by short shares — no shared divisor, so offsetting books don't cancel). Kind-parameterized across the LIVE and PAPER ledgers.

## GATE-2 findings resolved
1. **Same-day entitlement boundary** — the bound is deliberately date-level (broker \`DIV\` rows carry a date-only field). The consequence (a same-day fill stamped strictly after the \`DIV\` instant is entitled) is disclosed in the docstring and design-doc limitation #3, and pinned by \`test_same_day_fill_after_dividend_is_entitled\`.
2. **NULL/malformed DIV.ts** — fails closed to an unattributed account-level residual via \`AND ts IS NOT NULL\` + the \`_entitlement_as_of\` guard, which validates the **whole** \`ts\` (date-only OR full ISO datetime), not a 10-char prefix slice — so \`2026-06-06 garbage\` (valid prefix, malformed suffix) also fails closed rather than being accepted on its prefix.
3. **Test coverage** — same-day ordering, NULL ts, wholly-malformed ts, valid-prefix/malformed-suffix, and an explicit PAPER-lane credit test via \`build_paper_sizing_snapshot\`.

## Verification
- Codex GATE-2: PASS (prefix-validation blocker resolved, no new correctness bug).
- Full suite: 2952 passed. The single failure (\`test_cli_monitoring_decay::test_same_session_post_cert_tick_excluded_from_window\`) is a pre-existing date-dependent flake that fails identically on clean \`origin/main\` — unrelated to this diff.

author: ladianchad
body:
## 요약
Global planning 계보 점검(고전~2025) + 병렬 에이전트 구현 검증에서 나온 결함 3건(Major) + dead code 1건을 정정합니다. 계보 커버리지(BFS→…→FCIT* 2025) 자체는 촘촘하며, 아래는 정확성/미러링/정직성 결함 수정입니다.

## 변경 (원자적 커밋)
1. **fix: unify fast_rrt shortcut across C++/Python** — C++는 정점 1개씩 우회 반복형, Python은 greedy farthest-reachable single-pass로 서로 다른 shortcut을 써서 부분 차폐 경로에서 C++/Python 벤치마크가 갈렸음. C++를 Python과 동일 로직으로 통일.
2. **perf: limit AIT*/EIT* candidate_evaluated trace emission** — 기본 데모 config에서 trace가 ~13M 라인으로 폭발해 `replay.py` GIF 렌더 불가였음. `candidate_evaluated`를 feasible·improving edge로 제한(BIT* emit-on-accept와 정합) → 수십만 라인으로 축소. **탐색 로직·path_cost 불변.**
3. **fix: rename mislabeled anya to visibility_astar** — `anya`는 interval 기반 진짜 Anya(Harabor 2016)가 아니라 cell-centre visibility-graph A*였음. 회전점을 셀 중심으로 제한해 참 Euclidean 최적이 아닌데 "optimal any-angle (Anya)"로 오표기·오귀속. 알고리즘/클래스/config/demo/test/docs/README를 `visibility_astar`로 rename하고 거짓 최적성 주장을 삭제, visibility-graph 기원(Lozano-Pérez & Wesley 1979)으로 재귀속. `cost ≤ Theta*`는 셀-중심 그래프 위에서 성립하므로 유지. 진짜 interval Anya는 후속 추가 여지로 남김.
4. **chore: remove write-only dead code in SST** — 읽히지 않는 `pruned` 리스트 제거(C++엔 원래 없음).

## 검증
- **C++ 88/88, Python 132/132 통과** (전체 변경 합친 트리).
- visibility_astar: C++/Python 모두 `cost 27.7478 / expanded 95 / path_len 4` 일치.
- AIT* trace: 13.2M → 483K 라인, `path_cost 12.0473` 불변, `replay.py` GIF 렌더 정상.
- fast_rrt shortcut: 두 언어 동일 입력→동일 출력 코드레벨 확인.
- `docs/build.py` 재생성, `git grep -i anya` 잔존 0건.

## 미포함 (후속 권장)
- near-radius 고정상수(RRT*/Informed/Fast), rrt_connect 접합부 gap은 문서화된 변형이라 별도 판단.
- 계보 보강: anytime/bounded-suboptimal 축(ARA*/AD*), ABIT*(BIT*↔AIT* 고리), LQR-RRT*.

author: lawrenceeldridge
body:
### What is the purpose of this PR?

**Investigation result:** the anti-pattern catalogue was capturing almost nothing (≈0 project anti-patterns) despite many admitted mistakes over the project's life. The pipeline is healthy — the work queue is empty (no backlog/dead-letter), the `claude` distiller is available, and `extract_antipatterns` is implemented on the LLM distillers. The sole barrier is the **admission-marker gate** (`has_admission_markers`), the cheap pre-filter that decides whether to spend an LLM call on extraction.

It fired only on canonical phrases — `my mistake`, `i was wrong`, `you broke`, `let me fix that`. But the assistant's *own* corrective phrasing does not use those: `I misread`, `corrupted the`, `self-inflicted`, `I forgot to`, `I broke`, `you're right`, `let me revert`, `scratch that`. So real, catalogue-worthy mistakes (e.g. a `perl` edit that corrupted the whitepaper's LaTeX earlier this session) skipped the extractor entirely and never reached the catalogue.

**Fix:** widen `_ADMISSION_MARKERS` from 20 to 62, grouped by category (explicit self-admission, own omission, "the fault was mine", realisation/reversal, and conceding a user correction). The gate deliberately favours recall: the LLM extractor is the true filter and returns nothing on a clean session, so a false trigger costs one cheap call and never pollutes the catalogue.

### How was this tested?

`ruff` clean; full suite passes; the `AdmissionGateTests` regression cases now include the exact phrasings that previously slipped the gate ("My perl edit corrupted the LaTeX; let me revert", "I misread the build output", "You're right, that was my error", "I forgot to update the manifest; scratch that").

### Token / latency impact

None on the hot path — the gate runs in the detached capture worker. Slightly higher recall may trigger a few more Haiku extraction calls on sessions that mention corrections; each is cheap and off the interactive path, and the extractor discards non-durable admissions.

body:
## Homework 2: Intelligent Customer Support System

### ✅ What was implemented

A REST API for customer support ticket management built with **Python + FastAPI**, covering all required tasks:

**Task 1 — Multi-Format Ticket Import API**
| Method | Endpoint | Description |
|--------|----------|-------------|
| `POST` | `/tickets` | Create a new support ticket (optional `auto_classify` flag) |
| `POST` | `/tickets/import` | Bulk import from CSV / JSON / XML with per-row summary |
| `GET` | `/tickets` | List tickets with filtering by category, priority, status, customer_id |
| `GET` | `/tickets/{id}` | Fetch a single ticket by UUID |
| `PUT` | `/tickets/{id}` | Update a ticket |
| `DELETE` | `/tickets/{id}` | Delete a ticket |
| `GET` | `/health` | Health check |

All tickets are stored in an in-memory thread-safe store. Pydantic v2 enforces email format, enum values, and string-length constraints. Bulk import returns a structured summary: total, successful, failed, and per-row error details.

**Task 2 — Auto-Classification**
| Method | Endpoint | Description |
|--------|----------|-------------|
| `POST` | `/tickets/{id}/auto-classify` | Run or re-run the keyword classifier |

Keyword-based engine determines category (6 values) and priority (4 levels) with a confidence score (0–1), list of matched keywords, and reasoning text. Classification runs automatically on ticket creation when `?auto_classify=true` is passed. Manual override is always available via `PUT /tickets/{id}`.

**Task 3 — AI-Generated Test Suite**

58 tests across 8 files, all passing, **92.83% code coverage** (target: >85%):

```
tests/test_ticket_api.py       — 11 tests (CRUD + classify)
tests/test_ticket_model.py     —  9 tests (Pydantic validation)
tests/test_import_csv.py       —  6 tests (CSV parsing)
tests/test_import_json.py      —  6 tests (JSON parsing)
tests/test_import_xml.py       —  6 tests (XML parsing)
tests/test_categorization.py   — 10 tests (classifier logic)
tests/test_integration.py      —  5 tests (end-to-end workflows)
tests/test_performance.py      —  5 tests (throughput benchmarks)
────────────────────────────────────────
Total                          — 58 passed, 0 failed
```

**Task 4 — Multi-Level Documentation**

Four documentation files generated for different audiences using different AI models:

| File | Audience |
|------|----------|
| `README.md` | Developers — setup, architecture diagram, test commands |
| `docs/API_REFERENCE.md` | API consumers — all endpoints with cURL examples |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | Technical leads — component diagrams, data flow, design decisions |
| `docs/TESTING_GUIDE.md` | QA engineers — test pyramid, manual checklist, performance benchmarks |

All four documents include Mermaid diagrams (7 total across files).

**Task 5 — Integration & Performance Tests**

Integration tests cover:
- Complete ticket lifecycle (create → update → classify → delete)
- Bulk import with auto-classification verification
- 20+ concurrent simultaneous `POST /tickets` requests — all 201, no corruption
- Combined filtering by category and priority

Performance benchmarks all pass within SLA:
- 100 sequential `POST /tickets` < 1 s
- `GET /tickets` with 1 000 records < 500 ms
- Import 50-row CSV < 2 s
- Classify 1 000 tickets directly < 1 s
- 20 concurrent `POST /tickets` — all succeed

**Bonus — React Frontend**

A React + Vite + TailwindCSS frontend was built on top of the API (not required by TASKS.md):
- Dashboard with ticket statistics by category and priority
- Ticket list with filtering and sorting
- Create / Edit ticket forms with auto-classify toggle
- Bulk import page supporting CSV, JSON, XML drag-and-drop
- Toast notifications and slide-over panels

---

### 🛠️ AI tools used

**Tool:** Cursor IDE with:
- Claude Sonnet (agent mode)
- Codex 5.3(agent mode)
- GPT-5 Mini (agent mode)

**Workflow:**
1. Used the **Context-Model-Prompt** framework throughout: provided full TASKS.md + project structure as context before every major prompt
2. Prompted AI to scaffold the FastAPI project structure, Pydantic models, and routers; reviewed each generated file before accepting
3. Asked AI to implement the keyword classifier with confidence scoring — iterated on priority rules to match TASKS.md exactly
4. Used AI (different models per doc type) to generate all four documentation files with Mermaid diagrams
5. Used AI to generate the full test suite — provided the source code as context and asked for tests per file, checking coverage after each batch
6. Prompted AI to build the React frontend using the API reference as context; used a smaller/faster model for UI scaffolding

**What I verified manually:**
- Ran `./run_tests.sh` to confirm all 58 tests pass and coverage ≥ 85%
- Tested each endpoint manually via Swagger UI (`/docs`) and cURL
- Ran `./run_server.sh` with seed data to verify the full demo flow
- Reviewed every generated file for correctness before accepting
- Verified Mermaid diagrams render correctly in GitHub Markdown preview

---

### ⚠️ Challenges and how I addressed them

**1. Fixture files were too small**
Initial AI-generated fixture files had only 2–3 tickets each instead of the required 50 (CSV), 20 (JSON), 30 (XML). Fixed by prompting the AI with explicit count requirements and all valid enum values as context.

**2. `POST /tickets/import` vs `POST /tickets/{id}/auto-classify` routing conflict**
FastAPI matched `/import` as a `{id}` path parameter. Fixed by registering the import router *before* the tickets router in `main.py`, so `/tickets/import` is resolved first.

**3. `on_event` deprecation warning in FastAPI**
The startup event handler used the deprecated `@app.on_event("startup")` decorator. Identified via test warnings; left as a known non-breaking warning (fixing requires migrating to `lifespan` context manager).

**4. XML parser edge cases**
`lxml` raises different exceptions for malformed XML depending on whether the root element is missing vs. the file is empty. Added specific exception handling for both cases to ensure meaningful 400 error messages.

**5. Thread safety for concurrent tests**
The performance test sends 20 simultaneous POST requests. The in-memory store initially had a race condition on the UUID index. Fixed by wrapping writes in a `threading.Lock` inside `TicketStore`.

---

### 🚀 How to run

```bash
cd homework-2

# Create virtualenv and install dependencies
python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r src/requirements.txt

# Start API server with seed data (15 demo tickets)
./run_server.sh
# API: http://127.0.0.1:8000  |  Swagger: http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs
```

Run the full test suite with coverage report:
```bash
./run_tests.sh
# HTML report: src/htmlcov/index.html
# XML report:  coverage.xml
```

author: saibarathr
body:
Plan item 7 (audit #6), first batch: clears the 12 `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` errors outside the three add pages, plus the abandoned `AddIndexerModal` deletion held over from the last batch. Lint: 34 → 22 errors, still 0 warnings — the remaining 22 are all in `movies/add`, `music/add`, `series/add` (one shared form-sync pattern, next batch).

## The four patterns and their fixes

- **Browser-environment detection** (`use-push-notifications`, `use-install-prompt`): new shared `useIsStandalone()` hook built on `useSyncExternalStore` over the display-mode media query (now also reacts to display-mode changes). `isSupported`/`permission` become external-store reads, `previouslyEnabled` gets a lazy localStorage initializer, and `loading` is derived so unsupported browsers resolve immediately. The install hook tracks `appinstalled` as event-driven state since installing doesn't flip the current tab's display mode.
- **Seed-once-from-query** (settings: downloads, dashboard-refresh, discover-layout, instances): ref+effect replaced with a guarded one-shot during render — React's documented "adjusting state when props change" pattern. Same don't-clobber-edits-on-refetch semantics, one less render pass. The instances page's Jellyfin user-list fetch moves to its own effect keyed on primitive values so background refetches with unchanged data don't re-fire it.
- **Re-seed-on-data-change** (movies/music edit pages): prev-comparison render adjust, preserving the existing re-seed-when-cache-changes behavior exactly.
- **Mixed sync + side effect** (scheduled-alert dialog, watchlist-add dialog, activity tab resume, pending-approval deep-link walker): the sync state resets move to guarded render adjusts; the effects retain only what belongs there (preview/tag fetches, `loadMore` paging).

One justified `eslint-disable` with reason: the push hook's mount effect calls its async reconcile callback, whose setStates all occur after `await` points — the rule's static analysis can't see the async boundary.

## Verification

- `npm run lint`: 22 errors (all three add pages), **0 warnings**
- `npm run build` passes; `tsc --noEmit` clean in `src/`
- Behavior parity was the guiding constraint per pattern; the touched flows worth a manual pass: push subscribe/unsubscribe toggle, PWA install banner, the four settings edit forms, scheduled-alert + watchlist dialogs, activity tab resume, and the requests `?focus=` deep link.

author: 0xchasercat
body:
Fixes the stake.com `discover` failure diagnosed by v0.13.9's `--runtime-log`:

```
[loadscript] on-demand load budget exhausted (4130ms ≥ 4000ms); not fetched: .../chunks/BBKH46HI.js
```

`BBKH46HI.js` is a **static** dependency of the SvelteKit entry — part of the eager module graph hydration cannot proceed without — yet it went unfetched, then the on-demand fallback's budget expired before it could recover it, stalling the page at 0 endpoints.

## Root cause

`prefetch_scripts_with_budget` enqueued static imports and lazy targets (dynamic `import("…")`, webpack/Next chunk-loader refs) into **one FIFO frontier**. On a large code-split SPA (stake: 9.3 MB prefetched, budget-capped at 37 scripts) the file/byte/wall budget got spent on lazy route chunks while a critical dep of the entry was still queued behind them. That critical chunk then fell to the on-demand `LoadScript` path, whose own 4s budget expired mid-hydration.

## Fix

Two-tier frontier: `critical` (seeds + the static `import`/`export … from` closure discovered under them) is drained **fully** before `lazy` (dynamic imports + chunk candidates) is touched, with a shared `visited` set. The eager graph hydration requires is now fetched up-front and in parallel (8 concurrent); on-demand loading returns to being the rare fallback it was designed as. Helps every heavy SPA, not just stake.

Import extraction is split so priority is knowable from the one Oxc parse: `extract_imports` returns static vs dynamic specifiers (`ModuleImports`); `extract_module_imports` is retained as the order-preserving combined view for inline-`<script>` seeding, where every specifier is a page entry point.

**No API or wire-protocol change. Budgets and caps unchanged — this spends them on the right chunks.**

## Tests + gates

- New `prefetch_prioritizes_critical_static_over_lazy`: a per-URL recording fetcher over a seed → static (`a.js` → `a2.js`) + lazy (`import(d1.js)`, `chunks/c1.js`) graph asserts every critical node is fetched before any lazy node, and the whole critical closure is prefetched.
- New `extract_imports_splits_static_from_dynamic` covers the static/dynamic split (computed `import(expr)` still skipped).
- `cargo fmt --check` clean; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` clean; **full workspace `cargo test` — 364 pass / 0 fail** (was 362 + 2 new).

## Validation note

Proven by the ordering unit test + reasoning; the sandbox is region-blocked (403) from stake.com, so real-world confirmation is a `draco discover https://stake.com --runtime-log` on macOS — the critical chunk should now be prefetched up-front rather than starved. If a *lazy* route chunk is what a given site needs late, that's still the on-demand path's job (and now its budget isn't pre-spent on the critical graph).

author: adithya-s-edstem
body:
## Summary

Adds Section **80TTB** — the senior-citizen interest deduction — to the old regime. Previously only 80TTA (₹10,000, savings-bank interest only) was modelled, so resident senior citizens were under-deducted: they are instead entitled to ₹50,000 against **all** interest income (savings + fixed deposits).

80TTA and 80TTB are mutually exclusive. A **resident** taxpayer aged ≥ 60 now claims 80TTB (cap ₹50,000, against savings + FD interest); everyone else (including NRI seniors, since the higher deduction is resident-only) keeps 80TTA (cap ₹10,000, savings only). Each claim is still limited to the interest actually earned.

## Related issue

Closes #5

## Type of change

- [x] New feature (income/deduction field)
- [x] Tax-logic change

## What changed (by layer)

- **model** (`return.ts`) — added `s80TTB` to `Deductions` and `emptyReturn`.
- **config** (`types.ts`, `ay2025-26.ts`, `ay2026-27.ts`) — new `InterestDeductionConfig` (`s80TTA` cap, `s80TTB` = { cap, minAge }) on the old regime; no rates/caps/ages hardcoded in the engine.
- **engine** (`deductions.ts`) — `totalChapterVIA` now takes the interest-deduction config plus age and residency, and picks 80TTA vs 80TTB. `computeReturn.ts` computes `isResident`/`age` before Chapter VI-A and passes them in.
- **ui** (`InterestScreen`, `IncomeTypesScreen`, `DeductionsScreen`) — declares the 80TTA/80TTB maxima when interest is entered (engine picks and caps); resets clear both fields. FD interest now feeds 80TTB.
- **itr** — no change: the ITR-1 mapper consumes the aggregate `chapterVIA` total.

## Tax-correctness checklist

- [x] Engine reads all caps/ages from `src/config/` — nothing hardcoded there.
- [x] Computations cross-checked against the official IT Dept calculator.
- [x] Tests added with hand-verified values (`deductions.test.ts`, `computeReturn.test.ts`).
- [x] Whole-INR amounts; ISO dates.
- [x] Engine layer stays pure.

## Hand-verified figures (AY 2025-26, old regime)

- Senior (age 65), ₹50,000 savings + ₹10,50,000 FD interest, 80TTB claimed: deduction **₹50,000** (capped) → taxable ₹10,50,000 → slab tax ₹1,25,000 (10k + 1,00,000 + 15,000) → **₹1,30,000** with 4% cess.
- Same interest but age 59 (non-senior): only 80TTA **₹10,000** → taxable ₹10,90,000 → slab tax ₹1,39,500 → **₹1,45,080** with cess. Confirms the two paths diverge.
- Senior with FD-only interest ₹40,000: 80TTB **₹40,000** (below cap) where 80TTA would give ₹0.
- NRI senior: falls back to 80TTA (resident-only benefit).

## Verification

\`\`\`
npm run typecheck   # clean
npm test            # 9 files, 66 tests passed (12 new)
npm run build       # built in ~1s
\`\`\`

author: vikramsanthalia
body:
This pull request fixes critical reliability bugs and change-detection rendering skips in the Angular Renderer (`ComponentHostComponent`):

1. **Fix subscription memory leak:** Resolves a pattern where the component-host subscribes to `onSurfaceCreated` and attempts to unsubscribe self-referentially within the synchronous emission path, which evaluates to `undefined` and leaks listeners.
2. **Asynchronous surface resolution:** In progressive rendering or streaming environments, component host nodes can be mounted in the DOM before the surface itself is registered. Added a subscription to `onSurfaceCreated` to automatically bootstrap the component when the surface registers.
3. **Optimize reactivity (Signals upgrade):** Upgraded `componentType` and `props` to Angular Signals. In strict `OnPush` applications, asynchronous updates inside RxJS callbacks were not recognized by the change detector, leaving components unrendered.

author: pmquang87
body:
Stacked on #67 (base = `feat/oropt-reuse-iter0`); retarget to `master` once #67 merges. Bundles the two GUI follow-ups from #67 with the new concurrency feature.

## 1. Configurable concurrent solvers — `run.solver_concurrency` (default 1)

Each iteration's per-load-case solves are **independent** (each in its own `solve/case_<i>/` dir, its own OpenRadioss subprocess), so they can run in parallel. `loop._solve_cases` dispatches them to a thread pool (subprocess-bound work) capped at `min(solver_concurrency, n_cases)`, and reconstructs the exact **sequential contract** (`loop._sequential_contract`: `case_results` = successful prefix, `run_results` ends at the first failure) so **all downstream failure/divergence handling is unchanged**.

- `solver_concurrency == 1` keeps the byte-identical sequential path (per-case live activity in the Monitor).
- A single-case run is unaffected.
- On a strong PC this ~halves (or better) per-iteration wall time for multi-load-case runs. Each solver still uses `nt` threads (+ MPI `np`), so the user keeps `concurrency × nt ≤ cores` and watches RAM — hence opt-in with default 1.

## 2. GUI (Input tab)

- **"Concurrent solvers"** number input — capped at the number of load cases, disabled with an explanation for single-case runs.
- **"⏩ Seed iteration 0"** expander:
  - the **reuse_iter0** toggle (from #67), and
  - a **"copy iter_0000 from another run"** tool (`loop.copy_iter0`) — copies an old run's `iter_0000` into this run folder. The loop then validates + reuses it; the starter byte-compare (#67) means a copy from a different model is **refused at solve time**, so offering the copy is safe.

## Tests

- `_sequential_contract` truncation; `_solve_cases` concurrent **runs-all-in-order** and **failure-truncation** (faked `_solve_case`, no solver);
- `copy_iter0` copy / refuse-missing / overwrite / same-folder;
- `solver_concurrency` config roundtrip;
- GUI `AppTest`s: concurrency input (enabled multi-case, disabled single-case), reuse toggle default-on, and the copy button seeding the run folder.

**Full suite (587) green, `ruff` clean.**

## Notes

- Concurrency parallelises **load cases within an iteration** — iterations remain sequential (each depends on the previous design), which is inherent to topology optimisation.
- The log tee is called from worker threads; lines may interleave but won't corrupt (occasional per-solve messages only).

author: randallmlough
body:
## Plan

Implements plan 029 (deferred-hardening item 6): a signed-in user relaunching the app offline could not reach their Household even though all Lists/Items sit in the local PowerSync SQLite DB — without a Clerk resource cache, an offline cold start loads with `isSignedIn = false`, so the session machine never activated.

**Design gate resolved as Option B**: persist the last `BootstrapResponse` (pure directory identity — no tokens or secrets) as the single session artifact under the existing AsyncStorage key, and restore a ready session from it when Clerk loads signed-out. No Clerk config changes. The plan predates the repo restructure, so hook sites were adapted: the `markSessionHint` effect now carries the payload, and restore runs through new `sessionRestoreRequested` / `restoreSession` / `sessionRestoreSucceeded` machine transitions with the reducer kept pure (all async in the provider).

## What changed

- `session-hint.ts` stores one validated JSON payload; hint = payload presence (`bootstrapResponseSchema.parse` on read, `null` on corruption) — exactly one persisted artifact, no dual bookkeeping
- `session-machine.ts` models restore ownership (`pendingRestoreAttempt`), restored-ready state, `signInRequired`, and retained `restorableSession` for retry
- `provider.tsx` reads the payload when Clerk is ready-but-signed-out, connects PowerSync locally (non-blocking), publishes the restored session, and emits `authenticated_app_session_loaded` with `source: "cached"`
- `auth-gate.tsx` / `redirect-policy.ts` honor the payload after Clerk loads signed-out so restored sessions aren't bounced to auth, while `signInRequired` / `restoreFailed` states keep `/sign-in` reachable

## Dual adversarial review (Claude + Codex)

Both reviewers ran independently against `main...HEAD`; 8 merged findings, **all confirmed** by a validation pass, all fixed:

- **Mid-run Clerk auth loss** (major, Claude): a revoked user span forever on loading and relaunch restored them from disk → now marks sign-in-required, clears the payload, redirects to sign-in
- **Silent restore failure** (major, Claude): connect failure left a permanent spinner with `/sign-in` unreachable → now a retryable error state; retry re-issues the restore
- **User-switch data leak** (major, Claude): User B's activation connected over User A's local SQLite; A's queued uploads could push under B's token → wipe before connect **only when the fresh user id differs** (same-user reconnect preserves queued offline writes — orchestrator amendment to the proposed unconditional wipe, which would have reintroduced the data loss plan 030 prevents)
- **Connection ownership around restore** (major, both reviewers): stale activations could wipe data under an in-flight restore, and a restored view suppressed cleanup of stale wrong-user connectors → restore owns its attempt; non-destructive `db.disconnect()` for stale connectors under a restored session
- **Sign-out could leave a restorable identity** (high, Codex): payload clear was best-effort → now a critical step ordered before Clerk `signOut()`; a failed clear aborts sign-out (fail closed)
- **Reload/retry stranded restored sessions** (medium, both) → no-op while restored + signed-out
- Dead `markAuthenticatedAppSessionPresent` export removed; failure/race test coverage added (minor, Claude)

Security: clean from both reviewers — only directory identity is persisted, re-validated on every read.

## Verification

- `make verify` green at each commit: typecheck, Biome, ESLint (one pre-existing warning in `use-powersync-query.ts`), Jest **64 suites / 478 tests passed**
- Plan done criteria all checked: single artifact, `source: "cached"` on restore, sign-out clears payload (regression-tested), no out-of-scope files

## Worth watching

- Multi-device staleness (plan 029 maintenance note): a cached identity can outlive membership changes made while offline; PowerSync's server-authoritative purge covers data, but a `cache_invalidated` refresh decision is deferred to the plans 030/031 multi-device story
- The fully pre-existing variant of the user-switch gap (cold signed-out → signed-in as a different user, no restored session in between) predates this branch and was left untouched per surgical-change policy

body:
## 概述

在管理后台支持**同时管理/举办多场赛事**：创建、切换、编辑、删除多场赛事，并按所选赛事查看项目/评委/作品/统计。公众站点、评委端、选手仪表盘**保持单活跃赛事语义**，不受影响。

数据模型已按赛事隔离（`Event → Project → Submission → Score`），本次改动**无需数据库迁移**。

## 核心设计：两个独立的"当前赛事"

| 概念 | 含义 | 存储 | 数量 |
|------|------|------|------|
| **活跃赛事** | 公众/评委/选手端展示的赛事 | `Event.isActive` | 恒为 1 |
| **当前管理赛事** | 后台各页面展示的赛事 | `admin_event_id` cookie | 管理员本地选择 |

两者相互独立：管理员可管理一场未上线或已结束的赛事，而不影响公众看到的活跃赛事。

## 改动内容

**后端**
- `lib/event.ts`：新增纯函数 `resolveAdminEvent`（cookie → 活跃 → 最近 → null 回落）、`listEvents`、`getAdminEvent`；`getActiveEvent` 保持不变
- `lib/schemas.ts`：新增 `eventCreateSchema`，扩展 `eventUpdateSchema`（`isActive`/`track`/`startAt`/`endAt`）
- API：`POST /api/admin/event`（创建）、`PATCH`（单活跃不变式，原子事务）、`DELETE`（block-if-has-projects，不级联）
- `setAdminEvent` server action（写 cookie + revalidate）

**前端**
- 后台顶部赛事切换器；`/admin/events` 列表页（新建弹窗、设为活跃、删除）；新增"赛事管理"导航项
- 5 个后台页面改用 `getAdminEvent`；公众/评委/API 端保持 `getActiveEvent`

## 验证

- 单元测试 32/32 通过（含新增 `resolveAdminEvent` 回落逻辑与 `eventCreateSchema` 边界）
- 浏览器端全流程 E2E 实测：创建 / 切换（后台重新按赛事过滤）/ 设为活跃（单活跃不变式生效）/ 有项目时删除被拦截 / 空赛事删除成功 / 公众站仍展示活跃赛事
- 逐任务代码评审 + opus 全分支终审（结论：可合并），并已应用终审的 3 处轻量修复

body:
This pull request introduces version 2.2.0 of `node-tls-client`, syncing the wrapper with the native shared library v1.15.1 and adding extensive new features, options, and fixes. The update brings parity with the latest native capabilities, deprecates and replaces some configuration fields, and improves HTTP/3 support. It also ensures the native binary cache refreshes on upgrade, preventing stale binaries. Documentation, examples, and type definitions are updated to reflect these changes.

**Major feature and compatibility updates:**

* The default client profile is now `chrome_146` (was `chrome_131`), aligning with the native library. To keep the old fingerprint, explicitly set `clientIdentifier: ClientIdentifier.chrome_131`.
* The singular `certCompressionAlgo` field is deprecated in favor of the new array field `certCompressionAlgos`. The old key is still accepted for backward compatibility but will be removed in a future major version. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-eed2c4eba4e1306f5b9734d21bb72776163d064c728bc5ef6d7a7e1d27a10bf1L58-R82) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-5a831ea67cf5cf8703b0de46901ab25bd191f56b320053be9332d9a3b0d01d15L120-R120) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-5a831ea67cf5cf8703b0de46901ab25bd191f56b320053be9332d9a3b0d01d15L204-R204)
* The native shared library cache now uses a versioned marker file, ensuring the correct binary is used after upgrades.

**New features and options:**

* Added new client profiles (e.g., `chrome_130_psk`, `chrome_146_psk`, `brave_146_psk`, `safari_ios_18_5`, `firefox_148`, etc.).
* Introduced new top-level `SessionOptions`, including `disableHttp3`, `withProtocolRacing`, `withoutCookieJar`, `withCustomCookieJar`, `certificatePinningHosts`, `defaultHeaders`, and `timeoutSeconds`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-eed2c4eba4e1306f5b9734d21bb72776163d064c728bc5ef6d7a7e1d27a10bf1R47-R55) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-eed2c4eba4e1306f5b9734d21bb72776163d064c728bc5ef6d7a7e1d27a10bf1L58-R82) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-5a831ea67cf5cf8703b0de46901ab25bd191f56b320053be9332d9a3b0d01d15R216-R233)
* Added new custom-client (ja3string path) options: `h3Settings`, `h3SettingsOrder`, `h3PseudoHeaderOrder`, `h3PriorityParam`, `h3SendGreaseFrames`, `echCandidatePayloads`, `echCandidateCipherSuites`, `recordSizeLimit`, `streamId`, `allowHttp`, and `supportedDelegatedCredentialsAlgorithms`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-eed2c4eba4e1306f5b9734d21bb72776163d064c728bc5ef6d7a7e1d27a10bf1L58-R82) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-5a831ea67cf5cf8703b0de46901ab25bd191f56b320053be9332d9a3b0d01d15R216-R233)
* Expanded enum values: `KeyShareCurves` adds `X25519Kyber768Old` and `X25519MLKEM768`; `SupportedSignatureAlgorithms` adds `SHA224_RSA` and `SHA224_ECDSA`.
* Added a new HTTP/3 usage example in `examples/http3.js`.

**Deprecations and fixes:**

* Removed the dead `withDefaultCookieJar` payload field; cookie behavior is unchanged. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-eed2c4eba4e1306f5b9734d21bb72776163d064c728bc5ef6d7a7e1d27a10bf1R47-R55) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-06572a96a58dc510037d5efa622f9bec8519bc1beab13c9f251e97e657a9d4edR1-R37)

author: maxpayne89
body:
## Summary

Splits the 2347-LOC `KlassHeroWeb.Provider.DashboardLive` god-module (Louvain cohesion 0.058, recurring-friction surface across #890/#832/#872/#871) into four focused, route-level sub-LiveViews plus three shared helper modules. Closes #904.

**Four sub-LiveViews** (each owns one former `live_action`, its events, uploads, and render section):
- `OverviewLive` → `/provider/dashboard` (KPIs, top programs, pending requests/enrollments; the only tab that subscribes to PubSub)
- `TeamLive` → `/provider/dashboard/team` (staff stream, self-staffing, headshot upload)
- `ProgramsLive` → `/provider/dashboard/programs` (program CRUD, roster, invites, CSV import — the heaviest tab)
- `EditProfileLive` → `/provider/dashboard/edit` (profile + logo/verification-doc uploads)

**Three shared helper modules** (the only cross-tab surface, extracted from the god-module's private functions):
- `Dashboard.Params` — pure form parsers/coercions (unit-tested, incl. `stream_data` round-trip properties)
- `Dashboard.Uploads` — generic single-file upload plumbing
- `Dashboard.Chrome` — shared header state (`business`, `profile_draft?`, `dual_role?`)

Plus a `pv_dashboard_shell` component wrapping `pv_dashboard_chrome` + the profile-completion banner + dual-role cross-nav, so the three tab shells don't duplicate that boilerplate.

## Design decision

Chosen via a design gate: shared surface lives in **small pure helper modules** each sub-LV calls in `mount`, deliberately **not** a router-level `on_mount` hook (would fire across every provider route) and **not** duplicated per-LV. SessionsLive left out of scope.

## Review focus

- **Behaviour preservation.** This is a move-refactor: handler/helper bodies are byte-for-byte identical to the original modulo module boundaries. Two intentional changes, both forced by going route-level:
  - Tab nav `provider_nav_tabs`: `patch` → `navigate` (tabs are now distinct LiveView modules).
  - "New Program" header CTA: `push_patch` → open-in-place on Programs, `push_navigate(?new=1)` from the other tabs (opened in `ProgramsLive.mount/3`).
- **`active_nav` regression (caught in review, fixed).** The god-module set `active_nav` for the layout's `pv_sidebar`; the split initially dropped it, breaking the sidebar highlight + `aria-current` on all four routes. Restored in each mount, with regression tests.
- **Free bug fix.** Filtered-programs no longer corrupt the Overview "active programs" KPI (each tab computes its own count now).

## Test plan

- `mix precommit` green: compile `--warnings-as-errors`, format, `lint_typography`, full suite (3955 passed, 0 failures).
- New: `Dashboard.Params` unit + property tests; `active_nav` regression tests across all four routes.
- Existing dashboard tests relocated/renamed to match the split; the 4 cross-tab nav tests converted from `assert_patch` → `assert_redirect` (+ fresh re-mount where state carry-over was asserted).
- Reviewed by `regression-analyzer` (behaviour) and `code-reviewer` (standards): no surviving findings after the `active_nav` fix.

author: anarkiwi
body:
## T1.1 — Down-look launch enumeration + terminal test

New file `solver/launch.py`. Fixes a real correctness bug: the endgame shot is the player looking **DOWN** at the platform, legal where the reverse up-shot is blocked (ROM looking-up waiver `$1D2E`). This does **not** reuse the symmetric platform-vantage sweep `climb_search._launch_tiles` uses (which under-counts far launch tiles and over-counts near ones that cannot actually be down-shot).

### API (per plan §T1.1)
- `launch_tiles(state, plat, plat_ground) -> set` — every tile whose phantom-placed robot has down-look LOS to the platform. Phantom placement inlined from `sentinel.threat._place_phantom`.
- `down_look_los(g, plat) -> bool` — LOS from the player's current tile/eye down to `plat`, ceiling the observer on a fractional eye.
- `endgame_ready(g, plat, plat_ground) -> bool` — `g.eye > plat_ground and down_look_los(...)`.

### Gate (`solver/test_launch.py`, 5 tests, all green)
On ls0 (`plat=(12,4)`, real `plat_ground=8`):
1. `launch_tiles` **contains** the verified launch tile `(14,4)`.
2. `launch_tiles` **excludes** the tallest-terrain (z8) far dead-end corner `(28,18)`.
3. `down_look_los`/`endgame_ready` **True** for a player standing on `(14,4)` at a launch eye (8.875).
4. The symmetric platform-vantage reverse up-shot to `(14,4)` is **blocked** (`False`) — proving the down-look asymmetry recovers the tile.
5. Regression: the pinned human-win launch tile `(2,10)@9.375` is **not** a launch tile.

### Deviation from the plan's pinned facts (verified, not silently weakened)
The plan pins launch tile `(2,10)@9.375 → (12,4)`, `plat_ground=9`, "launch from afar" (cheb-10). In the bit-exact simulator:
- **`(2,10)@9.375` has NO down-look LOS to `(12,4)`** — verified across eye 8..11 and `max_steps` 200..20000. The ray toward the platform is blocked by the terrain ridge (the furthest tile toward the platform it reaches is `(9,3)`).
- The real `plat_ground` is **8** (`g.plat_ground`), not 9. The platform sits at the **maximum ls0 terrain height** (object z-height 8), so **no bare-terrain tile can down-look it** — a launch requires built height, and every reachable down-look launch tile is cheb 1–2 from the platform (no cheb-10 launch exists here).

The down-look **asymmetry itself is real and rich**: 7 of the 12 enumerated launch tiles — `(11,4),(12,5),(13,2),(13,4),(13,5),(14,3),(14,4)` — are missed by the symmetric platform-vantage sweep. The tests assert this verified behavior while preserving the down-look-asymmetry intent.

### Checks
- `black`: clean
- `pylint`: 10.00/10
- `pytest -n auto solver/test_launch.py`: 5 passed in ~9s

author: kim-em
body:
This PR records the measured negative result for issue #8642 next to the dormant `FpPoly.modByMonicPacked` kernel, correcting the docstring so a future agent does not re-attempt wiring it. The issue hypothesised that `FpPoly` is reduction-bound and that a packed `modByMonic` on `Array UInt64` backing words is the speedup lever; benchmarking the compiled binary disproves that premise, reproducing the `mulPacked` cautionary tale the issue itself cites.

A/B on `powModMonic` (Frobenius-shaped, F_65537, degrees 256..512, checksums identical): the reference `modByMonic` runs ~1310 ms; a `@[csimp]` swap for the pure-Lean `modByMonicPacked` runs ~1350 ms (~3% slower, since packing adds two copy passes and saves no boxing); a native C long-division extern that removes all boxing, per-term FFI and Lean `foldl` overhead runs ~1305 ms (flat), and moves the reduction only ~1% in isolation. `Array UInt64` boxes every element (`lean_box_uint64`, visible in the existing `lean_hex_fp_convolve` extern) exactly like `Array (ZMod64 p)` boxes its trivially-wrapped `UInt64` coefficients, so packing eliminates no boxing; `modByMonic` is bound by its intrinsic O(n^2) modular `% p` divisions, which the reference and any per-term packed kernel perform identically. The kernel stays dormant, proven and tested; it is intentionally not registered as the compiled implementation of `FpPoly.modByMonic`. Full analysis is in the issue thread and the progress note.

Closes #8642

author: gggaiitx
body:
## Bug 描述
MySQL 的 `GROUP_CONCAT` 函数默认 `group_concat_max_len` 为 1024 字节，当拼接大量字符串时输出会被静默截断，用户无法获取完整结果。在 DBX 中尝试手动执行 `SET SESSION group_concat_max_len` 也无效，因为每次连接会重置。

## 复现步骤
1. 连接 MySQL 数据库
2. 执行包含 `GROUP_CONCAT` 的查询，拼接结果超过 1024 字节
3. 返回结果被截断为默认长度

## 根因
`mysql_async` 的 setup queries 机制在连接建立后自动执行初始化 SQL，但没有设置 `group_concat_max_len`，导致使用 MySQL 默认值 1024。

## 修复方案
采用简单方案：在 MySQL 连接的 setup queries 中自动设置 group_concat_max_len 为一个较大的值。

在 `mysql_setup_queries_for_database()` 函数中，`SET NAMES {charset}` 之后添加：
```sql
SET SESSION group_concat_max_len = 1048576
```

将上限设为 1MB（1048576 字节），足够覆盖绝大多数使用场景。

## 影响范围
- 所有 MySQL 兼容数据库的连接（MySQL、MariaDB、OceanBase、TiDB 等）
- 不影响其他数据库类型

## 测试
- 更新了全部 18 个 `mysql_setup_queries` 相关测试断言
- `cargo test -p dbx-core mysql_setup_queries` 全部通过

## issue
[#2775](https://github.com/t8y2/dbx/issues/2775)

author: chetan-guevara
body:
## Why
The Learning page's "Narrative arcs" panel showed "No active narrative arcs yet" while the "Events" section right below it (same graph, same tier-scoped groups, same sparse-data fallback) rendered real recent data. Since both read the same Neo4j substrate the same way, the graph wasn't the problem -- something downstream of fetching facts was silently swallowing the result.

## Root cause
Two real bugs in `lib/graph/arcs.ts`:

1. **`parseArcsJson` required a bare JSON object**, but the prompt only *asks* Claude/GPT for that in text -- it's not enforced. Models commonly wrap the object in a markdown code fence or a leading sentence anyway. `JSON.parse` then throws, gets caught, and silently returns `[]` -- exactly the "no arcs" UI state, with zero diagnostics anywhere (nothing ever threw past that point, so no log, no Sentry event).
2. **`callLLM` had no try/catch**, despite `getArcs`'s own doc-comment promising "best-effort... returns [] when the graph/LLM is unavailable." A real LLM failure (bad key, rate limit, a retired model id) would throw uncaught through the API route -- 500, and the frontend's *different* error state ("Couldn't synthesize arcs right now"). Not what's happening here, but a real gap against the documented contract.
3. Noticed in passing: `ARCS_ANTHROPIC_MODEL` defaulted to an old model id while the Q&A path arcs is supposed to "mirror" has moved on to `claude-opus-4-8` -- updated the default to the current `claude-sonnet-5`.

## Fix
- `extractJsonObject()` unwraps a ```` ```json ```` fence, a bare ` ``` ` fence, or leading/trailing prose before `JSON.parse` -- handles the common cases, leaves a clean response untouched.
- `parseArcsJson` now logs (`console.error`, matching the bracketed-tag convention already used in `lib/ingest/scheduler.ts` etc.) when content still isn't parseable -- diagnosable instead of invisible.
- `callLLM` wraps the provider call in try/catch, logs, and degrades to `[]` -- actually implements the "best-effort" contract the code already claimed.
- System prompt now explicitly forbids markdown code fences (defense in depth on top of the parser fix).

## Test plan
- [x] 4 new cases in `test/graph-arcs-parse.test.ts`: fenced JSON, bare fence, leading/trailing prose, clean-response-untouched -- 11/11 pass
- [x] Full unit tier 411 passed, `tsc`, `eslint`, docs-drift clean
- [ ] Live verify: reload the Learning page after this deploys and confirm arcs populate (or, if they still don't, the new `[arcs]` server logs will say exactly why)

author: fmeriaux
body:
## Summary

Adopts the standard "train on logits" design: the output layer is now **linear**
(identity activation), softmax/sigmoid is no longer applied in the forward pass but
**folded into the cross-entropy loss** (training) and **reapplied at inference**. This
removes the loss-side probability clamp, keeps the backward pass uniform (the fused loss
gradient `p − y` reaches the affine map unchanged), and makes activations, losses, and
accuracies operate on **N-D tensors** — so a spatial/conv stack threads through end-to-end.

## What changed

**Logits everywhere, probabilities at the edges**
- New `Identity` activation (`f(x)=x`, identity VJP); `NeuronLayerSpec::output_for` now
  emits a linear output layer whose width still encodes the task (1 logit binary,
  `n_classes` multi-class), so the inference activation stays inferable.
- New `ClassifierActivations` trait reads an output stage's logits as class probabilities
  (sigmoid for one logit, softmax otherwise). `Predictor` gains `class_probabilities` /
  `classify_instance`; the decision boundary and activation diagram read through the same
  path.

**Cross-entropy split, from logits**
- `CrossEntropyLoss` → `BinaryCrossEntropy` (stable softplus, `σ(z)−y` gradient) and
  `CategoricalCrossEntropy` (max-shifted log-sum-exp, `softmax(z)−y` gradient).
- `LossFunction` gains a `Reduction` (Sum/Mean) and exposes per-term values; `build()`
  derives the loss **and** accuracy from the model's class count and stores both on the
  `Trainer`.

**Accuracy split**
- `MultiClassAccuracy` → `CategoricalAccuracy`; `accuracy_for(n_classes)` selects binary
  (threshold-at-0) vs categorical (argmax) — both scoring every trailing position.

**N-D data path**
- Activations, `Dense`, and `ModelDataset.targets` are now samples-last `ArrayD`: `Dense`
  folds trailing (sample + spatial) axes into columns and shares one weight matrix across
  every position. `ModelDataset` inputs/targets need only agree on sample count.

**Structure**
- `model.rs` split into `model/{specs,network,predictor}.rs`.

## Tests

All 551 tests green; lint + coverage gates pass (~98.5% line coverage, new files at/near
100%). New unit tests cover the identity activation, both cross-entropy variants (value +
gradient + reduction + spatial), categorical accuracy, the classifier
logits→probabilities path (incl. a conv network and a per-feature scaler on a rank-4
batch), and end-to-end backprop/finite-difference checks for binary and softmax outputs.

Added in review: a focused test locking `LossConfig::instantiate` — two-class → binary,
multi-class → categorical — mirroring the existing `accuracy_for` selection tests (the
selection was previously only reached indirectly through the convergence runs).

author: hetp88
body:
Summary
---

On the mobile dashboard header, tapping the hamburger only revealed the account trigger (avatar + username); a second tap on that was required to actually see the menu (Dashboard, Edit Profile, Security Settings, Log Out, ...). Since the hamburger's mobile nav panel has nothing else in it for a signed-in user, that second tap was pure friction with no benefit.

Why
---

User-reported UX issue: "in mobile view in user dashboard the hamburger menu reveal the username then clicking username will reveal another menu cant it be like at all once when click?" On mobile, the account trigger and account panel already sit inside the same hamburger-gated `.nav`, so gating them independently added a redundant disclosure step rather than protecting against clutter (unlike on desktop, where the trigger is the only way to reveal the dropdown at all).

What changed
---

* `app/static/js/theme.js` - the hamburger (`data-nav-toggle`) and account panel (`data-account-panel`) open/close state are now coupled: opening the nav also opens the account panel, and closing it (outside click, Escape, or clicking a menu item) closes both together. No new markup or CSS - reuses the existing `.account-panel`'s mobile layout, which already stacks correctly once expanded.
* Also fixes a latent bug found while making this change: the document-level "click outside closes the account menu" listener didn't exclude the hamburger button itself, so clicking it would open the panel and then immediately close it again in the same click (event bubbles from the button up to `document`). Now excluded via a `[data-nav-toggle]` check alongside the existing `[data-account-menu]` one.
* `tests/js/collect-browser-coverage.mjs` - new assertions: hamburger tap opens both nav and account panel together; clicking the hamburger itself isn't treated as an outside click; outside click / Escape / picking a menu item close both together.

Desktop is unaffected - the hamburger button is hidden outside the mobile breakpoint, so this coupling never fires there; the account trigger keeps its normal independent dropdown behavior.

Security impact
---

None - client-side disclosure-widget timing only, no new data exposed, no change to any auth/session control.

Deployment impact
---

* no deployment action

Verification
---

* `git diff --check`
* `.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest -q -n auto` - 1693 passed, 31 skipped
* `node tests/js/collect-browser-coverage.mjs` - 89.1% browser-script line coverage (>= 80% gate)

Notes

author: athvin
body:
Implements [`docs/implementation/phase-2-pg-sink/pr-2.15-pgarrow-tier3-text-carriers.md`](docs/implementation/phase-2-pg-sink/pr-2.15-pgarrow-tier3-text-carriers.md).

Some Postgres types have no lossless structural target in Parquet/DuckDB. This PR carries them as their **canonical text** in a single `VARCHAR` column — always exact as a string — and defers the lost *type metadata* to the descriptor (PR 2.17).

## What changed & why
- **`tier3.rs`** (new) — `is_tier3_text(oid, typmod)` and `tier3_field(name)` (one nullable `Utf8`). Value carried **verbatim** (the wire text is already canonical; re-formatting risks a lossy round-trip).
- **`schema.rs`** — `emit_fields` routes Tier-3 to one `Utf8` field, *after* the Tier-1 check so `numeric(p≤38)` still maps to `Decimal128`.
- **`batch.rs`** — `emit_kind` classifies Tier-3 as `Emit::Scalar`, reusing the existing `Utf8` `append_value` path.
- **`oids.rs`** — `XML 142, XID 28, CIDR 650, MACADDR8 774, MACADDR 829, INET 869, BIT 1560, VARBIT 1562, TXID_SNAPSHOT 2970, PG_LSN 3220, TSVECTOR 3614, TSQUERY 3615, XID8 5069`.
- **`tests/conformance.rs`** — each reads back as DuckDB `VARCHAR` verbatim; plus a 40+ digit numeric exactness test.

**The numeric split is the whole point** (§2.5): `p≤38` stays Tier-1 `Decimal128`; **unconstrained (typmod −1) or `p>38` becomes `VARCHAR`** because DuckDB's `DECIMAL` caps at precision 38 and its Parquet reader downcasts any `p>38` decimal to `DOUBLE` (so `Decimal256` would silently lose digits). `p==38` is the Tier-1 boundary. `uuid`/`enum` are deferred to PR 2.16; the loader-reapplied metadata to PR 2.17.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] `numeric(10,2)` still maps to `Decimal128(10,2)` (no regression); unconstrained `numeric` and `numeric(40,10)` map to a single `Utf8` field, value verbatim.
- [ ] `bit`/`varbit` carry `'0'/'1'` text; `inet`/`cidr`/`macaddr(8)`/`tsvector`/`tsquery`/`pg_lsn`/`xid(8)`/`xml` all map to `Utf8`.
- [ ] Conformance: each reads back as DuckDB `VARCHAR` with the exact string; a `p>38` value written as VARCHAR round-trips exactly.
- [ ] A comment records the DuckDB `p>38 → DOUBLE` downcast as the reason for VARCHAR (not Decimal256).
- [ ] **Green locally and in CI:** `cargo fmt --check` · `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` · `cargo test -p pg-to-arrow` and `cargo test -p pg-to-arrow --features conformance`

## Local verification
- `green.sh` — all passed
- `cargo test -p pg-to-arrow` — 55 passed
- `cargo test -p pg-to-arrow --features conformance` — 26 passed (3 new: unconstrained numeric, p>38 exactness, system types)

body:
This PR separates machine fixture intake from human adjudication for Quick Check v2 fixtures.

What changed:
- `npm run quickcheck:fixture:add` now writes `gold.draft.json` only and leaves `gold.json` absent.
- The intake metadata and manifest entry are marked `adjudicationStatus: "pending"`.
- `corrections.json` is now a pending sentinel instead of reviewed corrections.
- `REVIEW.md` now says `Adjudication not done.` and gives the later review checklist.
- Fixture loader tests treat missing or pending gold as non-truth and skip strict eval for pending fixtures.

Why:
- PR1 intake should store raw machine output without implying human-reviewed gold truth.
- Pending fixtures must not be consumed by strict eval as if they were adjudicated.
