author: paudley
body:
Closes #1380.

## Summary
A Rust-first producer that reads a **captured** HuggingFace GoEmotions classifier output (a checked-in JSON envelope — never on-gate inference) and emits **attributed GMEOW evidence**: a `gmeow:ModelInferenceRun` + one `gmeow:AffectClassifierOutput` per label (+ supported `gmeow:AffectiveClaim` / `gmeow:AffectEvaluationConcluded`). Evidence, never inner-affect fact. The output passes the existing Stage-4 hard-fail SHACL gates unweakened, and flows to the `gmeow` CLI.

## Scope decision (settled here)
In-tree Rust crate that is **also** the documented producer API **and** a `gmeow` CLI subcommand — forced by CONSTITUTION.md (RUST-FIRST, dogfooding, no-optionality) and the sibling producer precedent (`crates/foundation-corpus`, `crates/affect`). Determinism is preserved by transforming a captured output, never running live inference on-gate.

## Maintainer ruling (auditable)
#1380's **formal Acceptance criterion is GoEmotions-only**. The SST-2 / CardiffNLP / j-hartmann / zero-shot adapters named in the Requirements list ("then …") are OUT of this PR's acceptance and are tracked in the follow-on issue **#1392** opened for them (there was no pre-existing tracking issue; #1381 covers Stage-5 *bridges*, not adapters). The parameterized ingestion core makes each future adapter a capture + config, not new producer code.

## What ships
- **`crates/affect-ingest`** (`gmeow-affect-ingest`): the label-set-parameterized producer.
  - **Put leg** `produce(capture, config) -> Turtle`: all labels emitted losslessly; Rust hard-fails (before any emission) for missing revision (rule 7), unregistered label (rule 2), calibrated-without-calibration (rule 4), NaN/±Inf/out-of-`[0,1]` score, duplicate label, invalid/duplicate target IRI, `return_all_scores` subset, activation mismatch. Deterministic idempotent minted IRIs (FNV-1a of recoverable content — no `NOW()`/random).
  - **Get leg** `recover(turtle, config) -> capture`, authored **independently** of the put leg; the round-trip `recover(produce(cap)) == canonicalize(cap)` is the **executable proof of losslessness** (per the repo's put-honesty / section-discharge doctrine), not an emit-count.
  - Label set + canonical `EmotionType` typing loaded from the ontology **base graph**; the reviewed label→emotion `skos:closeMatch` correspondence loaded from the bundle's **SSSOM blob** (the pipeline keeps the correspondence lowering out of the base graph — Principle 17 — so the SSSOM surface is the runtime single source of truth). `grief`=broadMatch and `desire`→`gmeow:Desire` are correctly excluded from emotion-claim routing.
- **Real fixture** `crates/affect-ingest/fixtures/goemotions-sample.json`: real model id, real pinned commit revision, real 28-label vocabulary; representative multi-label-sigmoid scores (provenance documented in `fixtures/README.md`).
- **Conformance gate** `crates/validate/tests/conformance_affect_producer.rs`: the real fixture's emitted TTL conforms against the **unmodified** `whole_shapes()` corpus; round-trip holds end-to-end; `AffectEvaluationConcluded` conforms for all-sub-threshold; tampering fires the exact Stage-4 shape; Rust hard-fails for rules 2 & 7. Also pins the pre-existing `examples/goemotions-run.ttl` against the shapes (duplicate reconciliation).
- **CLI**: `gmeow affect ingest-goemotions <capture.json> [-o out.ttl]` and `gmeow affect recover-goemotions <graph.ttl>` (`-`=stdin); a smoke test pipes ingest→recover through the built binary.

## Changes
- New crate `crates/affect-ingest` (put leg + get leg + config + fixture + tests), registered in the workspace.
- New conformance twin `conformance_affect_producer.rs` (whole-ontology SHACL, round-trip, tamper, hard-fail, example-pin).
- `gmeow-cli`: two `affect` subcommands + SSSOM-driven config + stdin support + CLI smoke tests.
- Zero new ontology terms; zero Python. `make check` green (Docker-free, Java-free).

## Verification
- `cargo test -p gmeow-affect-ingest` (17) · `cargo test -p gmeow-validate --test conformance_affect_producer` (11) · `cargo test -p gmeow-cli --test cli` (24) · `make check` green after integrating current `origin/main`.

author: rukasakurai
body:
Closes #50.

## What

Adds `docs/policies.md` — a lean boundary note for the Foundry **Operate > Compliance > Policies** tab.

Core message: this portal surface is Azure Policy-based **configuration compliance** for guardrail/content-filter settings. It audits whether deployments meet a minimum guardrail bar; it does **not** inspect runtime prompts/responses or apply runtime blocking. Runtime enforcement belongs in **Build > Guardrails** for Foundry-managed models/agents, or in app code via **Azure AI Content Safety**.

Also registers `docs/policies.md` in the `e2e-foundry-baseline` skill's Documentation coverage table.

## Verification

- Microsoft Learn: checked the Compliance/Policies docs, Guardrails overview, Content Safety overview, Azure Policy overview, built-in initiatives, and Foundry Tools policy reference.
- Azure Policy definitions: inspected the built-in guardrail initiative (`[Preview]: Guardrail for Cognitive Services Deployments`) and member definitions; the guardrail/content-filter definitions expose `Audit`/`Disabled`, and inspect deployment `raiPolicy` configuration rather than runtime prompt/response payloads.
- Live portal: confirmed the Compliance workspace preview badge, the Create policy page footer (*"Setting a policy does not automatically enforce guardrails"*), content-safety-shaped inputs, and subscription/resource-group-only scope options.
- Live spikes: verified Foundry guardrails/content filters block unsafe prompts at inference; verified `approved models` Deny blocks portal/data-plane model deployment but not ARM/Bicep control-plane deployment.

One attempted live check did not complete conclusively: a portal-created guardrail policy did not appear as an Azure Policy assignment in `az policy assignment list` during the observation window. The doc therefore relies on Microsoft Learn + built-in policy definitions for that mechanism claim, not on an observed assignment object.

## E2E note

This is a docs-accuracy change with no required `azd provision` flow. Verification was done through Learn, live portal checks, Azure Policy definition inspection, and targeted live spikes against throwaway resources.

body:
## Phase E — Zweisprachigkeit für SEO (letzte Phase)

Baut auf A–D auf. Sprache läuft über `I18n` (`?lang=` + Cookie, Default **EN**) — es gibt keine `/de/`-`/en/`-Pfade, daher: **DE = `?lang=de`, EN/Default = paramlos**.

### Änderungen
- **Sprach-bewusster Canonical** (`SiteUrl::localized`): Default (EN) paramlos, DE = `?lang=de`. Jede Sprachfassung **kanonisiert sich selbst** → die hreflang-Alternates greifen (sonst hätte der paramlose Phase-A-Canonical sie ausgehebelt).
- **hreflang-`<link>`** (de / en / x-default) im `<head>` **aller 3 Layouts** (`SiteUrl::hreflangLinks`) — reziprok, identischer Satz je Fassung.
- **`og:locale`** dynamisch (`de_DE`/`en_US`) + `og:locale:alternate`; `<html lang>` folgt der aktiven Sprache.
- **Sitemap**: `xmlns:xhtml` + `<xhtml:link>`-Alternates (de/en/x-default) je URL.
- **GA**: `page_language` als Parameter (ga-data JSON → `gtag config`).

### Verifikation
- `php -l` (alle) + `node --check ga.js`: clean.
- `composer test:unit`: **184 Tests grün**.
- Smoke: EN self-canonical paramlos, DE self-canonical `?lang=de`, `<html lang>` + `page_language` korrekt, hreflang-Satz reziprok, Sitemap **valide (33 URLs + Alternates)**.

### Damit ist der SEO-/Analytics-Plan (A–E + Routen-og:image) vollständig.

author: neosinner
body:
## Description

The subscriber import auto-mapper was switched from substring regex matching to exact-match header arrays (PR #6949). That tightening dropped support for name headers that use a separator other than a space — `first_name`, `first-name`, `first.name` — as well as common abbreviations (`fname`, `lname`). Those columns were silently mapped to `ignore`, so exports from databases and CRM tools (Salesforce, HubSpot) required manual re-mapping with no error shown.

Rather than enumerate every separator × synonym combination, the header is now normalized before matching: underscore, hyphen and dot are collapsed to a single space, so `first_name` / `first-name` / `first.name` / `First Name` all resolve to the same value. The `fname` / `lname` abbreviations are added explicitly.

Matching stays whole-string, so the original tightening is preserved — unrelated headers like `first_updated`, `last_login`, `FIRSTUPDATED` still fall through to `ignore`.

## Code review notes

The exact-match arrays were introduced in #6949 specifically to stop the old `/first/i` and `/last/i` substring regexes from grabbing headers like `last_login`. Normalization keeps that guarantee because it compares the whole normalized header, not a substring — see the `does not match unrelated headers` test covering `first_updated` / `last_order`.

## QA notes

Import a CSV whose header row uses any of `first_name` / `first-name` / `first.name` / `fname` (and the last-name equivalents). Those columns should auto-map to First name / Last name instead of Ignore.

author: timmyy3000
body:
## Summary

`forest close <name>` silently exited 0 when the name matched nothing in Forest state, which reads as success and masks state drift (seen in the wild: a wiped `.forest/state` left orphaned git worktrees, and an agent misread the silent no-op as a partial close). Separately, `--include-dirty` could never actually close a dirty worktree because the underlying `git worktree remove` ran without `--force` and refused.

## What's Included

- `App.Close` now returns `unknown worktree <name> (run 'forest doctor' ...)` when a named close matches no state record; `--merged` mode is unaffected.
- `--include-dirty` now maps to `git worktree remove --force` (`git.WorktreeRemove` gains a `force` param); flag help text updated to disclose this.
- New tests: unknown-name error leaves state untouched, `--include-dirty` removes a dirty worktree end-to-end, dirty-without-flag still skips with reason `dirty`.

## Tests

- `go test ./...`: passed
- `go vet ./...`: passed
- `gofmt -l internal/`: clean

## Test Plan

- Traced `Close` with concrete inputs: non-matching name (now errors), matching-but-dirty without flag (skips, state kept), matching dirty with `--include-dirty --yes` (removed from git and state).
- Verified the unknown-name error returns from inside `state.WithLock` before any side effect, so no partial state writes and the lock is released.
- `--merged` with zero integrated worktrees still exits 0.

author: l0ng-ai
body:
Bundles two independent terminal-UI fixes.

## feat(menu): shortcut hints in the right-click menu

The context menu showed keyboard hints on some rows but not others: Clear /
Split / Maximize / New Tab / Close Pane are keybinding-backed so gpui-component
auto-renders their hint, while Copy / Paste / Select All / Find are dispatched
inline in `handle_cmd_shortcut` with no registered `KeyBinding`, so they showed
nothing.

- Render the missing hints ourselves via `menu_row_with_hint`, styled to match
  the auto-rendered ones — rather than register real bindings, which would risk
  the Ctrl+C SIGINT fall-through on Windows/Linux.
- ⌘A / ⌘F are macOS-only (on Windows/Linux those chords keep their readline
  meaning), so those two hints are gated behind `mac_only`.
- Also fixes the **"Select All" menu item diverging from ⌘A**: both now route
  through `select_all_contextual` (edited command line at the prompt, otherwise
  the whole terminal buffer), so click and shortcut stay in sync.

## fix(terminal): accept ASCII keystrokes in the Ctrl+R reverse-search prompt

The reverse-search query only took text from the IME commit path, so a plain
ASCII input source — and all typing on Linux (`prefers_ime_for_printable_keys`
false) — was swallowed. Forward printable `key_char` events into `push_query`,
mirroring the editor's key_char path; control/Cmd/Alt chords still fall through.
Reported on V2EX.

## Verification
- `cargo check` / `cargo clippy` clean (no new warnings), `cargo fmt` applied.
- `cargo test --bin tty7`: 357 passed.
- Ran the app via `cargo dev` and exercised the right-click menu.

author: ramazankarisan
body:
## What

Extends the backpressure quality gates with best-practice lint rules and duplication detection, using **one linter**: strict TS + React, `curly` (no braceless blocks), no frequent abbreviations, and jscpd for copy-paste.

## One linter: ESLint (`eslint.config.js`)

ESLint is the **single** linter — the only one that enforces every requested rule in one pass. **oxlint and biome have no abbreviation rule**, so a Rust linter can't cover the "no abbreviations" ask; ESLint (via `eslint-plugin-unicorn`) is the only option. Scoped to `src/`; Deno `supabase/**` excluded; `--max-warnings 0` makes warnings blocking.

- **strict TypeScript** — `no-explicit-any`, `consistent-type-imports`, `no-non-null-assertion`, `array-type`, `ban-ts-comment`
- **React** — `rules-of-hooks`, `jsx-key`, `no-danger`, `self-closing-comp`, `only-export-components`
- **general** — `curly` (no braceless blocks), `eqeqeq`, `no-var`, `prefer-const`, `no-else-return`, `object-shorthand`, `no-console`
- **no abbreviations** — `unicorn/name-replacements` with a domain/React allowList (`props`, `ref`, `env`, `db`, `fn`, …)

## jscpd — duplication gate (`.jscpd.json`)

Copy-paste detector (not a lint rule) with a **ratchet threshold** just above the current 2.25% baseline: passes today, blocks meaningful new duplication. `supabase/**` excluded (its date/message logic is duplicated from `src/` on purpose).

## Wiring

Single `lint` (eslint) + `dupes` (jscpd) across **lefthook** (pre-commit lint, pre-push dupes), the **Stop hook**, and **CI**. Docs updated: `docs/backpressure.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `README.md`, `SETUP.md`.

## Fixes for surfaced violations
Curly braces, `Array<T>` types, renames (`err`→`error`, `prev`→`previous`, `e`→`event`, `settingsRes`→`settingsResponse`), guarded `#root` lookup in `main.tsx`.

## History
Landed in two commits: first added strict rules + a jscpd gate (two-linter oxlint+eslint), second **consolidated to a single ESLint linter** per review (dropped oxlint).

## Follow-up (not in this PR)
5 existing clones (two `*Form.tsx`, two `*View.tsx`, self-dup in `useAppData`). Refactor, then lower the jscpd threshold.

## Verification
All 8 gates green locally + on push: prettier, eslint, jscpd, tsc, knip, secretlint, build. pre-commit + pre-push hooks exercised end-to-end.

author: nicolajhave
body:
## Hvorfor

På ægte udbryder-etaper (E4/E9/E13) floater rå form GC-stjernerne højt — de *er* stærkest på papiret — men i virkeligheden lader favoritterne udbruddet gå og ruller selv i bunken. På break-dage har værdikurven negativ baseline (−67.500), så en GC-stjerne der sidder op **taber** værdi (bunke ≈ −65k). Uden dette anbefalede hold-rådgiveren GC-for-GC-skifter til E4, hvilket du fangede som forkert.

## Hvad

Ny delt `breakStrength()`-helper, brugt af felt-sort, `teamWinProb` og `evOnProfile` — så kandidat-tabellen, transfer-evaluatoren, hold-rådgiveren og udsynet alle er konsistente på break:

- **top-12 GC-ledere** (rangeret på bjerg-styrke = `form + β·bjerg-fit`) demoteres til bunke (`−1` → `Math.max(0,·)` nulstiller dem i MC/softmax → altid feltværdi)
- **resten** rangeres på en klatrevægtet udbryder-score `0.6·bjerg + 0.4·break` i stedet for rå form

Kun break-profilen påvirkes; alle andre profiler er uændrede.

## Validering (headless mod E4-snapshot)

| Profil | Top | GC-stjerner |
|---|---|---|
| **break (fix)** | Grégoire, Jegat, Vacek, Van Gils, Baudin, Hindley … (klatrestærke udbrydere) | Pogačar/Vingegaard/Del Toro/Evenepoel/Lipowitz → felt-rank ~175, ev ≈ −63k |
| **mountain (kontrol)** | Vingegaard, Pogačar, Del Toro, Lipowitz | uændret — tilbage i toppen |

Ingen page-errors. `npm run prove` grøn. Break forbliver lav-tillid (lotteri) — dette fjerner blot det systematiske GC-bias.

author: jayykk
body:
…ntry

The real cause of the lobby flash: hostedSessions/joinedSessions were component-local refs, so every visit to the lobby reset them to [] — the "My events" section (which sits ABOVE the always-present quick actions) vanished and popped back in when the first snapshot arrived, shoving the whole layout down. onMounted also awaited loadMyRooms before even attaching the session listeners, delaying that pop further.

- Move the lists into a module-level cache in useSessions (myHostedSessions / myJoinedSessions, cleared on user switch): revisiting the lobby now renders the previous list instantly and refreshes silently
- Attach the session listeners before any awaited work in onMounted
- Wrap the section in a max-height/opacity Transition so its very first appearance slides open instead of jumping in a single frame

author: nischal94
body:
## What

Closes the highest-priority residual gap from PR #15's Tier 2 review: `rowToTool` blind-cast the `source_semantics` JSON blob (`JSON.parse(...) as SourceSemantics`), letting three vocabularies — `kind`, graphql `operation`, and custom_js `declaredRisk` — bypass the read-side guards PRs #14/#15 added for column values.

- **`parseSourceSemantics` at the deserialization boundary**: validates the discriminated union on `kind`, per-variant field checks (openapi `method`/`path` strings, graphql `operation` vocabulary, mcp boolean hints, custom_js `declaredRisk` vocabulary), rebuilding the value field-by-field so unknown keys drop and absent optionals stay absent. Same `[SqliteStore] Failed to read tool: ...` error format, JSON.stringify'd bad values, tool name as context.
- **Why this one had no CHECK twin**: SQLite CHECK constraints can't see inside a JSON blob, so unlike every vocabulary hardened in #14/#15, this read-side guard is the *only* enforcement layer — on fresh schemas too, not just legacy ones.
- **`deriveRiskClass` fails closed** (second commit): it's exported public API; an impossible `kind` previously fell off the default-less switch as `undefined`-as-`RiskClass`, and `declaredRisk` passed through unvalidated. Both now return `"destructive"`, with a `never` binding preserving compile-time exhaustiveness — policy.ts default-arm discipline. Deliberately independent from the store layer; do not deduplicate.
- **Bare-SyntaxError gap folded in** (rated cheap): every JSON column parse (`input_schema`, `output_schema`, `seeds`, `paused_on`, trace `input`/`output_summary`) now routes through a wrapper that throws with entity + row identity instead of a context-free `SyntaxError` — and carries the original error as `cause`, since its parse position is what locates corruption in a large blob.
- **Tier 2 fixes** (third commit, findings in the review comment below): the mcp arm of `deriveRiskClass` used truthiness and failed OPEN for untyped callers (`readOnlyHint: "false"` — a truthy string — earned "safe"); hints are now boolean-or-absent, anything else → `"destructive"`. A non-string openapi `method` classifies destructive instead of throwing a bare TypeError.

## Tests

21 new tests, 151/151 green (130 on main), tsc + Biome clean: rejects for each smuggled vocabulary and malformed variant shape via the legacy-schema fixture, store-context wrapping (with `cause`) for unparseable JSON across all four entities and both nullable columns, a compiler-pinned kind-exhaustiveness round-trip (`toStrictEqual` pins absent-optional discipline), unknown-key dropping, log-injection escaping on the tools error path, and fail-closed pins for every `deriveRiskClass` arm.

## Deviations

- Started stacked on PR #15's branch because #15 was still open and touched the same two files; #15 merged between sittings while the branch had no commits yet, so a `--ff-only` merge moved it onto origin/main — the PR is based on main exactly as the task specified. No net deviation.
- An earlier revision of this description said "13 new tests / 145 green" — that conflated RED-failure count with new-test count; corrected above.

## Follow-ups (from the Tier 2 reviews, deliberately not in this PR)

- `seeds`/`pausedOn` are still shape-unvalidated after parsing — corrupt seeds silently diverge §5.5 replay, and `"null"` in `paused_on` loads as a null `PendingApproval`. Must-fix before §5.5 resume ships, alongside `maybeText`/`maybeInteger` conflating NULL with type corruption.
- The invariant `status === "paused"` ⟺ `paused_on IS NOT NULL` is unenforced at the store boundary.
- Cross-field drift: `risk_class = "safe"` beside `declaredRisk = "destructive"` passes both vocabulary guards independently; consider re-deriving on read.

## Problema

Sem feature aprovada no backlog (`#59` Mascotes e `#61` bundle share seguem sem label `approved`) e sem PR travado, este ciclo seguiu o trilho A/C (bug de acessibilidade + polish). Um survey comparando os 4 builders, 4 páginas de lista, o `AppHeader` e todos os modais (`QuickRefModal`, `AddAdversaryModal`, `GeneratorModal`, `SessionTrackerModal`) encontrou duas inconsistências reais:

1. **`SessionTrackerModal` reimplementava seu próprio focus-trap** em vez de usar o hook compartilhado `useFocusTrap` (usado por `QuickRefModal`, `AddAdversaryModal` e `GeneratorModal`). A versão manual cuidava de Tab/Shift+Tab e Escape, mas **nunca devolvia o foco** ao elemento que abriu o modal ao fechar — o único modal do app com esse comportamento. Um usuário de teclado que abre "▶ Sessão" (o modal mais interativo do app, usado durante todo o combate) e fecha com Escape perdia a posição de tab e precisava recomeçar do topo da página.
2. **`AdversaryCard.tsx`** (botão de favorito, estado não-favoritado): hover usava `hover:text-amber-600` sem variante `dark:`, diferente do mesmo botão em `BestiarioCard.tsx` (`hover:text-amber-600 dark:hover:text-amber-400`) — mesma classe de bug de contraste que o PR #67 já havia corrigido em outros componentes, só que este arquivo ficou de fora.

## Solução

- `src/components/encounter/SessionTrackerModal.tsx`: remove o `useEffect` manual de ~35 linhas (Tab cycling + Escape) e troca por `useFocusTrap(containerRef, open, onPause)`, mesmo padrão dos outros 3 modais. Foco volta automaticamente ao botão "▶ Sessão" ao pausar/fechar.
- `src/components/library/AdversaryCard.tsx`: adiciona `dark:hover:text-amber-400` no botão de favorito (linha 59), igualando `BestiarioCard.tsx`.

## Riscos

Baixo — `useFocusTrap` já está em produção em 3 outros modais; nenhuma mudança de schema/storage/tipo. Diff líquido é negativo (-38 linhas).

## Como validei

- `npm run typecheck` e `npm run build` limpos.
- Rodei o dev/preview server com Playwright: criei um encontro com uma adversária, abri "▶ Sessão" com foco no botão, pressionei Escape, e confirmei via `document.activeElement` que o foco voltou ao botão que abriu o modal (antes: perdia o foco).
- Confirmei no CSS gerado que `.dark\:hover\:text-amber-400:hover:is(.dark *)` compila corretamente (mesma regra já usada em `BestiarioCard`).

## Checklist

- [x] Tipagem forte, sem `any` novo
- [x] Nomes explícitos, sem abstração nova (reuso de hook já existente)
- [x] `npm run typecheck` limpo
- [x] `npm run build` limpo
- [x] Diff escopado (2 arquivos, +4/-42 linhas)
- [x] Sem novas dependências

author: kenshin579
body:
## 개요

chronos-go가 operator-review의 `JobScheduler` 인터페이스(문자열 taskName + `[]byte` 페이로드)를 **코어 수정 없이 공개 API만으로 백킹**할 수 있음을 증명한다. 이 프로젝트의 **v1 성공 기준** 검증이다. operator-review 운영 코드는 건드리지 않았다.

## 접근

chronos-go는 제네릭(`Task[T]`, `Kind()`) 기반이라 문자열-키 `[]byte` 핸들러와 직접 안 맞는다. `examples/jobscheduler` 어댑터가 단일 브리지 타입 `rawTask{Name, Data}`(고정 Kind)를 쓰고, chronos 핸들러 하나가 `Name`으로 내부 맵을 라우팅해 원래 `SchedulerJobFunc`/`TaskHandlerFunc`를 호출한다.

- **스케줄 잡**: `chronos.RegisterInterval/RegisterCron`으로 `rawTask{Name}`을 주기 enqueue → 리더-only + 결정적 dedup으로 분산 단일 실행. scheduleID가 payload(taskName) 해시를 포함해 잡마다 구분됨.
- **Enqueue**: taskName/QueueKey를 FNV 해시 → N개 큐 분배(operator-review 동작 복제). `UniqueTTL` → `WithUnique`, 중복이면 조용히 skip.

## 검증 결과 (6개 동등성 테스트, 실 Redis)
- `[]byte` Enqueue → TaskHandler payload 왕복 ✅
- RegisterScheduledJob(interval) 주기 실행(분산 단일) ✅
- Enqueue + UniqueTTL 중복 억제(정확히 1회) ✅
- interval<1s 거부 / cron 스펙 검증 / 중복 taskName 거부 ✅

**결론: chronos-go 공개 API만으로 `JobScheduler` 6개 동작을 모두 백킹 가능 → v1 성공 기준 충족.** 코어 파일 수정 0건.

## 다음
이 증명을 바탕으로 operator-review의 `job_scheduler.go`를 asynq→chronos-go로 실제 교체(별도 저장소 작업)할 수 있다.

## Test Plan
- [ ] `make check` 통과
- [ ] `go test ./examples/jobscheduler/ -race` 6개 통과

author: ibanezar
body:
## Summary
- `_loadScript()` deduped concurrent loads by checking for an existing `<script>` tag in the DOM, but `appendChild` inserts the tag synchronously before the script has finished downloading/executing.
- A second caller loading the same script (e.g. two Leaflet-based widgets initializing around the same time — there are ~6 across the app) would see the tag already present and resolve immediately, even though the global (e.g. `window.L`) wasn't defined yet.
- This caused silent `ReferenceError: L is not defined` crashes swallowed by callers' `catch` blocks — observed as the new Surroundings-tab micro-climate map (#395) sometimes rendering as an empty box with no visible error.

## Fix
Track load completion with a `Set` populated only inside the real `onload` handler, instead of trusting DOM tag presence.

## Test plan
- [x] `node --check app.js` passes
- [x] Verified via browser agent: reproduced the original race 3/3 times, confirmed the fix removes reliance on the DOM-presence check; manually re-invoking the Leaflet map render after the real fix logic loads `L` correctly renders tiles/markers/popups

body:
The generator took a vague one-liner and made *bad tests*. Real tests come from a work item's **acceptance criteria** — so `ai-test-generator` now parses a ticket and produces **one traceable test per criterion**, then runs + repairs it via the existing closed loop.

## What
- `from-jira TICKET.md` (file / stdin / `-`) — a GitHub issue IS a git-hosted ticket, so `gh issue view 42 > TICKET.md` is all you need, **no Jira token**.
- `jira_ticket.parse_ticket` — offline, deterministic; handles Jira exports **and** `gh issue view` output (#/bold/colon headings, bullets/numbers/`- [ ]` checkboxes, wrapped + nested lines, fenced-code ignored, leading/bracketed keys only). A ticket with no criteria is **rejected**, not faked.
- `build_ticket_user_message` lists every AC + forbids merging/skipping + demands `AC1…ACn` tags.
- `validate_ticket_coverage` — the *good-tests* gate: ≥ one test per criterion, **each AC tag present** (per-criterion trace), key as a whole token.

## Trust
- **Adversarial multi-agent review → 18 confirmed defects fixed** (colon-bullet mis-heading, ISO-8601/UTF-8 key false-positives, code-fence leak, wrapped/nested criteria, cache-key collision, stale closed-loop path, non-playwright `--url`, unbounded input, substring key).
- **Validated live from git**: `gh issue view` → parser extracted 8 criteria from a real issue; smoke over 12 real tickets = **0 crashes**.
- **183 passing · 0 skipped · ruff clean.**

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves an Android CI flake where the saved-gateway reconnect test could fail when runtime auto-connect raced the test's explicit connection setup.

## Why This Change Was Made

The test now follows the real runtime lifecycle: await the saved gateway's automatic connection, rotate its stored credential, disconnect, refresh, and await the new desired connection. This removes the duplicate test-owned connection without weakening the reconnect assertion.

## User Impact

No runtime behavior changes. Android PRs get deterministic coverage that refresh reconnects the saved endpoint with current stored credentials.

## Evidence

- Before: the same assertion failed on two independent Android CI runs: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28841974007/job/85537799245 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28844741412/job/85546010186.

## Summary

Book & Seat's **Arrivals** lens (the *Expected · Waitlist · Seated* host queue) now handles the two host cases the Expected column couldn't:

- **Seat early** — a guest with a 14:00 booking who walks in at 12:30 gets a **Seat early** action that reschedules the reservation to *now* **and** seats it in one write (`seatEarly`). The record then matches reality — the timeline block, elapsed clock, and learned turn-time read the real seating moment instead of the stale future slot. It passes the service-window gate (can't seat before open) and overrides any table clash the earlier hour introduces; joins + needs are carried through.
- **Running late** — the Expected column now splits into two triage subsections: parties whose booked time has already passed and still aren't seated surface first under a danger-toned **◷ Running late** header (reading how many minutes over), then **Upcoming** below.

## Changes

- `src/core/service/CoreBook.tsx` — `seatEarly` handler (reschedule-to-now + seat in one POST); `lateExpected` / `upcomingExpected` split memos; Expected column rewritten into the two triage subsections with the early-seat action.
- `src/app/themes/core/parity/book.css` — `.apc.early` card accent + `.asubh` subsection dividers (Running late / Upcoming).
- `docs/design-system/core/modules/service.md` — Arrivals description updated to match (Rule #11).

Exercised end-to-end against a running dev server with real seeded bookings:

- Reschedule+seat: a 20:00 booking → `time 12:30, status seated, seatedAt stamped`.
- Side effects fire: floor table flipped to `seated`; POS check opened tagged with the guest.

author: echoowall
body:
## Summary

Closes #104.

The User Web **Document** page keeps rendering the Tutorial section even after an admin sets `subscribe.show_tutorial = false`. It's reproducible, not a flaky race.

## Root cause

1. The global store's initial `subscribe` state (`apps/user/src/stores/global.tsx`) has no `show_tutorial` field, so on first render `common.subscribe?.show_tutorial !== false` is `undefined !== false === true`.
2. `getGlobalConfig()` loads asynchronously in `__root.tsx`, so on the first render the config hasn't arrived yet — the tutorial query (`enabled: show_tutorial !== false`) fires immediately.
3. Once that query resolves, React Query caches the list. Flipping `enabled` to `false` afterwards stops *future* fetches but keeps the already-cached data.
4. The render gate only checked `TutorialList?.length > 0`, ignoring `show_tutorial` — so the section renders regardless of the setting.

## Fix

- **`stores/global.tsx`** — add `show_tutorial: false` to the initial `subscribe` state, so the query stays disabled on the first render until config loads. (The type already allows it: `subscribe.show_tutorial?: boolean`.)
- **`sections/user/document/index.tsx`** — extract a `showTutorial` flag and also gate the tutorial section's render on it, not only on the fetched list length. Defense in depth so cached data can never surface the section while it's disabled.

Either change alone fixes the reported issue; together they also close the cached-data path.

## Testing

- Tutorial disabled (`show_tutorial = false`) → Document page no longer renders the Tutorial section (query never fires, and the render is gated).
- Tutorial enabled → tutorial loads and renders as before.
- Both document and tutorial empty → the existing `<Empty />` state still shows.

author: cameronzucker
body:
Three modem-config usability fixes, root-caused against the operator's real box (r2-poe, x86 Ubuntu 24.04).

## Fixes
- **tuxlink-olxge** — declare `libhamlib-utils` (deb) / `hamlib` (rpm) as a dependency. Rig control (ARDOP+VARA CAT: the rig-model picker + rigctld QSY/VFO) hard-depends on `rigctl`/`rigctld`, but hamlib was neither bundled nor declared; on a box without it the picker silently degrades to a raw "hamlib model # (rigctl unavailable)" box. A fresh install now pulls it.
- **tuxlink-xj7e1** — enrich serial pickers with the real USB device name from sysfs (product/manufacturer/interface/serial), e.g. `/dev/ttyUSB0 — Silicon Labs CP2105 Dual UART Bridge (port 0) SN 01C71CA5`, so the two interfaces of a dual-UART DigiRig-class adapter are distinguishable instead of both showing "USB serial". Walks ancestors for `bInterfaceNumber` (ttyACM). Pure formatter + injectable sysfs reader + tests.
- **tuxlink-6urh2** — VARA drop-detection. The `SocketLost` heartbeat was deferred and never wired, so closing VARA left the session stuck `Open` with the config fields locked and no recovery. Implemented a consuming, EOF-aware liveness heartbeat (uses VARA's `IAMALIVE` as the alive signal; a non-consuming peek was tried first and **rejected** because VARA's buffered keepalives hide the peer FIN). Borrows the transport under a new `TransportOwner::Heartbeat` with a bounded ~50ms probe, generation-guarded re-install/`SocketLost`. Also fixes the shared root cause (`recv()` collapsing EOF+timeout) which cured the listener's blind spot, the double-open guard, and the frontend never polling `vara_status` (so the panel unlocks + shows "connection lost — reopen").

## Review
5-round-equivalent: full Codex adrev caught a **fatal flaw** in the first heartbeat (peek blind to the FIN) → rebuilt consuming; parent-verified the concurrency (lock discipline, close-generation guard, bounded borrow); Codex re-round quota-deferred, Claude self-adrev in its place. hamlib/serial Codex-clean.

## Verify
- CI `deb-install-test` proves the hamlib dep resolves on a clean container.
- Operator installs the fresh `.deb`: hamlib pulled + rig picker populates, serial names readable, closing VARA unlocks the panel instead of wedging.

Draft pending: CI (both arches) + self-adrev.

### Summary

Connects the frontend to the backend so the entire Civora flow works end-to-end: citizen submits issue → backend enriches/scores/clusters → confirmation shows real results → MP dashboard displays live data.

---

### What Changed

**Frontend — Issue Submission Flow**
- `AIProcessing.tsx`: Replaced fake 4-second timer with a real `POST /issues` call. Progress animation runs in parallel; navigation to confirmation happens only after the API responds. Error state shown on failure.
- `AIConfirmation.tsx`: Removed locally-generated mock interpretation. Now displays real backend response: `projectTitle`, `priorityScore`, `clusterId`, `clusterSummary`, `issueTheme`, `recommendedDepartment`, `explanation`.
- `ReportContext.tsx`: Added `backendResponse` state so AIProcessing can pass the API result to AIConfirmation.

**Frontend — MP Dashboard**
- `MPDashboard.tsx` (new): Dashboard page calling `GET /summary` and `GET /hotspots`. Shows stat cards, category/severity breakdowns, top wards/projects, and a Leaflet heatmap with cluster markers.
- `App.tsx`: Added `/dashboard` route.
- `BottomNavigation.tsx`: Added Dashboard tab.

**Frontend — API Layer**
- `endpoints.ts`: Added `seedDemoIssues()` and `clearDemoIssues()` functions.
- `types/api.ts`: Added `clusterSummary`, `explanation`, `projectTitle`, `issueTheme`, `recommendedDepartment`, `finalCategory`, `severity` to `IssueSubmitResponse`. Added `SeedResponse` and `ClearResponse` types.

**Backend — Response Expansion**
- `routes/issues.js`: `POST /issues` now returns `explanation`, `projectTitle`, `issueTheme`, `recommendedDepartment`, `finalCategory`, `severity` alongside existing fields.
- `services/issueService.js`: `submitIssue()` returns expanded AI fields in response.
- `services/aiClient.js`: Wrapped fragile `require("../../../ai-services/...")` in try/catch with graceful fallback. Added TODO comment for npm workspaces adoption.

**AI Services — Dependency Cleanup**
- `geminiAdapter.js`, `speechToTextAdapter.js`, `visionAdapter.js`: Removed `node-fetch` import; using native `fetch` (Node.js 22+).
- `translationAdapter.js`: Lazy-loaded `@google-cloud/translate` singleton. No crash at startup without credentials. Removed duplicate `module.exports`.
- `speechToTextAdapter.js`: Removed duplicate `module.exports`.
- `enrichIssue.js`: Fixed bug — `translationResult.detectedLanguage` → `translationResult.language` (property name mismatch with adapter return type).
- `package.json`: Removed `node-fetch` dependency.

**Shared**
- `contracts.md`: Full rewrite matching actual backend responses. Added dev endpoint documentation (`POST /dev/seed`, `DELETE /dev/clear`).

---

### End-to-End Flow (After This PR)

```
Citizen fills report (Steps 1-4)
  → Step4Review navigates to /ai-processing
  → AIProcessing calls POST /issues (real backend)
  → AIConfirmation displays: projectTitle, priorityScore, clusterId,
    clusterSummary, issueTheme, recommendedDepartment, explanation
  → Done navigates to /success with tracking ID

MP opens /dashboard
  → Calls GET /summary → stat cards, category/severity, top wards/projects
  → Calls GET /hotspots → Leaflet map with cluster markers
  → Empty state offers "Load Demo Data" button (calls POST /dev/seed)
```

---

### Files Changed (20)

| Area | Files |
|------|-------|
| Frontend pages | `AIProcessing.tsx`, `AIConfirmation.tsx`, `MPDashboard.tsx` (new) |
| Frontend core | `App.tsx`, `ReportContext.tsx`, `BottomNavigation.tsx`, `index.css` |
| Frontend API | `endpoints.ts`, `types/api.ts` |
| Backend | `routes/issues.js`, `services/issueService.js`, `services/aiClient.js` |
| AI services | `geminiAdapter.js`, `speechToTextAdapter.js`, `visionAdapter.js`, `translationAdapter.js`, `enrichIssue.js`, `package.json` |
| Shared | `contracts.md` |

---

### Verification

**Backend starts and all endpoints work:**
```powershell
cd backend-api; npm run dev
Invoke-RestMethod -Method Get -Uri "http://localhost:5001/"
Invoke-RestMethod -Method Post -Uri "http://localhost:5001/dev/seed"
Invoke-RestMethod -Method Get -Uri "http://localhost:5001/summary"
Invoke-RestMethod -Method Get -Uri "http://localhost:5001/hotspots"
```

**Frontend builds cleanly:**
```powershell
cd frontend-pwa; npm install; npm run build

```

**Manual test:**
1. Start backend (`npm run dev`) and frontend (`npm run dev`)
2. Submit a citizen issue through the 4-step wizard
3. Confirm AIProcessing calls backend and shows real progress
4. Confirm AIConfirmation displays real priority score, cluster, and AI fields
5. Navigate to `/dashboard` and verify stats/hotspots load from backend
6. Click "Load Demo Data" on empty dashboard to seed issues

---

### Remaining Risks

- `aiClient.js` still uses relative path `../../../ai-services/src/enrichIssue` — documented as TODO for npm workspaces
- `@google-cloud/speech` is a dependency but lazy-loaded at runtime
- `@react-google-maps/api` is installed but unused (~6.2KB waste)

author: rso
body:
## Summary

- Extend the `/api/profile` `GET` response with two additive fields:
  - `hasPersonalOrganization`: derived as the inverse of the user's `personal_account_disabled` flag (`true` when the personal account is not disabled).
  - `selectedOrganizationId`: the id of the first organization in the profile organizations list (`undefined` when the user has no organizations).
- Make `getProfileOrganizations` ordering deterministic (`created_at`, then `id`) so the first element is a stable default selection.
- Exclude "Access Blocked" organizations from the `/api/profile` organizations list. An org is excluded when its free trial has hard-expired without an active entitlement (`classifyOrganizationEntitlement(...).isTrialExpiredForEnforcement`). These orgs are locked to read-only, so they should not be offered as selectable orgs (and cannot become the default `selectedOrganizationId`).
  - Implemented as an opt-in `excludeAccessBlocked` option on `getProfileOrganizations`, enabled only for `/api/profile`.
  - Reuses the canonical `classifyOrganizationEntitlement` classifier (same logic the UI lock dialog and server-side trial enforcement use).
  - Stays a single query: when the option is set, each org's latest subscription status is selected via a correlated subquery; when it isn't (e.g. `/api/organizations`), no seat-purchase lookup runs and the query is unchanged.

## Verification

- Hit `/api/profile` as an authenticated user and confirmed the response includes `hasPersonalOrganization` and `selectedOrganizationId`, with `selectedOrganizationId` matching the first entry of `organizations`.
- Confirmed an org with a hard-expired trial and no active subscription is omitted from `/api/profile`, while the same org with an active seat purchase remains included.

## Visual Changes

N/A

## Reviewer Notes

- Changes are additive to the JSON contract, so existing consumers (`RedeemPromoCode.tsx`, `ProfileCreditsCounter.tsx`) are unaffected.
- `hasPersonalOrganization` is interpreted as `!personal_account_disabled`; flag if a different mapping is intended.
- The access-blocked filter targets only the non-dismissible hard-lock enforcement state (`isTrialExpiredForEnforcement`), not the earlier dismissible `trial_expired_soft` read-only state.
- `excludeAccessBlocked` defaults to `false`, so `/api/organizations` (the other `getProfileOrganizations` caller) issues the same query as before and is behaviorally unchanged.

author: clubanderson
body:
Fixes #20007

## Root Cause
The nightly unit test suite (2000+ test files across 41,573 tests) was crashing with "Worker exited unexpectedly" errors due to insufficient heap memory. The previous limit of 1792 MB (1.75 GB) was set for a 3-worker configuration but became inadequate after vite.config.ts was changed to maxWorkers=1 for CI stability. A single worker processing the entire suite requires significantly more heap to maintain test state, mocks, and module caches.

## Fix
Increased NODE_OPTIONS --max-old-space-size from 1792 MB to 3584 MB (3.5 GB) for CI environments. This provides sufficient headroom for the single worker to process all test files without OOM crashes while staying well within the ubuntu-latest runner's 7 GB RAM limit.

Memory allocation breakdown:
- 3.5 GB: Worker heap
- 1.5 GB: System + V8 non-heap overhead
- 2.0 GB: Safety margin
- Total: 7.0 GB (matches runner capacity)

## Testing
- No local testing required (CI-only change)
- Will verify in nightly test run

## Files Changed
- `scripts/unit-test.sh`: Increased NODE_OPTIONS --max-old-space-size from 1792 to 3584

itself as a declared route, so the runner no longer needs module-specific
knowledge to serve it.

body:
## Wave 2 of the workout logging redesign — education content

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-06-workout-logging-redesign-design.md §4

- `exercise_guides` table (migration 080, additive) + seed pipeline (same runSeed/adapter pattern as program_templates; auto-applies via the container init-seed oneshot on deploy)

- `GET /api/exercises/:slug/guide` (public cache; 404 → UI hides ⓘ)

## Fixes found during live end-to-end verification

Driving the real app (local JWKS + real API + real Postgres, browser via Playwright) surfaced two bugs component tests missed:

1. **Guide/history fetches dropped on effect re-fire** (`7ab10e0`) — the effect-cleanup cancellation plus forever-dedupe ref meant the resolved guide was discarded and never refetched under StrictMode (or any mid-flight `focusedEntry` identity change). ⓘ never rendered in the running app; W1's history prefill had the same latent bug. Fixed + StrictMode regression tests.
2. **Set logging 400s against the real API** (`d9069d7`) — **live W1 regression, deployed since 2026-07-06**: the UI never sets `rpe`, the queue serialized `rpe: null`, and the write schema is optional-absent, so every real set-log POST failed with 400 and stranded the row after 5 retries. The offline specs mock the server handler, so CI never saw it. Fixed by stripping null optionals at the wire.

**Deploy note:** any prod IDB rows stranded by (2) have burned their 5 attempts and will not auto-retry; they surface via the O7 staleness banner. Lifting is pre-launch per data-state, so real-user impact is expected to be nil — verify after deploy.

**Follow-up (not in this PR):** a permanent 400 in the flush loop is treated as transient and burns all 5 retries; consider a terminal `markRejected` path for 4xx.

- api: schema, seed adapter round-trip, content coverage (44/44 + no-jargon gate), route tests — 541 unit + 313 integration green on a reset DB
- frontend: client, SetupCardSheet, ExerciseFocus ⓘ variants, container wiring (guide 404/failure degrade to no-ⓘ), StrictMode resilience, set-log wire payload — 485 green

author: simonaronbacar-ui
body:
## Qué hace

Implementa todas las correcciones de la auditoría de seguridad y rendimiento documentada en `docs/AUDITORIA-ZERO-TRUST-2026-07.md` (incluida en este PR), más los fixes de un segundo ciclo de revisión sobre el propio diff.

### Seguridad
- **Sesiones con vencimiento firmado y revocación real (RF-01/02):** la cookie de Google lleva `exp` verificado server-side; `requireAdmin` re-chequea la allowlist `admins` en cada mutación; la cookie de contraseña deja de ser `SHA-256(password)` fijo (pass-the-hash permanente) y pasa a un token HMAC con vencimiento. Formato unificado en `lib/sesion.ts`, compartido entre middleware (Edge) y server actions (Node).
- **Login endurecido (RF-03):** rate limit de 10 intentos por IP cada 15 min + comparación en tiempo constante.
- **Cabeceras de seguridad (RF-04):** `next.config.ts` nuevo con `frame-ancestors 'none'`, `nosniff`, HSTS, Referrer-Policy y Permissions-Policy.
- **Feedback público validado (RF-05):** `enviarFeedback` verifica que el comercio exista (antes: 500 por FK y feedback inyectable con un id inventado).

### Integridad de datos
- **Transacciones (RF-07):** `crearCliente` (comercio + link de mostrador atómicos) y `generarLotePiezas` (lock consultivo — dos lotes concurrentes colisionaban en la PK).
- **UPDATEs atómicos:** `actualizarCliente`/`actualizarLink` y las capturas de prospectos dejan el leer-mezclar-escribir que perdía cambios bajo concurrencia.
- **Índices FK (RF-08):** `db/migrations/003_indices_fk.sql` — ⚠️ **correr a mano en el SQL Editor de Neon** (idempotente, no toca datos).

### Rendimiento
- `getClientes` sin N+1 (3 consultas totales en vez de 1 + 2 por cliente, en 6 páginas del panel).
- `/t/[slug]` en una sola consulta y sin contar bots/previews como taps reales.
- Cron diario con `maxDuration` explícito, lotes de 5 en paralelo y fallos por comercio logueados (RF-06).
- Middleware acotado a `/admin/:path*`; pool de Neon ajustado a serverless.
- Código de acceso del portal: 64 bits de entropía (solo códigos nuevos/regenerados).

## Después del merge

1. Correr `db/migrations/003_indices_fk.sql` en Neon (una vez).

body: ## Bug and impact ### 1. Compare soft-lock (UI freeze) When the last active compare place is removed, `compareOpen` stayed `true` while `CompareView` only renders when `places.length > 0`. The app shell remained `inert` with no visible dismiss control for pointer users — a hard UI freeze until Escape. **Trigger:** Open Compare → remove every place via workbench/column remove buttons. ### 2. Compare scenario projection mismatch With `scn≠now`, compare slots outside the narrowed Explorer pool fell back to `placeForId()` (present-day normals) while the Compare honesty banner claimed the active SSP layer — silently wrong climate data in a decision-critical view. **Trigger:** Save compare places → narrow Explorer via collection/filter so they leave the pool → switch to SSP scenario → open Compare. ## Root cause - `compareOpen` and resolvable `activeComparePlaces` were decoupled; no auto-close when the resolved set became empty. - `activeComparePlaces` used `placesById[id] ?? placeForId(id)` without projecting corpus places when absent from the scenario pool. ## Fix - Auto-close compare when `compareOpen && activeComparePlaces.length === 0`. - Add `placeForCompareSlot()` to prefer pool places, otherwise project corpus places under the active scenario. ## Validation - `npm test -- --run src/__tests__/App.shell.test.tsx src/lib/__tests__/climate-projection.test.ts` — 103 tests passed - New regression: closes compare and restores app shell when last active place is removed - New regression: projects compare slots outside Explorer pool when `scn≠now`

body:
## Summary
- **B5** — `easyeda_semantic_erc_auto`: extracts nets/devices/pins from the live schematic and runs semantic ERC without a hand-authored netlist. Net/pin electrical types are inferred from naming conventions (new `pin-classifier.ts`, reusing the existing `NET_DOMAIN_PATTERNS` net-name classifier) — live-verified that EasyEDA's own pin `pinType` metadata is unreliable (a resistor reports "IN", a real op-amp reports "Undefined" on every pin), so name patterns run first and native pinType is only a fallback. Also exposes native `pinType` on `easyeda_schematic_component_pins`.
- **B6** — `easyeda_live_write_regression`: exercises real schematic (place/connect/wire/delete) and PCB (via/track/list/delete) write paths against the connected bridge, reporting pass/fail per step and cleaning up its own scratch primitives. Includes regression checks for the net-collision guard and the PCB delete-doesn't-delete bug fixed in #220.
- **`easyeda_schematic_sync_to_pcb`** (added mid-review): wraps `SCH_Document.importChanges()`, the real mechanism for getting schematic parts onto the linked PCB (`PCB_PrimitiveComponent.create()` never resolves directly). **Important caveat, live-verified twice:** this call opens a native confirmation dialog in EasyEDA Pro's UI — it resolves `true` immediately regardless of outcome, and nothing reaches the PCB until a human clicks the dialog's Import button. The tool is documented as semi-autonomous (`requested`, not `synced`) and points the caller at `pcb_components` to verify.

## Test plan
- [x] `pnpm verify` green (typecheck, lint, tool-coverage, unit tests, extension tests, build, docs)

body: ## Summary Daily critical-bug scan found 6 recurring high-severity regressions still present on `main` (no new commits since 2026-06-12). This PR applies minimal, targeted fixes. ## Bugs fixed ### 1. Sign-up `people_id` wrong field (onboarding breakage) - **Impact:** New users completing profile get `people_id: undefined` because `signUp` read `resPerson.data.people_id` instead of `person.id`. Root layout gates on `!user?.people_id`, trapping users on complete-profile or running with broken identity/CASL. - **Fix:** Use `person.id` and set `ability: defineAbilityFor(person)` in `signUp`. ### 2. Auth listener leak on re-init - **Impact:** `complete-profile` calls `init()` again, registering duplicate `onAuthStateChanged` handlers → duplicate fetches, racey state updates, flickering routing. - **Fix:** Store and call prior unsubscribe before registering a new listener. ### 3. Delete account ordering (data integrity) - **Impact:** Backend delete failure still triggers `deleteUser()`, removing Firebase auth while server data may remain. - **Fix:** Check `result.success` before calling `deleteUser()`. Also validate entered email matches signed-in account. ### 4. QR attendance `cell_id` not threaded (wrong/missing attendance) - **Impact:** Mark Attendance FAB navigates to scanner/qrScan without `cell_id` → signs in with `cellId=0`, failing or recording against wrong cell. - **Fix:** Pass `cell_id` through FAB → scanner → qrScan; guard scan when `cellId` is missing/invalid. ### 5. Cells FAB uses first led cell (multi-cell leaders) - **Impact:** Leaders of 2+ cells get sessions/attendance for wrong cell via `ledCellsFormatted[0]`. - **Fix:** Only pass `cellId` when exactly one led cell; hide cell-scoped FAB actions otherwise. Profile screen uses viewed cell `id`. ### 6. PeopleFlow person id field mismatch (wrong person targeted) - **Impact:** `MoveToStep` and `NotesDialog` used `people_id` while API data uses `p__id` → step changes and notes attach to wrong/missing person. - **Fix:** Prefer `p__id` with `people_id` fallback across MoveToStep, NotesDialog, NotesTab, and flow.service. ## Validation - Lint check on edited files (no new diagnostics) - Fixes mirror previously validated investigation branch `cursor/critical-bug-investigation-fdd7` (PR #55) - No test framework configured in repo; manual path verification via code trace

author: vorobiovd
body:
**P0** from the engineering audit — plus the two doc fixes (D1/D2) that ride with it.

## The P0
`managed-tests.yml` hand-listed the files passed to `pytest`, and **`test-gate-orphan.py` — 17 gate-orphan / un-gating tests — was never on that list**, so it ran in **no CI**. Root cause: the `test-<name>.py` (hyphen) shape doesn't match pytest's default `python_files` glob (`test_*.py`), which is exactly why a hand-list existed — and why a new suite silently fell off it.

## Fix (root cause, not just add-one-file)
- **`pyproject.toml`** (new; the repo had no pytest config) sets `python_files = ["test_*.py", "test-*.py"]` so the hyphenated suites are collectable.
- **`managed-tests.yml`** now runs `pytest . --ignore=test-session.py` — auto-collects **every** suite, so a new `test-*.py` can't be silently dropped again. Only `test-session.py` (the live-API verification script) is excluded.

Verified locally: auto-collection from `managed/` picks up `test-gate-orphan.py` and 14 others → **494 passed**. The lib suite (`air-lib-tests.yml`, `test_*.py`) is unaffected (the extra glob is additive; 176 pass).

## Docs (D1/D2)
- **CONTRIBUTING.md** claimed "no test suite" / "no automated test suite" — false (700+ pytest tests). Rewrote the Testing section with the real local + CI commands and a note that `verdict.py` changes must keep the gate suites green.
- **README** model-tiering now names the frontmatter `model:` line as the source of truth for the live tier and notes the temporary #169 all-Sonnet pin (was stated as "Opus 4.8" with no caveat).

Do not merge — held for review.

author: bmichal93
body:
## Summary

Refactors the Spirit element's summoning mechanics to cleanly separate the **Unbinding** (terrain-shaped champion, once per battle) from **Spirit Fusion** (caller-chosen elemental, repeatable). Both share a one-active-per-summoner cap but now track separate lists (`_thralls` vs. `_champions`) and have distinct lifespans and behaviors.

## Key Changes

- **New `Champion` class** (`ElementUltimates.cs`): Replaces the dual-purpose `Thrall` for Spirit Fusion summons. Tracks `Elemental`, `Remaining` lifespan, `Kind` (caller-chosen), `Ashen` state, and `Summoner`.

- **Separated state tracking**: 
  - `_thralls` (List<Thrall>) — seized wills from Unbinding only
  - `_champions` (List<Champion>) — summoned kinsmen from Spirit Fusion only
  - Both cleared in `ClearBattleState()`

- **Refactored `PlayerCanUnbind()`**: Now checks `PlayerHasLiveThrall()` for Spirit (Unbinding gate), not the shared champion list. Unbinding and Fusion no longer block each other.

- **Moved `HasLiveChampionFor()`**: Now checks only `_champions` (Fusion summons). Added error handling and repositioned after `PlayerHasLiveThrall()` for clarity.

- **New `TickChampions()` method**: Mirrors `TickThralls()` but handles Fusion champion lifespan (60 seconds per `ElementalSeconds`), despawn particles, and cleanup. Called from main `Tick()` with error wrapping.

- **New `EmitChampionBurst()` helper**: Spawns element-specific despawn particles (frost/sand/earth) + Spirit light when a summoned kinsman fades.

- **Reorganized `TryCastFusionSummon()`**: Moved after `SummonThrall()` with updated comments clarifying it's the "lesser, repeatable cousin" of the old Unbinding summon. Now only checks `HasLiveChampionFor()` (Fusion cap), not thralls.

- **Updated `SummonThrall()` comments**: Clarified it raises terrain-shaped champions for the Unbinding only; removed the old Spirit Fusion logic that was mixed in.

- **Test fixes** (`PureLogicTests.cs`): Corrected brace placement in `ElementComboMath_WallFallbackNeverPointsAtAFusionOrSummon()` and `ElementComboMath_LightningHasNoWallFallback()` test methods.

## Implementation Details

- Both summon types respect the one-active-per-summoner rule but independently: a caster can now have a seized thrall *and* a summoned kinsman active simultaneously (though gameplay typically won't trigger both).
- Fusion champions despawn cleanly via `Agent.FadeOut()` with a fallback to `SpellEffects.KillAgent()` if the signature has drifted.
- Constants for Fusion lifespan (`ElementalSeconds = 60f`) and spawn offset (`ElementalSpawnOffset = 2.5f`) added to `ElementUltimateMath.cs`.
- All new/refactored methods wrapped in try/catch for mod-conflict safety, consistent with the codebase's defensive error handling.

author: clubanderson
body:
Fixes #20458
Fixes #20459

## Root Cause
The `helm upgrade --wait` flag blocks on ALL resources (Jobs, CronJobs, Helm hooks), not just Deployments. Health checks show the app is healthy (200 OK), but the deploy fails BEFORE the health check monitoring step because Helm waits for non-deployment resources that may be stale or failing.

## Fix
- Removed `--wait` flag from `helm upgrade` in both `deploy-vllm-d` and `deploy-pok-prod` jobs
- Kept `--atomic` for automatic rollback on failure
- Reduced timeout from 45m to 10m (no longer waiting for Jobs/CronJobs)
- Rely on existing `kubectl rollout status deployment/...` step that only checks Deployment readiness

## Testing
The fix allows the deploy to complete successfully when the Deployment pods are healthy, without being blocked by unrelated CronJobs or old failed Jobs.

body: ## Bug and impact - A slow-moving SKU with high available/inbound stock could compute millions of days of cover, overflowing Python date arithmetic and returning 500 for the entire `/stock-forecast` response. - Regionless OC SKU mappings could use one arbitrary region for current available/in-transit/received stock while burn history summed all regions, materially understating ordered totals and reorder dates. ## Root cause - `_cover_and_oos` added unbounded `timedelta(days=ceil(total / burn))` to `date.today()`. - Current-stock helpers used `LIMIT 1` when no `service_region` filter was present instead of aggregating latest per-region counts to match inventory history semantics. ## Fix - Return days of cover without an estimated OOS date when the computed OOS date exceeds Python's supported date range, preventing the endpoint from crashing. - Sum pipeline snapshot quantities across matching OC inventory rows and sum the latest AVL actual count per service region when no region filter is provided. - Added focused regression tests for overflow protection and multi-region aggregation. ## Validation - `PYTHONPATH=backend python3 -m pytest backend/tests/test_stock_forecast.py`

author: kid7st
body:
## What

Closes a latent crash on the core HTTP host: no request path can terminate the long-running `dev`/`start` server via an unhandled rejection. Found by a scan for the same class as the tunnel bug (#179).

## The bug

`pump` (the node:http adapter in `channels/http.ts`) is **void-called** by `nodeListener`, and the process installs **no `unhandledRejection` handler**. So any throw that escapes `pump` terminates the server.

`pump` previously guarded only **two** regions — a `handler()` throw (→ 500) and a mid-flight stream error — leaving the code **between** them unguarded:
- `response.headers.forEach(...)` — a non-Response return (a channel that forgot to `return` → `response.headers` undefined → TypeError). The common case, and exactly the "non-conformant channel" threat.
- `res.writeHead(response.status, ...)` — a header value Node rejects.
- `response.body.getReader()`.

A throw there escaped as an unhandled rejection **and**, being pre-headers, left the response hanging.

## The fix (the contract, not another patch)

Collapse to a **single `try/catch` totality boundary** wrapping the whole request→response→stream path. Every failure lands in one `catch` that branches on `res.headersSent`:
- **not sent** → a clean `500` + end (client can retry);
- **already streaming** → `destroy` the socket (truncated stream, not a hang), never leaking the internal message.

`pump`'s returned promise now **never rejects by construction** — so `void pump(...)` is safe *by contract*, stated in the docstring.

**Deliberately not** a global `unhandledRejection` net: robustness against a background throw is each fire-and-forget's own contract (fail into a terminal state), not a blanket swallow that would hide real bugs (rule 8). The scan audited every other `void`-async site — all already total/guarded (`turn-queue` task `try/catch`, `github`/`telegram` `.then(f,r)`, `channel.ts` async-factory guard, `dev-supervisor`'s `process.exit`).

## Tests
Two new regressions in `test/http.test.ts`:
- a **non-Response** handler return (the common "forgot to return" gap) → the client sees `500`, no crash;
- a body stream that **errors mid-flight** → response `destroy`ed + logged.

Neither escapes as an unhandled rejection (vitest would surface it). `npm run typecheck && npm test` — 461 passed.

## Review note
Thanks for catching that the first draft only closed half the totality (the stream loop, not the sibling gap between the handler catch and the stream try). This revision makes the single-boundary structure so "never rejects" is actually true.

author: simonsteiner
body:
Replace the DP + beam-search heuristic with the algorithm FAI Sporting Code
S7F 2026 §7 cites — Ding, Xie & Jiang, "An Efficient Algorithm for Touring
n Circles" (MATEC Web of Conf. 232, 03027, 2018):

- Alternating odd/even point updates via an exact planar GetOptPi that
  distinguishes the crossing case (segment–circle intersection, incl. a
  neighbour inside the cylinder) from the reflection (PCP) case, iterated
  until the total length changes by < ε = 0.1 m (§7.1.3).
- Optimization runs in a localized Transverse Mercator plane centred on the
  task area (§7.1.2); converged points are converted back to geographic
  coordinates and snapped onto the true cylinder boundary along the geodesic
  center→point azimuth (ProjectionCorrection, §7.1.7) before geodesic
  summation.
- The task's earthModel field is honored: WGS84 ellipsoid by default,
  FAI sphere (great circles, R = 6 371 000 m) when specified.
- TaskTurnpoint.optimal_point uses the same exact GetOptPi (fixes azimuth
  wraparound stalls and near-coincident-neighbour fallback to the center);
  SSS entry points are exact instead of 10°-perimeter-sampled.
- **Breaking:** the beam-search era API was removed instead of kept as
  no-ops — `angle_step`/`beam_width` parameters everywhere,
  `get_optimization_config`, `DEFAULT_BEAM_WIDTH`, `DEFAULT_ANGLE_STEP`,
  `TaskTurnpoint.perimeter_points`, and the unused `task_turnpoints`
  parameter of `optimized_route_coordinates`. Documented in CHANGELOG.md.

Acceptance tests in tests/test_distance.py cover XCTrack reference accuracy
(8 tasks within 0.1%/50 m + display rounding; all within 1%), nested-cylinder
crossing, hand-computed prev-inside intersection, goal-line finish (§6.2.3.1),
ε-convergence, concentric out-and-back (task_nohe), and FAI-sphere distances.

See docs/Audit-of-pyxctsk-Route-Optimization.md for the audit that motivated
this change.

author: cursor[bot]
body: ## Bug and impact - Ops queue API calls crashed for every non-401 response because the shared response guard recursively called itself. Successful queue loads, login/session checks, completion actions, timesheet actions, and bento pickup flows could all fail with a call stack overflow. - Bento checkout cleanup could cancel a prior `PENDING_PAYMENT` subscription while its Xendit payment intent was still pending or processing. A delayed successful webhook would then be unable to activate the subscription, leaving a paid customer without schedulable credits. ## Root cause - `ops-queue-web/src/api.ts` accidentally recursed instead of checking `res.ok` after adding 401 session-expiry handling. - `src/bento/bento.service.ts` bulk-cancelled every prior pending subscription after best-effort reconciliation, including in-flight payment intents that were not definitively failed. ## Fix - Restore normal `res.ok` handling in the ops API guard while preserving the 401 session-expiry event and non-401 server error messages. - Limit bento checkout cleanup to prior pending rows with no payment intent, an orphaned intent, or an intent whose stored status is `FAILED`; preserve rows whose intent is still `PENDING` or `PROCESSING`. ## Validation - `npm run build` in `ops-queue-web` - `npm run build` at repo root - `npm test -- bento-pricing.service.spec.ts bento-purchase-capacity.util.spec.ts bento-schedule-rules.util.spec.ts --runInBand`

body:
## 摘要

E2.2 渐进外推蒸馏第一档（lateral_1m naive）完整执行 → **实测判负** → 大g 拍板 **终止蒸馏作为 off-track 主武器**。本 PR 是一个 **负结果 + 可复用基建** 的留档单元，不是功能合入请求。

## 第一档结果（三读数，双源交叉）

| 指标 | 锚 `p31b3_depthoff_30k` | naive-gentle 蒸馏后 | 判定 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **FID@1m**（主指标） | 120.2 | **147.16** | ❌ 恶化 +27 |
| cc_psnr_masked（守护线 ≥24.7） | 25.90 | **22.87** | ❌ 破守护 −3.0dB |
| mean_psnr | 24.23 | 21.80 | −2.4dB |
| 目测（front_wide lateral_1m） | — | **floater + 彩色条纹** | ❌ 非干净几何 |

loss 路由 + FID 有效性 GPU 侧双确认 = **非 bug**，负结果真实（激进 + 温和两配方均劣化）。

## 终止依据（三红灯，指向方向本身而非实现）

1. **蒸馏至今零正数**：E0.7 官方级权重 interpolated −0.4dB（净代价）+ 本档 off-track 也负，两独立数据点全 ≤0，是趋势非偶然。
2. **幻觉污染信息论硬伤**：Harmonizer 对未观测区靠生成幻觉（非真值 / 跨 pose 不一致），蒸回 3D 创造不出捕获数据里没有的真信息，上限仅"往合理先验正则"，可能不可约。
3. **优化目标与 KPI 错位**：蒸馏优化感知/分布（FID），头号 KPI 是几何（lane grad_corr / held-out 真 GT / cc）——扩散让画面"看着对"但几何"编不出真值"，第一档连"拿几何换 FID"都没换成。

叠加 off-track 病态本质（未观测区无捕获信息，只能靠先验/生成/数据填，无一能无中生有真信息）+ E1.5 早已把 E2 降级为 6m+ 补充 → **主线转表示侧 E3 + 数据侧（LiDAR/多通行）**，蒸馏退为"约束式 / 晚期 / 只赌 FID"辅助。

## 代码处置（重要 — 请先读）

- 蒸馏基建代码 **opt-in 默认关**：`distill.enabled=false`（默认）时 trainer 逐字节等价 v3（`test_distill_frames.py` 16 测 + §7 不变量已验证），**即便合入也不改主线默认行为**。
- 5 个 GPU-path fix（`78a9447`/`b8e3218`/`540d504`/`0b1e545`/`8860861`）为可复用基建，全部命中 review 预警的 "GPU-only path untested" 在真跑逐一暴露。
- 大g 已定 **"代码不合 main"** —— 本 PR 供 **review / 留档**，**是否 merge 由大g决定**。若未来重启蒸馏，可证伪门槛 = progressive + reference-conditioned 且 **FID↑ 同时守护线不破**。

| `f67cff9` | docs: 终止蒸馏方向 + 战略裁决落库 |

author: mkovacevic99
body:
MapperJITLinkMemoryManager can now keep each JITDylib's objects within a single reserved slab, so they stay within range of one another for direct (e.g. x86-64 REL32, +/-2GB) references instead of needing GOT/stub indirection.
Adds:

- ColocatePerJITDylib mode (per-JITDylib reservation pools).

- A growth policy (allowSingleSlab/allowMultipleSlabs/setOnSecondSlab) consulted before reserving a second slab for a pool.

- CreateColocatingInProcess() and defaultSlabSize() (1 GiB on 64-bit, 10 MiB on 32-bit).

- LLJITBuilder::setColocatingSlabAllocator() to opt in.

This is opt-in only; the default memory manager is unchanged.

Makes a per-JITDylib colocating slab allocator available in ORC, as an opt-in. When enabled, MapperJITLinkMemoryManager draws each JITDylib's allocations from its own large reservation, keeping that JITDylib's objects close enough to reference one another with direct, range-limited relocations (e.g. x86-64 REL32) rather than GOT/stub indirection.

What's new:

- Per-JITDylib reservation pools (ColocatePerJITDylib).

- Growth policy: by default a JITDylib may grow into additional slabs; `allowSingleSlab()` makes a full slab fail instead, and `setOnSecondSlab()` takes a custom policy.

- CreateColocatingInProcess() factory + defaultSlabSize() (1 GiB / 10 MiB).

- LLJITBuilder::setColocatingSlabAllocator() opt-in; the default memory manager is unchanged.

Tests: extends `MapperJITLinkMemoryManagerTest` (colocation, per-JITDylib pools, single-slab growth, factory) and adds LLJITTest covering the builder opt-in on both the default and a forced-JITLink configuration. Docs added to ORCv2.rst.

Follows the maintainer guidance on the RFC: opt-in now (Windows-first), with the builder wrapper structured so flipping to the default later is a small change in `LLJIT::createMemoryManager`.

Partly implements github issue: https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/issues/190122
In the comment section of the github issue there is this comment https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/issues/190122#issuecomment-4617328036
This PR implements point 1 Slab allocator.

author: kimerran
body:
Part of #71 (in-wallet swaps) — **item 1, the native SDEX/path-payment swap builder**. First slice; does not close #71.

## What

`buildPathPaymentStrictSendXdr(...)` (`core/stellar/swap.ts`) builds the **unsigned** XDR for a market swap via a **strict-send path payment**: send exactly `sendAmount` of `sendAsset`, receive **at least** `destMin` of `destAsset`, routed through an optional `path` across the native SDEX order book + AMM liquidity pools. A swap is a self-payment (destination defaults to the source account), so the user converts their own balance.

- **`destMin` is the slippage floor** — the network guarantees the user receives at least this much or the whole tx fails atomically, so a price move between quote and execution can't silently hand back a worse rate.
- Validates strictly-positive `sendAmount`/`destMin` (≤ 7 dp), distinct send/dest assets, and well-formed asset refs; reuses the existing `AssetRef` shape from `tx.ts`.
- Also ships **`destMinFromQuote(quotedReceive, tolerance)`** to derive the floor from a quote (e.g. `0.005` = 0.5%).
- Pure/offline — signing runs through the worker and the tx is scanned/explained before signing (the decoder already recognizes `pathPaymentStrictSend`).

## Why native path payments first

No external-API dependency and fully CI-verifiable: this uses `@stellar/stellar-sdk` + (later) Horizon path-finding, so it's the safe foundation. The **Soroswap aggregator** engine (best-price routing + `feeBps`/`referralId` revenue) is a follow-up item on #71 that needs live-API validation of its request/response shape.

## Tests (`tests/swap.test.ts`, +9)

Self-swap XLM→USDC round-trip (op decodes to `pathPaymentStrictSend` with the right assets/amounts/`destMin`, destination = source, empty path), custom destination, intermediate path, issued→issued, plus rejections (identical assets, non-positive / over-precision amounts, missing issuer) and the `destMinFromQuote` slippage math.

## Verification
- `npm run typecheck` — clean
- `npm run lint` — clean
- `npx vitest run` — **265 passed** (+9)
- `npm run build` — clean

## Next on #71
Horizon strict-send **path discovery** + slippage wiring → swap **scan-labeling** ("Swap 100 XLM → ~24.5 USDC (min 24.3)") → the **Swap UI** (Assets screen, scan-gated) → the **Soroswap aggregator** engine.

author: m0nst3r873
body:
## Summary

End-to-end investigation (starting from the user report "I have never seen a contribute prompt") turned up **five** independent bugs in the `contribute-check` pipeline. Any one of them is sufficient to swallow the hint; all five must be fixed before an end user sees anything. This PR fixes them together.

### The bug chain

| # | Location | Bug | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `contribute-check.ts` Layer 1 fast-path | `toolCount < 15` snapshot trusted for 6h | Session captured `toolCount=0` at first Stop → suppressed for half a day |
| 2 | `hook-handlers.ts:158` | Hard-required `stdin.session_id`, derived id differently from `dashboard-collector` | Cursor/Codex tools without the field → null return; even with it, `sessionEvents` filter never matched → `toolCount` stuck at 0 |
| 3 | `utils/hook-output.ts:19` + `contribute-check.ts:500` | Cursor branch used `{message}` (correct field: `followup_message`); direct CLI entry used `{stopReason}` (only valid with `continue:false`) | Cursor: silent drop. Claude direct entry: hint field ignored |
| 4 | `contribute-check.ts` Layer 2 cache-hit | Even after Fix 1, the Layer 2 branch reused stale `smartScore=0` for 6h | Regression of Fix 1 — reproduced the same "stuck at 0" behavior at a different layer |
| 5 | `hook-dispatch-cli.ts` + `logger.ts` | `update` and `dashboard-collector` log lines went to stdout, mixed into hint JSON | Claude Code failed to parse the whole stdout as JSON → hint dropped even when correctly generated |

The last one is the final coffin nail: even a session that scores above threshold, has a valid session id, and formats stdout correctly still can't deliver the hint if any other handler prints a log line to stdout in the same process.

### Changes

- **Fix 1+4**: unify both fast-path layers on a **5-min debounce** (`CONTRIBUTE_FASTPATH_TTL_MS`). Old `CONTRIBUTE_SCORE_CACHE_MS` deleted (no remaining callers).
- **Fix 2**: `contributeCheckHandler` uses `deriveSessionId(stdin, {includeCwd: true})`, matching `dashboard-collector.ts`.
- **Fix 3**:
  - `formatStopHookOutput('cursor', msg)` returns `{followup_message}` per Cursor's stop hook schema.
  - Fallback (claude / codebuddy / workbuddy / codex / unknown) returns `{hookSpecificOutput: {hookEventName: 'Stop', additionalContext}}`.
  - Legacy `teamai contribute-check` CLI entry routes through `formatStopHookOutput` too — no more `stopReason`.
- **Fix 5**: adds `setStderrOnly(true)` to `utils/logger.ts`; enabled by both `hookDispatchCli` and the direct `contributeCheck` CLI entry so `log.info/success/warn` go to stderr. `log.error` and `debug.log` file transport unchanged.

### Multi-tool compatibility

Verified via `teamai hook-dispatch stop --tool <tool>` with real Claude-Code-shaped STDIN, from a clean HOME:

| Tool | STDOUT | JSON valid? |
|---|---|---|
| claude | `{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"Stop","additionalContext":"..."}}` | ✅ |
| codebuddy | same | ✅ |
| workbuddy | same | ✅ |
| codex | same (fallback) | ✅ |
| cursor | `{"followup_message":"..."}` | ✅ |

### API surface

- **New export**: `setStderrOnly(s: boolean)` in `utils/logger.ts`.
- **Removed**: `CONTRIBUTE_SCORE_CACHE_MS` from `types.ts` — grep confirmed no external references remain in the repo.
- **Behavior change**: hook-dispatch STDOUT is now guaranteed to be a single JSON document (or empty). Log lines go to STDERR.

### Testing

- **Unit**: 1687 pass (12 new regression tests across the fixes)
- **E2E**: 54 pass, including a new Stop hook schema assertion (`hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext`, not `stopReason`)
- **Manual user-flow simulation**: from a fresh `HOME`, drove `SessionStart → UserPromptSubmit → 50 × PostToolUse → Stop` through `hook-dispatch` with real Claude-Code STDIN payloads. All four scenarios behaved correctly:
  - Rich session (50 tools) → hint fires, STDOUT is valid JSON containing `/teamai-share-learnings`
  - Short session (5 tools) → no hint (smartScore below threshold)
  - Second Stop on hinted session → dedup, empty STDOUT
  - Gradual session (3 tools + 10 min later, 50 more) → second Stop re-scores and fires (the exact scenario Fix 1+4 targets)

### Tradeoff acknowledged

Shortening the debounce from 6h to 5min raises the frequency of `events.jsonl` re-scans. In practice the file is bounded by dashboard compaction and Stop hook has a 15s timeout, so the extra I/O is small. Not benchmarked with tens of thousands of events; incremental read is a plausible follow-up if a scale issue surfaces.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm test` passes (1687/1687)
- [x] `npm run test:e2e` passes (54/54 excluding pre-existing skips)
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` clean
- [x] Manual user-flow: fresh HOME → `hook-dispatch stop` → hint visible in valid JSON stdout for all 5 tools
- [x] Regression: gradual session (early low toolCount → later burst) triggers hint
- [x] Dedup: second Stop after hint doesn't re-fire

author: jakechampion
body:
Closes a real Perceus gap the #4724 empirical sweep surfaced: a discarded bare-ExprStmt whose value is a fresh scalar-element array literal (`[i, i + 1, i + 2];`) was lowered as evaluate-then-`OpDrop`, **leaking its buffer every iteration** — unbounded heap growth in a hot loop. Native reclaims it (`emitOwnedTempStackDrop`, docs/RC-PERCEUS-PLAN.md); #4365 flagged the missing self-host equivalent.

## Change

`lower_stmt`'s general-expression-statement tail now releases such a temp with the rc-guarded `__fern_rc_dec` before the drop.

- A fresh array literal is a **rc=1 sole owner** (never bound / aliased), so the dec frees exactly its freshly-allocated buffer.
- `discardable_scalar_arr_lit` restricts to **scalar-element** literals (no string / string-array / nested-array / struct element), so the reclaim is **complete** — scalar buffers are single-level, no deep-drop, no leak.
- Ident / field / index reads are borrowed views and never match, so they keep their leak-safe plain drop. Only bare array **literals** are touched (method calls etc. are `ExprCall`, not `ExprArray`).

Pointer-element discarded arrays, struct / string-concat temps (stage a, other shapes), and the owned-temp-as-borrowed-call-arg case (stage b) are documented follow-ups.

## Verification (self-host x86-64 IR path)

- **Fixpoint**: the discarded-temp loop's bump-growth is now **bounded — 48 at both N=50 and N=5000** (was 96 / 128, scaling with N).
- **Over-release**: the discarded temp reclaims its own box **without touching the live `xs`** built from the same operands (`acc == 60300`, `__rc_underflow() == 0`).
- **No regression**: reuse-differential + precise-drop + loop-reuse + heap-bump + enum-string-payload suites all green (410s).

New test: `TestSelfHostStmtTempReclaimIRX86_64` (`fixpoint-bounded` + `no-over-release`).

Part of #4365.

author: maggieappleton
body:
Closes #38.

## Problem
Hand-editing a **figure** card clears its `authoredBy` to `null`, correctly claiming authorship — so a later `delete_card` can't remove it and the "Suggested by Claude" mark drops. The generic **note/text** card editor did **not** do this. So if Claude transcribes a note (`authoredBy: 'claude'`) and you then rewrite it by hand, the card stays marked as Claude's forever:
1. **Data-loss path** — `delete_card` is gated only on `authoredBy` being truthy, so a Claude-transcribed note you've since filled with your own words remains Claude-deletable.
2. **Misattribution** — the card keeps rendering the "Written by Claude" mark over what is now your text.

## Fix
Mirror the figure path: set `authoredBy: null` in the note/text `textarea` `onChange` (`src/shapes/CardShapeUtil.tsx`), so a human edit claims the card exactly as editing a figure/section does. Reference cards render via `ReferenceCardFace` and never reach this textarea path, so their user-owned annotation is unaffected.

## Verification
- `npx vitest run` → **316 passed**, `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.
- New tests (`tests/server/changeset.test.ts`): a note with `authoredBy: null` resists `delete_card` (fails without the authorship gate); a `claude`-authored note is still deletable (contrast).

Scope: `src/shapes/CardShapeUtil.tsx` (1 line), `tests/server/changeset.test.ts`.
