body:
## Summary

Après PR #14 (tunnel B2C public créant une réservation `pending`), le cycle de traitement agence s'arrêtait. Cette PR construit le **cycle complet post-réservation** côté back-office.

Base de cette PR : la branche de PR #14 (`devin/1783252198-omra-b2c-booking`), pour que le diff ne montre que le travail post-booking.

### Phase 1 — Liste `/admin/omra/reservations`
- Recherche (référence, client, email, téléphone, programme), filtres (statut via onglets, programme, plage départ, plage réservation), tri (création/départ/montant/référence), pagination (20/page).
- Colonnes : référence, client+email, téléphone, programme, départ, pèlerins, montant, statut, créée le, actions.
- `loading.tsx` (skeleton anti double-clic).

### Phase 2 — Détail `/admin/omra/reservations/[id]`
- Infos réservation (réf, programme, statut, dates, montant, acompte), liste pèlerins (nom, sexe, passeport, expiration, nationalité, visa), historique (timeline depuis `audit_events`), fiche client.

### Phase 3 — Actions métier (transactions atomiques + `FOR UPDATE`)
`lib/omra/reservation-actions.ts` :
- `confirmOmraReservation` : `pending → confirmed`, `confirmed_at`, stock `reserved → confirmed`, audit + notif.
- `cancelOmraReservation(reason?)` : `→ cancelled`, `cancelled_at`, **stock restauré** (`reserved_count -= pèlerins`, `available_count += pèlerins`), audit + notif + email client.
- `completeOmraReservation` : `confirmed → completed`.
- `addOmraReservationNote` : événement d'historique.

```
tx: lockReservation (FOR UPDATE) → update statut → lockAllotment (FOR UPDATE) → ajuste stock → auditEvents → queueInAppNotification
post-commit: dispatchNotification (email best-effort)
```

### Phase 4 — Notifications (`lib/notifications/dispatch.ts`)
Architecture extensible multi-canal (in_app / email / SMS / WhatsApp) :
- `queueInAppNotification(tx, …)` — sûr dans une transaction (aucune I/O).
- `dispatchNotification(…)` — sortant best-effort après commit (email via Resend si `RESEND_API_KEY` configuré).
- À la création (tunnel B2C) : audit + notif admin. Badge compteur back-office = réservations `pending` (auto-décrémenté à la confirmation/annulation).

### Phase 5 — Dashboard KPIs
Widget Omra (`components/admin/omra-kpi-widget.tsx`) : réservations aujourd'hui, en attente, confirmées, chiffre d'affaires (confirmées), taux de conversion, places restantes.

### RBAC
`requireOmraAgent()` — `super_admin` / `manager` / `agent_resa` (écriture) ; nav item + badge ajoutés à `admin-shell`.

## DB Changes
- Nouvelle table `notifications` (in_app + sortant, statut/canal/entité). Migration idempotente `drizzle/manual/0011_notifications_and_reservation_timestamps.sql` (+ garde `confirmed_at` / `cancelled_at`).

## Tests
- `pnpm test` : 86/86.
- `tsc` / `eslint` : propres sur les fichiers de cette PR (les erreurs restantes sont pré-existantes sur `main` : `lib/repositories/*`, `wallet-service`, `validations`).
- `next build` : OK, routes `/admin/omra/reservations` et `/admin/omra/reservations/[id]` générées.
- E2E (create→admin, confirm, cancel+stock, concurrence, cas limites) : à exécuter en test mode avec enregistrement.

## Summary

Closes #674.

The daemon accumulated 40+ open `palace.db` file descriptors because 13 `PendingMessageStore` methods each opened a fresh `Connection::open` per call. Under WAL mode these connections don't immediately release fds, causing SQLITE_BUSY timeouts that intermittently broke `mcp_context`, `mcp_brief`, and CLI CRUD operations.

## Changes

Generalized the `ClaimConnectionCache` pattern from #672 to all `PendingMessageStore` paths:

- **`ConnectionCache`** (renamed from `ClaimConnectionCache`) now holds three lazily-initialized cached connections:
  - `claim_writer` — 100ms busy timeout (for claim_next, same as #672)
  - `writer` — 30s busy timeout (for enqueue, confirm, complete, mark_failed, release_claim, refresh_heartbeat, reclaim_stale, retry/archive)
  - `reader` — query_only (for stats, preview_failed_action)

- All 13 `self.open_connection()` / `self.open_connection_with_busy_timeout()` call sites replaced with `self.with_connection(|conn| { ... })` or `self.with_query_connection(|conn| { ... })`

- `fork_claim_connection_cache()` → `fork_connection_cache()` (updated in daemon.rs and worker.rs)

- New test `confirm_and_enqueue_reuse_cached_writer_connection` verifies writer connection reuse

body:
- For #11705 relates to #13159

## What does this change?

Reimplements the upgrade to nextjs-auth0 to v4, that [was reverted ](https://github.com/wellcomecollection/wellcomecollection.org/pull/13231) and then fixes the issue that was breaking the identity app


### Problem

The kiosk navigation history feature (commit b36e1d9de7) causes the identity app to fail when using nextjs-auth0 v4

Error: Invariant: AsyncLocalStorage accessed in runtime

This happens even though the identity app doesn't use kiosk mode.

The above commit added a HistoryProvider inside KioskProvider and while the latter is conditionally rendered (only when kiosk cookie exists), when Next.js compiles the identity app, it still loads all imported modules including HistoryProvider which uses browser APIs that conflict with how Next.js sets up AsyncLocalStorage for middleware.

### Solution

This PR moves the HistoryProvider out of KioskContext and dynamically imports it in _app.tsx

Identity: No kiosk cookie so the wrapper function never runs and the HistoryProvider is never imported
Content (kiosk mode): Has kiosk cookie so the wrapper runs and the HistoryProvider is dynamically loaded client-side

## How to test

- run the identity app, check you can log in
- run the content app with T&R [kiosk mode](https://dash.wellcomecollection.org/toggles/#modes)
- visit the [T&R landing page](https://www-dev.wellcomecollection.org/exhibitions/tenderness-and-rage/explore-more)
- click around a bit and then check the prev/next navigation (left side of navigation bar) still works as expected

## Have we considered potential risks?

None really, could cause a brief layout shift on first kiosk page load.

author: huanchong-99
body:
## Problem

In the **Orchestrated Workspace** (auto-orchestration, `execution_mode == "agent_planned"`), after a workflow is generated it would sometimes stay pinned at **`running`** forever — the terminal panel showed no activity and no terminal ever entered execution. No error surfaced; the workflow just hung.

## Root cause

Terminal launch in agent-planned mode depends entirely on the orchestrator's **initial planning** LLM call producing `create_task` / `create_terminal` / `start_terminal` instructions. That planning runs **only once, at `run()` startup** (3 quick retries that only fire on a hard `call_llm` error).

If planning fails to create any task — either because `call_llm` errored on every startup attempt, or because it returned output that could not be parsed into instructions (in which case `run_initial_agent_planning_if_needed` returns `Ok` with zero tasks and the startup loop breaks) — the workflow is left **`running` with zero tasks and zero terminals**, and:

- `auto_sync_workflow_completion` early-returns for a zero-task workflow (`!workflow_planning_complete && !all_tasks_final`), so it is never marked complete **or** failed;
- `recover_stalled_terminals` / `dispatch_queued_terminals` / `auto_complete_stalled_tasks` are all no-ops with zero terminals/tasks;
- **nothing re-drives initial planning.**

Net effect: a single transient planning failure permanently bricks the workflow at `running` with no terminal and no user-visible error.

## Fix

A bounded, watchdog-driven recovery for exactly this state (`crates/services/src/services/orchestrator/agent.rs`):

- On each watchdog tick, `recover_missing_initial_plan` checks for a **running, agent-planned workflow with zero tasks** and re-attempts initial planning (first attempt immediately, subsequent attempts spaced ~30s apart, up to 5 attempts). This **self-heals the common transient failure** — the workflow proceeds to create tasks and launch terminals on a later attempt instead of hanging.
- When the budget is exhausted, the workflow is **marked `failed` with a diagnostic** and an `Error` bus event, so a persistently-broken orchestrator config surfaces a clear, retryable failure instead of an eternal silent `running`.
- No-op for any other state (tasks present → reset budget; not running / not agent-planned → skip; run-state busy → skip to avoid racing an event handler).

## Tests

Two deterministic unit tests (mock LLM, in-memory DB) in `agent::tests`:
- `recover_missing_initial_plan_fails_workflow_after_budget` — planning always errors → workflow leaves `running` and becomes `failed` after the bounded budget.
- `recover_missing_initial_plan_redrives_and_creates_task` — planning succeeds on re-drive → a task is created, the workflow stays `running`, and the recovery budget resets.

## Scope

Backend only, single file. No API/schema/type/frontend changes.

body:
## Summary

Follow-up to the GUI gap-filling validation audit (double-check found the earlier audit report was accurate for the *default* workspace shell — `rheojax-gui` with no flags — even though several items had already been closed in the legacy `--legacy` window). This PR fixes the audit's Critical/Important findings plus the highest-priority still-open gaps in the default shell, and has grown to include two full feature builds (diagnostics panel parity, app chrome) that were originally scoped as deferred follow-ups but were built and merged into this same branch instead of opening new PRs.

**Critical**
- `uv run pytest tests/gui/` segfaulted partway through, masking whatever ran after it. Root cause: an upstream FreeType/matplotlib raster-overflow bug corrupts the process heap in an earlier test; the corruption only manifests as a SIGSEGV later, inside `test_main_cli_wiring.py`'s real `main()` calls, which shared a QApplication with 500+ other tests. Fixed by running those specific tests in isolated subprocesses. Also added the missing `draw_idle()`-neutering cleanup pattern (already used by `base_arviz_widget.py`/`plot_canvas.py`) to `ResidualsPanel`/`MultiView`, which lacked it.

**Bugs**
- `y_band` (posterior credible-interval band) was dead code — nothing ever set the key `step5_visualize.py` read. Now computed in `subprocess_bayesian.py` from posterior draws.
- `bayesian_page.py`'s Advanced Options dialog computed `target_accept_prob`/`max_tree_depth` but never passed them to the sampler — silently dropped. Wired through `process_adapter.py`/`bayesian_worker.py`/`subprocess_bayesian.py` (the core NUTS kernel already supported `max_tree_depth` via `**kwargs`; only the GUI layer was missing it).
- `ModelService.predict()` mutated the caller's `model_kwargs` dict via `.pop()` — silently dropped `fitted_model_state` after the first posterior draw for stateful models (HL/DMT/HVM/VLB) whenever a caller reused the same dict across a loop of `predict()` calls (`_compute_y_band`, `bayesian_page.py`'s posterior-predictive plot).
- `ResidualsPanel`/`MultiView` only released matplotlib resources via `closeEvent()`, which never fires for widgets destroyed through Qt's parent-cascade `deleteLater()` (the common case when embedded in `VisualizeStep`/the Compare Models dialog). Wired cleanup to the `destroyed` signal instead, which fires on every teardown path.

**Feature gaps (default workspace shell)**
- Transform parameter form: `TransformState.config` stayed `{}` forever (no UI ever wrote to it). Reused the existing `ParameterFormBuilder` widget in `SlotsStep`.
- NUTS sampler settings: `num_warmup`/`num_samples`/`num_chains`/`seed` were hardcoded with no UI; added spinboxes to `step4_nuts.py`.
- Export step silently wrote to `Path.cwd()`; added a directory picker.
- Model picker was a flat list; grouped by family (reusing `fit_page.py`'s grouping), with a safety net so no model ever silently disappears if the two registry queries disagree.
- **Diagnostics panel parity**: the default wizard's Diagnostics tab covered only 6 of legacy's 8 ArviZ plot types and had no R-hat/ESS/Divergences numeric summary or credible-intervals table. Added the 2 missing plot types (trace, posterior), R-hat/ESS/Divergences labels (reusing `step4_nuts.py`'s own convergence thresholds so the labels can never disagree with the badge on the same screen), and a credible-intervals table.
- **App chrome**: the default shell had no status bar (just a static `QLabel`), no theme switching, no Preferences menu item, and no command palette — all present in the legacy shell. Added a real `StatusBar` (reused from the legacy shell as-is), Light/Dark/System theme switching with OS-scheme detection/watching and restore-on-launch/reload, a "Preferences..." menu item (opens the existing `PreferencesDialog`, reused as-is), and a `Ctrl+K` command palette listing 10 actions across file/mode/view/theme.

**Deferred** (flagged, not built): Compare Models (needs a multi-fit-per-dataset state design the workspace shell doesn't have yet) — a substantial standalone feature build, out of scope for this PR.

## Test plan
- [x] `uv run pytest tests/gui/` runs to completion (no crash; remaining failures are the same pre-existing FreeType/MemoryError host-environment issues, now consistently skip-guarded across the affected visual-regression tests rather than failing)
- [x] `uv run pytest tests/gui/workspace/` full pass (one flaky Qt-teardown-ordering failure under the full sweep, confirmed to pass cleanly in isolation — not a regression, same class of pre-existing flakiness as the FreeType issue)
- [x] New regression tests added for every fix (`test_subprocess_bayesian_y_band.py`, `test_step2_param_form.py`, `test_max_tree_depth.py`, `test_residuals_panel_render_errors.py`, `test_widget_cleanup_on_destroy.py`, `tests/gui/workspace/test_window_chrome.py` for app chrome, plus extensions to `test_step1.py`/`test_step3_wiring.py`/`test_step5.py`/`test_step6.py`/`test_transform_controller.py`/`test_project_codec.py`)
- [x] Diagnostics panel and app chrome each went through a full spec → plan → two-round adversarial review (`codex exec` + `agy`, independently verified against the actual codebase) → subagent-driven-development execution → final whole-branch review cycle before landing

author: markmhendrickson
body:
## What

Closes the swarm loop: when a build PR is ready for review, the operator gets an **email**, and can **approve it three equivalent ways** — reply APPROVE to the email, click Approve on the PR in GitHub, or comment `/approve` — all converging on **one gated merge**. Motivated by neotoma#1902 (the first autonomous build PR) sitting ready with no notification or approval path.

## Three approval channels, one shared path

All route through `_approve_and_maybe_merge()`, so checkpoint resolution, the GitHub confirmation comment, operator-reviewer cleanup, and the (flag-gated) merge are identical regardless of channel:

1. **Email reply** — Turdus detects an operator `APPROVE` reply to a merge-ready email and POSTs to the Apis loopback `/approve-email` route.
2. **GitHub review** — a `pull_request_review` "approved" event from the operator.
3. **`/approve` comment** — the existing Phase-H1 command, now sharing the path.

## The merge gate

`APIS_APPROVAL_TRIGGERS_MERGE` (new, **default OFF**) — when ON, an explicit operator approval performs the real `gh`-equivalent REST merge (`PUT /pulls/{n}/merge`). Distinct from `APIS_AUTONOMY_AUTO_MERGE` (which merges *without* the operator). `_merge_pr()` returns an honest `(merged, detail)` and **never claims a merge that did not happen** — a 405/409 surfaces as "did NOT complete, merge manually".

## Security properties (tested)

- Only the operator (address match / GitHub login) may approve; bots ignored (defence-in-depth).
- An `APPROVE` inside the **quoted original** email does not count — only the operator's own unquoted text.
- `/approve-email` is loopback-only **and** shared-secret gated; **fails closed** when the secret is unset.
- Self-trigger guard preserved (neotoma#1686): no approval comment body contains a command token.

## Rollout

Ships with `APIS_APPROVAL_TRIGGERS_MERGE=0` — the routing runs end-to-end (email, comment, checkpoint resolve) but **does not merge** until the operator opts in by flipping the flag.

## Also

Hardens `apis.py`'s `.env` loader to strip inline `# comments` from unquoted values — the actual root cause the PR-ready email never fired: `ATELES_NOTIFY_EMAIL=1  # …` parsed to the value `"1  # …"`, failing the `== "1"` check.

## Operator action required (post-merge)

The live GitHub webhooks on ateles + neotoma must add the `pull_request_review` event (see the `github_gateway.py` header). Without it, the GitHub-approve path won't deliver. The other two channels work without any webhook change.

## Tests

+33 tests. Full apis suite **348 pass**, turdus **15 pass**. No new lint; the 5 pre-existing ruff findings in `test_swarm_dispatch.py` are untouched.

author: danielpolowork
body:
## Summary

Both `DispatchDomainEventsAsync` overloads published an aggregate's buffered events and then cleared its
*entire* buffer — so an event a handler raised on that aggregate *during* dispatch (a synchronous
publish) was wiped unpublished. Each aggregate is now **drained to a fixed point** before clearing, so
handler-raised events are delivered. Closes #30.

## Motivation

Issue #30 (2026-07-01 enterprise audit). Per-aggregate events were snapshotted, published, then
`ClearDomainEvents()` wiped the whole buffer. If publishing event A caused a handler to raise event B on
the same aggregate, B was appended but not in the snapshot — never published, yet cleared. Silent,
exception-free loss; the documented at-least-once contract (ADR-0012) did not cover handler-raised events.

You chose **drain to a fixed point** (over "clear only published" / "document the limitation").

## Changes

- Extracted `PublishThenDrainAndClearAsync(aggregate, batch, publish, ct)`: publishes `batch`, then
  re-reads the aggregate's buffer and publishes anything that appeared while handlers ran, looping until
  none remain, and clears only then. Published events are tracked by **reference identity**
  (`ReferenceEqualityComparer`) so the whole-buffer clear is deferred until everything — including
  handler-raised events — has been delivered. Both overloads use it (change-tracker seeds the batch with
  the live events; snapshot seeds it with the captured pre-save copy, then drains the live buffer).
- **Contract preserved:** on a publish failure the exception propagates *before* the clear, so the failing
  aggregate and every one after it keep their events for an at-least-once retry, and already-cleared
  aggregates are not re-published — the per-aggregate clear-on-success semantics from ADR-0012 are
  unchanged.
- **ADR-0022** records the decision and **amends ADR-0012's delivery contract** (which now carries an
  "Amended in part by ADR-0022" note). XML `<remarks>` on both overloads updated.
- Tests for both overloads (handler raises a follow-up on the aggregate during dispatch → delivered, in
  order, buffer ends empty); both verified **red pre-fix**.
- CHANGELOG `Fixed` entry; journal entry + index row; ROADMAP checkpoint advanced.

## Design Patterns

- None — a delivery-contract correctness fix on the domain-event dispatch flow (ADR-0012 / ADR-0022).

## Verification

- [x] Builds cleanly (`dotnet build -warnaserror`) — 0 warnings/errors
- [x] Unit tests pass — **156 pass / 2 Redis skip** (both regressions verified red pre-fix)
- [x] `dotnet format` clean; warnings-as-errors clean
- [ ] `python tools/consistency_lint.py` — not run locally (no Python); hand-verified. Touched invariant:
      **adr-index** (0022 added, indexed, sequential 0001–0022). CI re-runs it.

## Documentation Impact

- [ ] README.md — n/a (no user-facing surface change)
- [x] docs/ROADMAP.md — "Latest checkpoint" pointer advanced
- [x] ADR added — **ADR-0022**, amending ADR-0012's delivery contract
- [ ] docs/patterns/README.md — no pattern change
- [ ] Spec — no divergence (spec §4 describes dispatch at a high level; unchanged)
- [x] CHANGELOG.md — `Fixed` entry
- [x] PR metadata set — assignee, one `fix` type label, `Maintenance` milestone

## Notes

No public API or signature change. Two documented caveats (ADR-0022): a handler that raises events on the
same aggregate **without bound** will not terminate (a consumer error); and an event raised on a
**different**, already-dispatched aggregate earlier in the same pass is not re-visited (raise
cross-aggregate follow-ups in a new unit of work).

Closes #30.

body:
## Description

This PR implements a **Progressive Video Loading Framework** that enables efficient streaming of large cultural videos using **HTTP Range Requests** and the browser's **Media Source Extensions (MSE)** API.

Instead of downloading an entire video before playback, the frontend requests configurable byte ranges from the backend, allowing videos to start almost immediately while dynamically buffering upcoming content based on playback progress. The implementation also includes multiple fallback mechanisms to ensure compatibility across different video formats and servers.

Closes #504

---

# Type of Change

- [x] Frontend Feature
- [x] Backend Feature
- [x] Performance Improvement
- [x] Reliability Improvement
- [x] Networking Enhancement
- [ ] Database Changes
- [ ] Documentation

---

# Checklist

- [x] Progressive video streaming
- [x] HTTP Range support
- [x] Media Source Extensions integration
- [x] Smart look-ahead buffering
- [x] Buffer progress overlay
- [x] Seeking support
- [x] Auto-healing fallback
- [x] Edge-case handling
- [x] Production ready

---

# ✨ Features Implemented

## Progressive Video Loader

Implemented a custom **ProgressiveVideoLoader** using the browser's **Media Source Extensions (MSE)** API.

Instead of downloading an entire video before playback, the loader streams configurable **1 MB chunks** as needed.

Benefits include:

- Faster playback startup
- Lower bandwidth usage
- Reduced memory consumption
- Improved experience on slow networks

---

## Smart Look-Ahead Buffering

The player continuously monitors playback.

Whenever the remaining buffered video drops below approximately **10 seconds**, the loader automatically requests the next video segment.

Advantages:

- Smooth playback
- Minimal unnecessary downloads
- Lower bandwidth consumption when users stop watching early

---

## Real-Time Buffer Overlay

Added a live buffering indicator displaying progress during chunk downloads.

Example:

```
Buffering...
45%
```

The overlay automatically disappears once enough video has been buffered for playback.

---

# Backend HTTP Range Streaming

Implemented full support for:

```
Range: bytes=X-Y
```

The backend responds using:

```
206 Partial Content
```

with proper HTTP headers including:

- Content-Range
- Accept-Ranges
- Content-Length

This enables efficient byte-range streaming compatible with modern browsers.

---

## In-Memory Video Slicing

For locally stored community videos:

- Raw buffers remain in memory
- Requested byte ranges are sliced dynamically
- Only requested segments are transmitted

No unnecessary data is sent.

---

## External Video Proxy

Implemented proxy support for remote videos hosted on:

- CDN providers
- Cloud storage
- External media servers

The backend forwards incoming Range requests and streams the requested bytes back to the browser while preserving range semantics.

This avoids browser CORS limitations.

---

# Auto-Healing Playback

When Media Source Extensions cannot continue safely, the loader automatically falls back to the browser's native video engine.

Users experience uninterrupted playback instead of playback failures.

---

# Edge Case Hardening

## 1. HTTP 200 Memory Exhaustion

### Problem

Some external servers ignore the Range header and return:

```
200 OK
```

with the entire video.

Calling:

```javascript
arrayBuffer()
```

would attempt to load hundreds of megabytes into browser memory.

### Fix

Implemented an `AbortController`.

If a server ignores the Range request:

- download is immediately aborted
- native video playback is activated instead

This prevents browser memory exhaustion.

---

## 2. HTTP Redirect Handling

### Problem

Many cloud providers respond with:

```
301
302
307
```

redirects.

Traditional Node HTTP modules do not automatically follow these redirects, causing streaming failures.

### Fix

Refactored proxy streaming to use the native Node.js `fetch()` API.

Benefits:

- Automatic redirect handling
- Range headers preserved
- Seamless proxy streaming
- Compatible with modern Node.js

---

## 3. Malformed Range Headers

### Problem

HTTP allows multiple valid Range formats:

```
bytes=0-
```

```
bytes=-500
```

```
bytes=100-500
```

Previous parsing logic could produce invalid indices or `NaN`.

### Fix

Implemented a robust Range parser supporting all valid HTTP byte-range formats while safely rejecting invalid requests.

---

## 4. Unfragmented MP4 Playback

### Problem

Some MP4 files are not fragmented.

Seeking during MSE playback caused:

```
SourceBuffer.appendBuffer()
```

to throw decoder exceptions.

### Fix

Wrapped buffer appends inside a guarded `try/catch`.

If fragmentation errors occur:

- playback seamlessly switches to the browser's native decoder
- playback continues normally

No visible interruption occurs.

---

## 5. Smart Fallback

If MSE cannot continue because of:

- decoder limitations
- unsupported containers
- malformed streams

the loader automatically switches to:

```html
<video src="...">
```

using the browser's optimized media engine.

This maximizes compatibility across browsers and mobile devices.

---

# Performance Improvements

Streaming now provides:

- Faster startup
- Smaller downloads
- Lower RAM usage
- Reduced bandwidth consumption
- Efficient look-ahead buffering
- Improved playback on unreliable connections

---

# Backend

Added:

- HTTP Range endpoint
- Partial content responses
- Dynamic in-memory slicing
- External proxy streaming
- Redirect support
- Robust Range parsing

---

# Frontend

Added:

- ProgressiveVideoLoader
- Media Source Extensions
- Smart buffering
- Buffer overlay
- Automatic fallback
- AbortController protection

---

# 🧪 Edge Case Testing

## Test 1 — Progressive Startup

### Scenario

Load a large cultural video.

### Expected

Playback begins after the initial chunk without downloading the full file.

✅ Passed

---

## Test 2 — Look-Ahead Buffering

### Scenario

Watch until remaining buffer drops below threshold.

### Expected

Next chunk downloads automatically.

✅ Passed

---

## Test 3 — HTTP 200 Response

### Scenario

Remote server ignores Range header.

### Expected

Download is aborted.

Native playback activated.

Browser memory remains stable.

✅ Passed

---

## Test 4 — HTTP Redirect

### Scenario

Video URL returns:

```
302 Found
```

### Expected

Proxy follows redirect.

Streaming continues.

✅ Passed

---

## Test 5 — Malformed Range Header

### Scenario

Requests such as:

```
bytes=-500
```

or

```
bytes=0-
```

### Expected

Correct byte calculations.

No parsing failures.

✅ Passed

---

## Test 6 — Seeking on Unfragmented MP4

### Scenario

Seek through an unfragmented video.

### Expected

Automatic fallback to native playback.

No decoder crash.

✅ Passed

---

## Test 7 — External CDN Video

### Scenario

Stream video hosted on external storage.

### Expected

Proxy preserves Range requests.

Playback functions normally.

✅ Passed

---

# Technical Highlights

- Media Source Extensions (MSE)
- Progressive byte-range streaming
- Smart look-ahead buffering
- HTTP Range support
- Partial content responses
- External proxy streaming
- AbortController protection
- Automatic decoder fallback
- Robust Range parsing
- Redirect handling

---

# Acceptance Criteria

- [x] HTTP Range support implemented
- [x] Progressive streaming
- [x] Media Source Extensions integration
- [x] Dynamic buffering
- [x] Buffer overlay
- [x] Seeking support
- [x] External proxy streaming

## PR description

First of three stacked PRs restoring Amsterdam to the
`tests-glamsterdam-devnet@v6.1.1` spec. Followed by #10907 (state-gas accounting) and
#10908 (intrinsic gas and delegation); the three together take the `_amsterdam_`
reference tests from 808 failures to 0.

Rebased onto main now that #10765 has landed — the EIP-2780 commit that used to be in
this PR is superseded by it, so this branch is now EIP-8246 only (7 files, +131/−38).

### EIP-8246: SELFDESTRUCT no longer burns the originator's balance

A `SELFDESTRUCT` on an account created in the same transaction previously destroyed
the account and burned its balance. Under EIP-8246 the account is cleared at
transaction finalization — nonce reset, code and storage removed — but keeps its
balance; EIP-161 state clearing then removes it only if that balance is zero.

Because the balance is preserved rather than burned, no EIP-7708 closure (burn) log is
emitted. `isSelfDestructBalancePreserved()` gates both behaviours so pre-Amsterdam
forks are unaffected.

Also updates the two acceptance tests whose expectations encoded the burn behaviour.

body:
## Kontekst

Zadanie D4 obejmowało (1) logowanie w sondach zamiast `except Exception: pass` oraz (2) martwy zewnętrzny `try/except` w `check_ollama` + bezpieczne wyłuskiwanie nazw modeli.

**Punkt 1 był już zrealizowany** przy wcześniejszym hardeningu (zmergowane): oba moduły mają `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)`, a każdy `except Exception: pass` został zamieniony na `except Exception as exc: logger.debug(...)`. Zero pustych `pass` już w kodzie (potwierdzone `grep`). Ta zmiana skupia się więc na **punkcie 2**.

## Problem

Zewnętrzny `try/except` w `check_ollama` był praktycznie **martwy**: `probe_http_service` jest z kontraktu bezrzutowe (zwraca `available=False`, nie rzuca). Jedynym realnym źródłem wyjątku było samo wyłuskanie nazw:

```python
result["models"] = [m["name"] for m in data.get("models", [])]
```

— rzucało `KeyError`/`TypeError`/`AttributeError` przy nietypowym kształcie JSON, a wyjątek był po cichu łykany, degradując **cały** wynik do `available=False`.

## Zmiany (`check_ollama`)

- **Usunięty martwy `try/except`**; nazwy wyłuskiwane defensywnie:
  - `data` nie-`dict` → brak modeli,
  - `"models"` nie-lista (np. `null`) → pusta lista, bez iterowania po `None`,
  - wpisy nie-`dict` lub bez `str`-owego/niepustego `"name"` → pomijane.
- Osiągalny serwer raportuje teraz `available=True` z tymi nazwami, które dało się poprawnie sparsować, zamiast kolapsować do `unavailable` przez jeden zły wpis.

## Testy (`tests/test_services.py`)

- `test_check_ollama_skips_entries_without_name` — mieszanka wpisów (brak `name`, pusty `name`, `name: null`, element nie-`dict`) → `available=True`, `models` tylko z poprawnych nazw.
- `test_check_ollama_available_with_unexpected_shape` — `"models": null` → `available=True`, `models=[]`, bez rzucania.

Publiczne API i kształty zwracanych słowników **bez zmian**.

- coder could still materialize over `PLAN.md`
- missing staged files could still reach Git Boundary approval
- unrelated dirty tree state could still reach Git Boundary approval
- `--execute` without `--no-dry-run` stayed dry-run but did not make that explicit enough

This PR fixes those issues as one cohesive execution preflight and routing gate.

## Changed

- Added dogfood payload artifact routing
  - CLI stage/allowed payload path reaches Pipeline Runner
  - Pipeline Runner routes payload path to coder expected artifact path
  - coder materializes `dogfood-proof.yml` in temp dogfood-like tests
  - no PR 0131 hardcoding added
  - Prompt Composer remains unchanged

- Added overwrite protection
  - existing `PLAN.md` is not silently overwritten
  - existing review artifacts are protected from silent overwrite
  - `overwrite_allowed` policy is explicit and tested

- Added stage-file existence preflight
  - missing staged payload blocks before Git Boundary approval
  - reason includes `stage_file_missing`

- Added dirty-tree strictness
  - unrelated dirty files block before Git Boundary approval
  - dirty tracked `PLAN.md` / `plan-review.yml` blocks dogfood execution
  - `.ariadne/` and `captures/` remain local residue, not commit payload

- Clarified dry-run semantics
  - `--execute` alone remains non-mutating
  - `--execute --no-dry-run` is the real execution path
  - fake no-dry-run execution records execution results and persists them

## Validation

- compileall — pass

## Safety Boundary

This PR does not add agent execution authority.

- No Docker enabling
- No real git/gh in tests
- No network
- No dependency installation
- No agents run
- No Prompt Composer changes
- No Verdict Parser changes
- No Docker adapter / Adapter Registry / Local Harness changes

Adds a per-run **"Clone into folder"** field to the Start dialog — your "take a directory as input to clone into" ask. Threaded exactly like the branch picker.

`Start dialog (cloneDir)` → `startTargetSchema` → `startWorkItemTarget` globals → executors → `run_context.clone_dir` → the laptop runtime materializer.

## Changes
- **`mcp-server/sandbox.ts`** — `targetDir` on `WorkspaceRootRequest`. In `workspaceRootForRunContext` it's resolved **under** `workItemWorkspacesRoot()` via `safeWorkspaceSegment` — a plain folder name lands in a safe, predictable spot, and an arbitrary FS path can't escape the managed root (same guard as the existing explicit-`workspaceRoot` seam). Every stage of the run shares the chosen folder.
- **`mcp-server/tool-run.ts`** — accepts `run_context.clone_dir` / `cloneDir` → passes as `targetDir`.
- **`AgentTaskExecutor`** — sends `run_context.clone_dir` from `globals.cloneDir`.
- **work-items start schema/service + `RunWorkflowPage`** — the `cloneDir` plumbing + input (mirrors `sourceRef`).

## Scope / honesty
Fully wired for the **copilot / AGENT_TASK** path + the runtime seam. The **WORKBENCH** path clones at the deterministic per-work-item root; honoring `cloneDir` there needs Context Fabric to forward `clone_dir` into the governed `run_context` — a follow-up (and untestable until the dial-in bridge is reconnected). Blank field = today's behavior, so it's non-breaking.

## Security
The chosen folder is **always resolved under the managed workspaces root** — it cannot point the runtime at an arbitrary location on disk.

## Verification
esbuild parses all 6 files (mcp-server + workgraph-api + web) clean. This is runtime-side, so end-to-end exercise needs the bridge up; the seam reuses the existing `workspaceRoot` override that tool-run already threads.

## **🚀 Related issue**

closes #31 

## **#️⃣ Summary**
- StageResultCount 집계 테이블이 이벤트 유실 등으로 원본과 어긋날 수 있어, 주기적으로 원본과 대조해 보정하는 배치를 추가했습니다.
- posting.service에 성격이 다른 클래스가 섞여 비대해져, 역할별 하위 패키지로 분리했습니다.

## **🎯 Work Description**

### 집계 테이블 정합성 보정 배치 추가
#### 배경
- StageResultCount는 등록/변경 이벤트로 갱신되는데, 이벤트 유실·예외 시 원본(Registration)과 드리프트가 발생할 수 있음
- 기존 rebuildAll(전량 삭제 후 재생성)은 초기화용이라, 운영 중 실행하면 배치 도중 데이터가 비어 조회가 0으로 보이는 문제

#### 변경 사항
- StageResultCountReconciler 추가
  - 삭제 없이 원본 집계와 현재 테이블을 대조해 **어긋난 것만** 보정
  - 원본엔 있고 테이블엔 없는 (posting, stage)는 신규 생성
  - 불일치 발견 시 WARN 로그로 드리프트 규모 노출
  - 멱등 (여러 번 실행해도 결과 동일)
  - @Scheduled로 매일 새벽 4시 실행
- StageResultCount.reconcile() 추가 (카운트를 실제값으로 보정)

#### 설계 결정
- **rebuildAll은 초기화용으로 유지, Reconciler는 운영 배치로 분리**
  - 초기화: 확실히 깨끗한 상태에서 전량 재생성 (DataInitializer)
  - 운영 보정: 삭제 없이 대조 보정 (조회 중단 없음)
- **announcedDate는 배치가 건드리지 않음**
  - "15 최초 돌파일"은 과거 사실이라 재계산 불가·불변
  - 배치는 카운트만 보정


### posting 서비스 패키지 구조 정리

#### 변경 사항
- `aggregate/`: 집계 갱신·배치
- `calculator/`: 계산·판정 로직 (NextStageCalculator, CurrentStageResolver...)
- `support/`: 서비스 도우미·값 객체 (PostingAggregateLoader, PostingResponseAssembler, PostingSortComparators, PostingAggregate...)
- service 루트: 요청 처리 서비스만


## **👍 동작 확인**

(생략)

구현해주신 ViewCountCleanupScheduler 도 패키지 위치를 변경하였습니다. 이에 따라 해당 class 를 사용하는 다른 파일들의 import 문도 변경되었습니다! 참고 부탁드려용~!

Stacked on #20 (branched from its head `39849421`) — this diff is only the D8 work and its refinement pass. When #20 merges, this retargets to main.

## D8 — corpus-free documents + view modes (11 commits)

The workbench no longer requires a corpus spine or line numbers:

- **New document…** takes pasted/file text in any language, detects lines-vs-paragraphs (overridable), numbers with `¶N` or plain lines. New `paragraph` / `plain-line` citation schemes with `spineSource: 'corpus' | 'document'`; everything gates on capabilities, never scheme ids (`schemeIdIsolation` test).
- **Paragraph view** (original left, translation right, one row per paragraph) and **Interpolated view** (original under the field, by-paragraph or by-sentence). Sentences auto-detected at import, hand-fixable.
- **Two coexisting translation layers**: paragraph-level (`englishPara`, new 1:1-line `[ENGLISH.PARA]` section) and sentence-level — switching granularity never moves or destroys text; the other layer shows read-only.
- **Structure editing**: paragraph split/merge with automatic renumbering (document-spine only — the corpus owns row count elsewhere), sentence-boundary fix-up, plain-line chunk grouping (`paragraph_starts`, display-only).
- AI suite, export (incl. bilingual interleave), and undo work across the new units.
- Codex adversarial review round 1: 4 findings, all fixed + regression-pinned (footnote markers are sentence-layer-only; malformed `paragraph_starts` degrades with a notice; free-doc bilingual compile was silently English-only; paragraph Check reads the visible draft).

## Refinement pass (6 commits)

- **Corpus-paragraph (Busse) works first-class**: open in Paragraph view, wrap correctly in the grid, get the by-sentence toggle — and a latent export bug fixed: their `englishPara` translations never reached docx/bilingual export (routing keyed on `spineSource` instead of row unit).
- **Multi-sentence AI paragraph suggestions keep line breaks**, stored as an escape-aware `⏎` token at the `[ENGLISH.PARA]` boundary (pilcrow-analog; existing files byte-identical, test-pinned). Export flattens breaks to spaces (v1).

- **Interpolated originals get full structure-gesture parity** with the two-column views, with display→model offset mapping through the trimmed slices; source blocks count as the source column for batch translate.
- Codex adversarial review round 2: 2 findings, both fixed (`⏎` escape confined to the paragraph boundary so existing `[ENGLISH]` bytes never change; slice-join clicks map to the next word, not a dead whitespace offset).

## Что и зачем

Часть решения [1c-syntax/intellij-language-1c-bsl#31](https://github.com/1c-syntax/intellij-language-1c-bsl/issues/31): при скачивании релиза BSL Language Server клиент (плагин IntelliJ) мог показать только бесконечный «крутящийся» индикатор, потому что загрузчик качал ассет через `HttpResponse.BodyHandlers.ofFile(...)` — без какой-либо обратной связи о ходе загрузки.

## Was

Ein **„Abbrechen"-Button** beendet einen laufenden Transkriptions-/Korrektur-Job **samt Prozessbaum** (`python → claude → node/MCP`). Bisher hielt `jobs.py` nur die PID, nutzte sie aber nie — ein projektweiter Korrekturlauf = `1 + N × 900 s` Opus ohne Abbruch.

## Warum taskkill /F /T

Die Prozesse laufen nur mit `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` (keine Prozessgruppe/Job-Object). `terminate()` auf den äußeren Prozess **verwaist** den `claude`+MCP-Subtree (schon dokumentiert in `correct.py:147-149`). `taskkill /F /T /PID` läuft die PPID-Kette ab und killt den ganzen Baum.

- **`app.py`**: `POST /api/jobs/{job_id}/cancel` (404 bei unbekannt/terminal).
- **Frontend**: `#canceljob`-Button, poll-getrieben ein-/ausgeblendet; onclick nur POST + selbst sperren — der nächste Poll sieht `cancelled` und beendet sauber.
- **Docs**: CLAUDE.md/README — Endpoint + „Abbruch resumbar per Re-Run".

## Verifikation

- **81 pytest grün** (+4), inkl. **echtem Enkel-Prozessbaum-Kill-Test**.
- **E2E gegen echten `claude`+MCP-Baum** (Demo-Dogfood): mitten in der Glossar-Phase abgebrochen → `claude.exe` tot, Descendants der Job-PID = 0, Status `cancelled`, Server unbeschädigt.

author: upuddu
body:
`shuffle`'s type switch accepts arrays, slices and strings (and pointers to those), but the result was built with `reflect.MakeSlice(reflect.TypeOf(l), ...)`, which panics with "reflect.MakeSlice of non-slice type" for anything but a plain slice value - so `{{ shuffle "abc" }}`, an array, or a pointer to a slice crash the build.

Build the result from the indirected value's type so a pointer to a slice works, collect arrays into a slice of their element type, and drop strings from the accepted kinds so they return the regular "can't iterate over" error instead of panicking. Behavior for a plain slice (including named slice types) is unchanged.

Roadmap Track 3: **NY** — the largest remaining gap (~6,900 rows at aggregators; DB floor 2025). Route per the merged spike (#140), scope confirmed with Raphael: **detail harvest only** (the 2021–2024 modern era and 2016–2020 index PDFs are follow-ups decided after the post-run audit).

## Discovery
`_discover_ny_detail_urls` queries the CDX API for `labor.ny.gov/app/warn` (prefix, statuscode:200) and dedupes by `details.asp?id=N` keeping the **latest** capture per id (URL variants — scheme/www/`&_ga` — survive urlkey collapse). Live result: **4,293 replay URLs, ids 3–9536**.

`parse_ny_detail` handles the retired ASP portal's labeled record: date of notice, control number (stripped from employer names), company + street + `City, NY ZIP`, county with `| WIB | Region` (→ extra), business type (→ extra), **Number Affected**, layoff/closing dates (`Layoff Date` first-date, `Closing Date` fallback), reason → closure_type. `-----` → None; `\xa0`-heavy cp1252 pages parsed from bytes. **Multi-site filings**: the `Other site affected:` appendix rows become their own NoticeRows with per-site counts (`(8 affected)`) and control numbers. Chrome-only shell captures (some ids were dead when archived) parse to 0 rows and are skipped. Real per-notice `notice_date`s — no month proxy needed. `source_url` = the original labor.ny.gov URL.

## Infrastructure
- **`--limit N`** on `backfill-historical` (url-list mode) so the gated pilot can dry-run ~100 pages instead of a full 4.3k pass twice (~4.5 h each at Wayback pacing).
- **Retry/backoff in `_backfill_url_list`** for Wayback connection refusals (one 30s backoff — observed recovering 2 of 3 refusals during validation; benefits MN/CA/… too).

- Residual Wayback drops are expected even with retry — completion is verified **per-id against prod** (the PA lesson), with a top-up run if needed.

After merge: gated w_homelab round — pilot Job (`--limit 100 --dry-run`, ~7 min), then the full run (~4.5 h), per-id verification, roadmap strike + `/refresh-audit`. Expected yield: **~4,000–4,500 rows with counts and geocodable addresses**, taking NY's floor from 2025 to ~2001.

author: jongio
body:
## What

Adds a `--fail` flag that makes `azd rest` exit with a non-zero code when the response status is 400 or higher.

Closes #233

## Why

Today the command exits 0 even on a 404 or 500, so a script or CI step cannot tell a failed request from a successful one without parsing the body. That is surprising for anyone used to `curl --fail`.

## How it works

- `--fail` off (default): behavior is unchanged, exit 0 regardless of status.
- `--fail` on and status is 400 or higher: the response body and any `--write-out` output are printed first, then the command exits with code 22 (the same code `curl --fail` uses).
- `--fail` on and status is under 400: exit 0.

Printing the body before exiting mirrors `curl --fail-with-body`, so error details stay visible instead of being swallowed.

```bash
# Fails the step if the resource is missing
azd rest get "https://management.azure.com/subscriptions/$SUB/resourceGroups/missing?api-version=2021-04-01" --fail
echo "exit: $?"   # 22
```

## Changes

- New `--fail` persistent flag wired through `config.Config`.
- New `httpFailError` in the service package that carries exit code 22 through the existing `ExitCoder` path in `main`.
- Applied after the body is written in the single-request path.
- Unit tests for error status, success, redirect, and the flag being off.
- Reference docs: new `--fail` row and exit code 22 entry; corrected the exit code 1 description.
- README usage example.

## Testing

- `go test ./src/...` passes.
- `gofmt`, `go vet`, `golangci-lint`, `cspell`, and the website build are clean.

author: malinosqui
body:
## Problem

Customer-reported (first report, item 5): an old rule persisted; toggling sync off auto-removed it, toggling on re-added it on the next run.

Root cause: toggle-off "delete" is a soft-delete (status → DELETED, record stays in the rules array), and `findRuleBySourcePath` matched with `Array.find` over ALL rules — soft-deleted included — returning the **first (oldest)** record for a sourcePath. When a stale deleted record coexisted with a newer live one, every re-import matched the stale uuid, and `createOrUpdate` merged the fresh content into it and flipped it back to ACTIVE — a resurrection of the oldest record, not an update of the current one.

## Fix

`findRuleBySourcePath` now prefers the **newest non-deleted** match. Falling back to a deleted record when it's the only match is kept intentionally: if the source file still exists in the repo, reviving that record (with content refreshed from the file) beats accumulating duplicates.

## Tests

4 new tests covering: newest-live wins over older-deleted, live wins even when older, sole-deleted fallback (revive), and no-match. Full kody sweep green.

## Summary

Stage 3 task **L** (session #4) — makes the game keyboard-playable and screen-reader-friendlier, with **no change to combat or game logic**.

- **Arrow keys / WASD** → move to the adjacent tile. Reuses `main.js`'s existing `onTileClick` → `tryMove`; the only game-coupled hook is a one-line `move(dx, dy)` callback.
- **Esc** → closes the top-most open modal (mirrors the existing scrim-click by hiding the last visible `#*-overlay`, so a stacked modal like the duel-over-profile closes in order).
- **Digit keys 1–9** → open the Nth `#nav-menu` panel. Queried live, so the runtime-injected Forge / Meridians / Trials buttons are included automatically.
- **Guards**: ignores keys while typing in an input/textarea/select or with Ctrl/Meta/Alt held; suppresses map movement while a modal is open (Esc still closes).

## Accessibility

- `applyA11y()` (in JS, so it covers runtime-injected modals) sets `role="group"` + a keyboard-hint `aria-label` + `tabindex="-1"` on `#map-grid` (the skip-link target), and `role="dialog"` / `aria-modal="true"` / a heading-derived `aria-label` on every `#*-overlay`.
- `css/a11y.css` adds a **skip link**, an `.sr-only` utility, and a keyboard-only `.tile:focus-visible` ring (building on the polish-pass `--ring`).

## Coordination with Task Z (mobile/touch, owner #2)

Keyboard (this PR) and touch (Z) are **separate modules**. My entire `main.js` footprint is:
- one import: `import { initInput } from './input.js';`
- **one wiring line, placed last** in the init block: `initInput({ move: (dx, dy) => onTileClick(state.pos.x + dx, state.pos.y + dy) });`

So whichever of L/Z lands second only needs to keep both single-line hooks near the other `init*` calls — no shared handler. (Noted in `TASK_4.md` Worker Log for #1.)

## Files

- **New (owned):** `js/input.js`, `css/a11y.css`.
- **Shared (minimal):** `index.html` (a skip-link `<a>` + one `<link>` in `<head>`), `js/main.js` (one import + one call). **No `ui.js`, no `combat.js`, no `style.css` edit, no save fields.**
- `CLAUDE.md` status bullet.

## Verification

Cloud session (no localhost link) — verified in-container:
- **Headless** (DOM-stubbed `input.js`): key→delta mapping (arrows + WASD), digit → nav click, Esc hides the open overlay + `preventDefault`, Esc no-op when nothing open, guards (typing target / Ctrl held / modal-open suppresses movement), ARIA applied to grid + overlays.

author: egnalmada
body:
_NewClient_ pings the broker once at startup and returns the error on the first failure. When the broker is briefly unreachable at startup - DNS not yet resolvable, broker not yet ready, or the broker rescheduled while clients are starting - callers get an immediate error and typically fail fast, causing cold-start crash loops.

Wrap the startup ping in a bounded retry loop before returning the error: default 100 attempts with a 3s backoff, per-attempt ping timeout unchanged. Configurable via new options `WithPingRetries` / `WithPingBackoff` alongside the existing `WithPingTimeout`. Default-on, so consumers get the behavior by bumping the version.

author: sviluppatore
body:
## Summary

Improvements from a code review of the server, in two rounds. Bumps version to 0.2.0.

## Round 1 — reliability and core coverage

### Client refactor (`client.py`)

- Rewrote the module-level global-state client as an async `WallabagClient` class backed by a pooled `httpx.AsyncClient`. Tools previously called synchronous `httpx` from `async def` functions, blocking the event loop for up to 20s per request; every request also opened a fresh connection.
- The OAuth `refresh_token` grant is now actually used: expired access tokens are renewed via refresh first, falling back to the password grant. (The refresh token was previously stored but dead code.)
- On HTTP 401, the request is retried once with a freshly acquired token when credentials allow re-authentication.
- `configure()` drops cached token state whenever credentials change, and a new `reset()` clears everything — fixing state leakage across reconfigurations (and test-order dependence in the suite).

### New tools

- `wallabag_search` — full-text search via `GET /api/search` (wallabag 2.5+)
- `wallabag_entry_exists` — check if a URL is already saved (dedupe before add)
- `wallabag_remove_tag_from_entry` — remove a tag from one entry without deleting it globally

### Tool/API fixes

- `wallabag_list_entries` now requests `detail=metadata`, so wallabag no longer transfers full article HTML that the server immediately discards
- Exposed the `since` filter (UNIX timestamp) on listing
- `sort`/`order` are constrained with `Literal` types in the schema
- Removed the `unread` filter — the wallabag API has no such parameter (unread is `archived=false`)
- `WALLABAG_TIMEOUT` parse errors now fail with a clean message instead of a traceback

### CI

- The live external-docs check (`scripts/live_docs_test.py`) moved to a weekly scheduled / manually dispatched job so third-party site hiccups no longer block pushes and PRs

## Round 2 — content tools, packaging, metadata

- **`wallabag_export_entry`** — full readable article content via `GET /api/entries/{id}/export.{format}` (txt/json/xml/csv), with a `max_chars` truncation guard; the shared 401-retry logic was extracted into an `_authorized()` helper so it covers non-JSON responses too
- **`wallabag_update_annotation`** — edit annotation text via `PUT /api/annotations/{id}`
- **`wallabag_get_entry(include_content=true)`** now returns plain text extracted from the article HTML, bounded by a new `max_content_chars` parameter, instead of dumping the raw HTML payload into context
- **CI matrix** — tests now run on Python 3.11, 3.12, and 3.13

author: code-yeongyu
body: ## Why A senpi-task child could finish and never wake its parent, leaving the parent waiting forever. Two suppression paths caused this: 1. **`queue_silently` idle completions** were parked behind the optional `wake_idle_parent` knob. When a parent went idle and the child completed, the notification sat in the buffer with nothing to flush it — the parent stayed asleep with no turn ever triggered. 2. **Streaming completions** were delivered without `triggerTurn`, so even when the notification reached the parent session the renderer and steer never ran — the message landed but the turn did not resume. The `wake_idle_parent` config was the wrong lever: making "does the parent ever wake up" opt-in meant the default configuration could silently hang. ## What changed - **Idle completions always wake the parent.** The `wake_idle_parent` suppression knob is removed from the schema, config loader/writer, and docs. Child completion always routes through the arbitrated coordinator, which owns the single-dispatch wake so concurrent idle/error/completion edges collapse to one injection (no duplicate-wake regression). - **Streaming completions deliver direct with `triggerTurn`.** Streaming now routes as a direct delivery carrying `triggerTurn: true` plus the configured `deliver_as`, so the renderer and steer survive the wake. Idle stays on the coordinator; streaming takes the direct path — the two routes are kept distinct on purpose. - **`deliver_as` is preserved end-to-end** through the streaming adapter and the team-message notifier, so downstream rendering keeps the configured presentation instead of falling back to a bare inject. ## QA / evidence - **Live idle-wake proof:** drove a real idle parent + completing child and confirmed the parent wakes and the turn resumes (no longer waits forever). - **Streaming adapter tests:** new `unconditional-wake.test.ts` + updated `parent-notifier.test.ts`, `routing.test.ts`, `notifier.test.ts`, `team-message-notifier.test.ts`, and `deliver-lead.test.ts` pin the direct-delivery `triggerTurn` + `deliver_as` behavior and the coordinator-owned idle wake. - **Unit + `bun run test:senpi`** green across the senpi-task and omo-senpi suites. - **Schema freshness:** `assets/omo.schema.json` regenerated with `wake_idle_parent` removed (no drift). - **Task e2e regression:** `packages/omo-senpi/scripts/qa/task-e2e*.mjs` updated and re-run — no regression in the end-to-end task flow. ## Residual risk The two completion routes (idle → coordinator, streaming → direct) share the same wake contract but distinct code paths; regression tests cover the concurrent/idle/streaming triggers collapsing to a single dispatch, so duplicate-injection risk is pinned by test. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Always wake the parent when a background child completes, and deliver streaming notifications directly with `triggerTurn` while preserving `deliver_as` and the custom renderer. - **Bug Fixes** - Removed `wake_idle_parent` from config and schema; idle completions in `senpi-task` now always wake via the coordinator (single, deduped injection). - Streaming completions and team lead messages in `omo-senpi` deliver through the renderer with `triggerTurn: true` and the configured `deliver_as` (`steer` or `followUp`); they no longer reroute through the idle coordinator. - Updated tests and e2e flows to pin unconditional wake and direct streaming delivery; regenerated `assets/omo.schema.json` and refreshed docs. - **Migration** - Delete `task.notification.wake_idle_parent` from `omo.json`. Only `task.notification.deliver_as` remains. Behavior now always wakes idle parents. Written for commit 53fa9b3cad35091a250a72908c52c76083c9503f. Summary will update on new commits.

author: gochi20
body:
## What

Complete, production-ready Mentorship Management System built with Next.js 15 (App Router), React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS + shadcn/ui, Prisma + Neon PostgreSQL, Auth.js v5, Gmail SMTP, React Hook Form + Zod, and Vercel deployment configuration.

## Features

- **Auth & approval workflow** — Admin / Mentor / Mentee roles; every new account is Pending Approval; only admins approve/reject; only approved accounts can log in (credentials + JWT sessions, bcrypt hashing, edge middleware route protection).
- **Automatic pairing** — runs immediately on mentee approval: same department (hard filter when requested) → shared interests → mentor availability → random tie-break. Mentor capacity is never exceeded (transactional re-check + partial unique index). Unmatched mentees are waitlisted, admins notified, and pairing retries automatically when a new mentor is approved or a slot frees up.
- **Admin dashboard** — overview stats (mentors, mentees, active semester, waitlist, pending approvals, pairing & meeting statistics), user management with search/filters, manual pairing & reassignment, semester management (create/activate/archive, open/close registration), announcements, bulk email, CSV import/export, analytics.
- **Mentor & mentee dashboards** — assigned mentees/mentor with contact info, meeting history and log form, upcoming meetings, announcements, profile editing.
- **Messaging** — internal 1:1 chat with unread counts, read/unread toggle, conversation search, and quick actions: Send Email (mailto) and Open WhatsApp (wa.me link from the recipient's phone).
- **Email automation (Gmail SMTP)** — registration received, account approved/rejected, pairing notifications, weekly reminders and meeting reminders via Vercel cron, announcement blasts.
- **Search** — cross-entity search over mentors, mentees, meetings, messages and semesters, scoped by role.
- **Security** — role-based authorization on every API route, CSRF protection via Auth.js, rate limiting, input sanitization, HTML-escaped email templates, security headers.

## Database

Normalized Prisma schema (users, semesters, mentor/mentee profiles, interests + join tables, pairings, meetings, messages, announcements, notifications) with indexes, check constraints, a partial unique index guaranteeing one active pairing per mentee, and a hand-written initial migration. Seed script creates the admin, an active semester, predefined interests and sample users.

## Verification

- `npm test` — 59/59 Vitest tests pass (pairing priorities/capacity, validators, CSV, sanitization, rate limiter, plus mocked-Prisma integration tests for the register API and pairing flow)
- `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean
- `npm run build` — production build succeeds (all routes + middleware)

## Docs

`README.md` plus `docs/INSTALLATION.md`, `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md` (Vercel + Neon + Gmail + cron setup) and `docs/TESTING.md`; CSV import templates in `sample-data/`.

## Notes for reviewers

- Rate limiter is in-memory (fine per serverless instance); swap for Upstash Redis for strict global limits — documented in the deployment guide.
- Gmail caps ~500 recipients/day; bulk mail sends in batches of 20.
- Seed admin credentials come from `SEED_ADMIN_EMAIL` / `SEED_ADMIN_PASSWORD` (defaults in `.env.example` — change in production).

body:
Completes the open-answer / sessions feature: timeout auto-submit, an open-answer grading fix, and the per-quiz **session history** UI (Part C).

## 1. Auto-submit open answers on timeout

For open questions, if the timer ran out before the player pressed **Enviar**, their answer was lost. Now the draft is auto-submitted when time is almost up.

- At **≤ 1s left** on an unanswered open question, the current draft is submitted automatically (partial answers count).
- An **empty** draft is submitted too, so a non-response is recorded (`answer_text` empty, `is_correct` null → shows as "(sin respuesta)").
- Fires at 1s (not 0s) to avoid racing the server's question-close (`QUESTION_CLOSED`).
- The draft is cleared between questions. Client-side because the partial text only lives in the browser.

## 2. Open-answer punctuation fix

A stored key phrase with trailing punctuation (e.g. `"stracciatella."`) forced players to type the punctuation too, or it was marked wrong. `normalize()` now strips surrounding whitespace **and** punctuation from both keywords and responses. Also removes a temporary grading debug log.

## 3. Session history per quiz (Part C)

- **`GET /api/quizzes/:id/sessions`** — lists a quiz's `finished` sessions (newest-first) with player counts, gated by `requireAdmin + authGate + ownerGate`.
- **"Historial"** action on each quiz card → `/admin/quizzes/:id/sessions`.
- Read-only **`QuizSessionsView`** lists past sessions; clicking one expands its leaderboard + per-player answers (reuses `GET /api/sessions/:pin/results`).
- Extracted `groupResultsByPlayer` into a shared, tested lib.

author: tlongwell-block
body:
## L5 — Relay-signed moderation notice DMs

Fills the `moderation_notices.rs` scaffold (contract tip `4c58489b`) per plan §0.3. One lane file changed.

### What it does
`send_moderation_notice(tenant, state, recipient, notice)`:
1. **DM channel** — `state.db.open_dm({relay mod key, recipient})`, participant-hash idempotent ⇒ one thread per (community, user).
2. **Discovery** — reuses `emit_group_discovery_events` on first use, which already emits kind:39000 with `hidden` / `t=dm` / `p` for DM channels (no reimplementation).
3. **Profile** — relay-signed kind:0 `"{host} Moderation"` (replaceable) on first use.
4. **Notice** — relay-signed kind:9 with `h=<dm_channel_id>` + an `e` tag naming the source id, inserted and fanned out via `dispatch_persistent_event` (same path as every other relay-authored event).

### Idempotency
Per (source id, recipient): the `e`-tagged source id is queried before insert; an existing relay-authored notice for that id short-circuits. A crash-retry between insert and fan-out is a safe no-op.

### Privacy (module invariant)
Bodies are built **only** from the notice's own sanitized fields (`status` / `summary` / `public_reason`). Never reporter identities, other reporters, or raw report notes.

### Notes for reviewers
- The `ModerationNotice` enum shape is unchanged from the scaffold (pinned contract).
- `"{Community}"` resolves to `tenant.host()` — the `communities` table has no display-name column; host is the community's public identity.
- Non-replyable v1: nothing wires inbound replies to this thread.

### Verification
- `cargo check -p buzz-relay` ✅
- `cargo clippy -p buzz-relay --all-targets` ✅ zero warnings
- `cargo test -p buzz-relay --lib moderation_notices` ✅ 4/4 (source_id selection + per-variant body rendering / privacy)
- Pre-commit hooks green.

Base: `eva/community-moderation`. Trailers: Co-authored-by + Signed-off-by Tyler Longwell.

author: cmungall
body:
## Glucose-6-phosphatase system (endogenous glucose production)

Batch-by-module PR for the ER glucose-6-phosphatase system — the terminal, committed step of endogenous glucose production shared by gluconeogenesis and glycogenolysis (directly downstream of the glycogenolysis module's PGM1 step).

### Module
`modules/glucose_6_phosphatase_system.yaml` — two obligate ER-membrane components:
1. **SLC37A4 (G6PT)** — glucose-6-phosphate:phosphate antiporter that imports cytosolic G6P into the ER lumen
2. **Glucose-6-phosphatase catalytic subunit** — hydrolyses luminal G6P → **glucose + Pi** at the ER-lumen face; FAMILY selector (PTHR12591) generic over the G6PC1/G6PC2/G6PC3 paralogs, with G6PC1 (liver) + G6PC3 (ubiquitous) as verified representatives

GO MFs from human GOA; Reactome reactions R-HSA-198513/71825/3262512 verified against the local cache (cache files committed in this PR); cross-linked to the three gene reviews via `file:` evidence.

### Gene reviews
| Gene | UniProt | Core MF | Disease |
|------|---------|---------|---------|
| G6PC1 | P35575 | GO:0004346 glucose-6-phosphatase | GSD Ia (von Gierke) |
| G6PC3 | Q9BUM1 | GO:0004346 glucose-6-phosphatase | severe congenital neutropenia 4 |
| SLC37A4 | O43826 | GO:0061513 + GO:0015152 (G6P:Pi antiporter) | GSD Ib (glycogenosis + neutropenia) |

The shared transporter explains why SLC37A4 (GSD Ib) couples the hepatic-G6PC1 metabolic phenotype with the neutrophil-G6PC3 immune phenotype.

### Validation
All three gene reviews pass `just validate`; the module passes structural (`ModuleReview`) + term-label validation.

author: divyeshpatro
body:
## Problem

Admin > Payments always showed empty even though real purchases were happening.

Root cause: the payment persistence mapper (`toDbPayment` in `backend/db.ts`) wrote to a non-existent `metadata` column (the Prisma model's column is `notes`) and sent a lowercase status that violates the `PaymentStatus` DB enum. Every payment insert was rejected by Prisma — and `safeUpsert` swallowed the error with an empty `catch {}`, so the failure was invisible. Payments existed only in server memory and vanished on every restart.

## Changes

- **`backend/db.ts`** — `toDbPayment`/`fromDbPayment` now use the real `notes` column and convert status casing between the API (lowercase) and the DB enum (UPPERCASE); `fromDbPayment` also normalizes `createdAt` and strips `updatedAt` so rows round-trip cleanly
- **`backend/db.ts`** — `safeUpsert` now logs persistence failures (count + first error) instead of silently swallowing them
- **`scripts/backfill-payments.ts`** (+ `npm run backfill:payments`) — reconstructs one SUCCESS payment per subscription that has no payment row, so historical purchase records are restored. Dry-run by default; pass `--apply` to write. Backfilled rows are marked with `notes.backfilled: true`
- **`tests/payments-mapper.test.ts`** — 9 regression tests covering both mapper bugs and a full round-trip

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit` clean; full vitest suite passes (80 tests / 11 files)
- Backfill tested against a local DB: dry-run correctly identified 314 subscriptions with no payment row; `--apply` inserted all 314; re-run reports 0 missing (idempotent)
- End-to-end on a running local server: admin payments API returns the backfilled records, and a freshly created payment order persisted to Postgres and appeared in the admin payments API with its Razorpay order id

## After merging

1. Deploy, then run `npm run backfill:payments` on the server (review dry-run output), followed by `npm run backfill:payments -- --apply` to restore historical payment records
2. Note: backfilled rows have `providerOrderId = null` (the original Razorpay ids were lost with the in-memory state); amounts, plans, users, and dates are all present

author: tszaks
body:
## Summary

Eleven reliability features plus a review-driven repair round. Stacked on #11.

**Never hang, never lie:**
- Per-agent wall-clock timeout (`--agent-timeout`, default 600s, per-call `timeout_seconds` override, persisted across resume). A hung worker becomes a null item instead of stalling the run forever. `cmd.WaitDelay` prevents zombie-pipe wedges
- Run-level `failures` list: every dropped item (agent failure, parallel mapper throw, pipeline stage error — the last was previously swallowed) is persisted and surfaced in `read`/`inspect`/`report`, with a stderr line per drop. Race-free (serialized append+persist)
- Custom-provider structured output is validated against the schema with one corrective retry (read-only agents only, so side effects can never apply twice), closing the prose-leak gap vs codex's native `--output-schema`
- Real usage accounting: providers can report tokens/cost via `PALLIUM_WORKFLOW_USAGE_FILE`; reported cost feeds the budget, accumulated correctly across retries

**Never misclassify:**
- Typed sentinel errors + recorded fatal cause replace all `strings.Contains` control flow; interrupt rethrows carry a run-scoped sentinel token, so a script that rewraps an error can no longer turn a clean stop into a budget exhaustion (or vice versa)
- `currentPhase`/capture data race fixed (stabilizes resume cache keys); suite passes `-race`
- `stripMeta` uses a brace-depth scan, so nested objects in `meta` no longer break valid scripts
- Resume warns on stderr and flags `script_changed` when the script hash differs from the original run

**Never leak, never lose work:**
- Edit-agent worktrees are removed after patch capture (patch is the durable artifact); `pallium workflow gc` reclaims old terminal run artifacts (`--older-than`, `--dry-run`; failed runs kept unless `--include-failed`)
- `verify.untilGreen` redesigned to actually compose: check and fix agents share one loop worktree so fix rounds are visible to subsequent checks; the combined patch is captured incrementally after every fix round and restored on resume, so interruption can never silently lose fix edits or register an empty patch; lazy worktree creation means an already-green check needs no git repo at all
- `isolation: "none"` is rejected at the script boundary (it would have let script agents edit the live repo with no worktree or patch)

## Review

An 8-angle high-effort review with per-candidate adversarial verification ran on the initial implementation and confirmed 1 P0 (untilGreen resume data loss) and 7 P1s; all were repaired with regression tests in the final commit, plus targeted P2 cleanups.

## Verification

- All 11 packages `go test ./... -count=1` green; `internal/workflow` green under `-race`
- `go build`, `go vet`, gofmt clean
- End-to-end parity proof: the failure-semantics script that previously killed the run now completes with per-contract nulls and a populated `failures` list, matching documented Ultracode semantics

Captured requests carry real staging JWTs with a ~24h expiry; replayed against the local service (same demo JWT secret) they authenticate, but a pull left overnight would 401. `refresh-tokens.py` re-signs each bearer with the same claims and a 2030 expiry using the demo secret — the local equivalent of the capture-token blueprint a redacted BYOC replay uses to swap in a live token. author: adev07
body:
## Problem

Another Instagram account running its **own** AI messaged A Colorful Tale, and both bots kept replying to each other **indefinitely**.

**Root cause:** the GENERAL flow has no stop condition — the reply-limit check explicitly exempts GENERAL (`currentFlow !== "GENERAL"`) and `getFlowReply` rotates continuation messages forever. So a GENERAL-classified peer bot ping-pongs with ours. (Professional flows already self-terminate at 4 replies, so they never loop.)

## Fix

An **identity-agnostic velocity guard** in `processAIResponse`. Before generating a reply, count our assistant messages sent in the last `LOOP_GUARD_WINDOW_MS` (5 min). If we've already sent `>= LOOP_GUARD_MAX_REPLIES` (15), tag the conversation `LOOP_GUARD_TRIPPED`, persist, and send nothing.

## Why it's safe for real users

- **A loop is infinite; a human plateaus.** A bot-to-bot loop climbs past any ceiling, while a real back-and-forth slows down (read → think → type). A high threshold kills loops while sparing even a fast, chatty fan.
- **It's a pause, not a ban.** Once our replies age out of the 5-min window, the next message is answered normally. No permanent block.
- **No schema migration** — reuses the existing `messages` array and tag system.
- **Visible.** The `LOOP_GUARD_TRIPPED` tag surfaces any trip in the admin view, so the threshold can be tuned if a real user is ever affected.

## Changes

- `config/assistant.ts` — `LOOP_GUARD_WINDOW_MS` / `LOOP_GUARD_MAX_REPLIES` (the two tuning knobs)
- `services/instagram.ts` — `countRecentAssistantReplies` helper + guard in `processAIResponse`
- `types/index.ts` — new `LOOP_GUARD_TRIPPED` tag

## Testing

- `tsc --noEmit` clean
- Counter self-check passed (recent-only counting, empty-conversation → 0)

## Deliberately skipped

- **Blocklist** — would need frontend work; the velocity cap already handles repeat offenders automatically, including fresh accounts.
- **PAUSED status / admin-reopen flow** — the self-healing pause makes it unnecessary.

- **`js/game.js`** — self-defending `st.x = (st.x||0)+…` increments at the existing `attack()` outcome branches (win/loss/draw + the loot-collected branch); a new `tickPlaytime(state)` that accrues **active** play only (ignores >5s gaps so a backgrounded tab / offline time isn't counted); `player.stats` lazily back-filled in `createGame`.
- **`js/actors.js`** — `stats: {}` on `createPlayer` (additive, no VERSION bump).
- **`js/main.js`** — `initStats(state)` + one `tickPlaytime(state)` line on the world tick.

To run locally: `git checkout claude/lifetime-stats && npx serve -l 8123 .`, open `http://localhost:8123`, and click **📊 Chronicle of Deeds**.

author: llfzzz
body:
## Summary

Final full-project audit found a cluster of internal-only, service-to-service write endpoints reachable by any authenticated user through the gateway's per-service `/api/**` catch-all routes:

- **Critical: privilege escalation** — `POST /api/users` upserts a user record including `roles`; externally reachable, it let any rider self-assign `ADMIN`, then refresh their token to gain operator/admin access.
- **Payment bypass** — `POST /api/orders/{id}/pay` marked any order paid with no auth and no payment, bypassing the signed-callback pipeline. The legacy `POST /api/payments/simulations` / `simulate-success` were a second such bypass.
- **Inventory/state tampering** — `POST /api/orders/{id}/timeout` and `POST /api/trips/{id}/seat-locks[/release]` let any user force-cancel orders and tamper with seat inventory.
- **Broken access control** — driver review (`GET /api/drivers/verification-cases`, `POST .../approve|reject`) had no operator check; any rider could view/approve/reject any driver's documents.

**Fix** (concentrated in `GatewaySecurityFilter`, the sole external entry point):
- `isInternalOnlyPath()` returns `404` for external requests to internal-only paths. In-mesh Feign callers use direct `O2O_*_SERVICE_URL` addresses and bypass the gateway, so service-to-service traffic is unaffected.
- `requiresOperator()` now gates the driver-review list and approve/reject; self-service submission stays open to verified drivers.

**Dead-code cleanup**: removed the legacy payment-simulation path (controller/service/repository/command/test) and the now-unused `PaymentSimulation`/`PaymentStatus` domain types (H5 moved to payment intents in S15); removed the dead `POST /api/orders/{id}/timeout` controller method (timeout runs in-process via RabbitMQ consumer + scheduled scan); dropped an identity ternary in `OrderService.markPaid`.

Docs updated: `api-contract.md`, `security.md` (incl. two documented low-severity gaps left as recommendations: order read IDOR, trip-publish identity binding), `architecture.md`, `README.md`, `.env.example`, `AGENTS.md`.

## Test plan

- [x] `./mvnw test` — 177 tests / 15 modules / 0 failures
- [x] `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm build` clean for both frontend apps
- [x] Live verification on the deployed gateway: internal-only paths return 404, driver review is operator-gated (200 vs 403), real login → internal user-creation still assigns `RIDER` server-side
- [ ] Full docker-compose E2E business flow not re-run this session (documented as unverified)

> **Rebased onto `main` after #109 merged.** No overlap with #109 (it touched Lamp3DPreview/geometry/SAM; this branch touches App.tsx and SheetPanel), so every commit is kept as-is.

## Fixes (auto-close on merge)
- **Fixes #112** — Cmd+Shift+Z redo never fired and Caps Lock broke Cmd+Z: handler compared `e.key === 'z'` but Shift/Caps produce `'Z'` (`cd8d599`)
- **Fixes #113** — Smart Pack was invisible to undo: every placement used `skipHistory`, so Cmd+Z reverted the user's previous action instead (`537bf8b`)
- **Fixes #97** — rapid refine clicks dropped the previous prompt point (stale `project` closure; the issue's other items were already fixed by #108) (`351433d`)

## Partial fixes (issues stay open; details in issue comments)
- **Part of #94** — tool shortcuts (V/H/C/M/Esc) fired on both panels at once; `M` could fabricate a default sheet calibration. Now scoped to the hovered panel. Also fixed a stale Delete-handler dep that applied the old symmetry mode (`399b77e`)
- **Part of #96** — pan/marquee/rotation gestures stuck when the pointer was released outside the panel; fixed with pointer capture at gesture start (`20030e1`)
- **Part of #103** — App.tsx hardcoded strings (delete-project confirm, tooltips, mobile menu labels) routed through i18next with English fallbacks; the fr/en keys for these land in #115's `0a12455` (`10f1090`)

## Review follow-ups
- Added the four Smart Pack popover locale keys (`packing`/`smartPack`/`allowRotations`/`startPacking`) to en+fr — the review flagged 14 missing keys, but the other 10 are App.tsx keys already provided by #115, so only these four (owned by this branch's SheetPanel) are added here to avoid a merge collision (`cf8173a`).
- SheetPanel tool shortcuts now compare keys case-insensitively (Caps Lock) and the Stage handles `pointercancel` so a system-cancelled gesture no longer sticks "on" (`e9600c3`).
- The matching ResultPanel fixes (hover-scoping + Caps Lock) were made on #116 (`081c3cf`), since ResultPanel is that branch's file.

## Verification notes
Pointer-capture and undo-granularity behavior can't be exercised headlessly — worth a quick manual pass in `pnpm dev`: release a drag outside the panel, and Cmd+Z after a Smart Pack.

## Summary

To dig into the 91-vs-66 unit count discrepancy, I need to see the *actual* fields MUL returns per unit — specifically whether there's a tech-base, rules-level, or uniqueness flag we're not yet using that could explain the gap. Every attempt to independently inspect MUL's schema or its `Era/FactionEraDetails` browsing page (which seems to power the combined faction+era view shown on MUL's own site) was blocked with a 403, both from this session's sandboxed tools and from general web fetches to third-party sources (Medium, Kaggle, Postman docs). The only thing that can currently reach MUL directly is the user's own browser.

### What this adds
A **"🔍 Inspect raw data"** button next to the catalog unit count. Clicking it dumps the first 5 raw unit records — every field MUL actually returned in the response, not just the subset we currently parse — into a selectable, read-only textarea. This lets real production data be copied out for troubleshooting without needing browser DevTools.

Verified in a headless browser: clicking the button correctly surfaces the full raw JSON of loaded units.
