author: martinbha
body:
Closes #5

## Summary

Adds an NFT auction house hosting both **English** (ascending, highest bid wins) and **Dutch** (descending price, first taker wins) auctions over a single escrow + pull-payment core. Auctions are where Solidity's sharp edges live — weaponizable ETH refunds, timestamp-based price curves, custody — and this is built to confront each one head-on.

## What was added

### Contracts — `src/auctions/`

- **`AuctionableNFT.sol`** — minimal ERC721 with a public mint, something to auction.
- **`AuctionHouse.sol`** — both auction types:
  - **Pull over push payments** (the load-bearing decision): an outbid bidder is *credited* a withdrawable balance, never refunded inline. Inline refunds would let a contract that reverts on receive permanently block anyone from outbidding it (the King of the Ether bug). Sellers and outbid bidders call `withdraw()`.
  - **English**: `bid` requires the reserve, then `MIN_INCREMENT` over the standing bid; a 15-minute anti-snipe window extends the end if a bid lands in the closing moments; `settleEnglish` awards the winner or returns the NFT to the seller if there were no bids.
  - **Dutch**: `currentPrice` decays linearly from `startPrice` to `floorPrice` and clamps there; `buy` lets the first taker win at/above the current price, refunding overpayment pull-style.
  - Checks-effects-interactions plus a `nonReentrant` guard throughout; NFTs escrowed on create, `cancelAuction` lets a seller reclaim a no-bid auction.

### Tests — `test/auctions/` (19, all passing)

- English: highest bidder wins and seller is paid; below-reserve and below-increment bids revert; late bid extends the deadline; settle-before-end reverts; no-bid returns the NFT
- **Malicious bidder**: a contract that reverts on receiving ETH holds the high bid, and another bidder still outbids it cleanly — proving pull payments defeat the refund-blocking attack
- Dutch: price decays linearly and clamps at floor; buy at current price wins; overpayment refunded; second buyer reverts; invalid price range rejected
- Cross-kind guards (can't `bid` on Dutch or `buy` English)
- **Solvency invariant**: a handler drove 128,000 random calls (create/bid/buy/settle/withdraw/warp across 4 actors, 0 reverts); the house's ETH balance never drifts from `withdrawable balances + standing English bids` — i.e. ETH is never created or destroyed

### Deployment — `script/auctions/` + `utils/auctions/`

`deploy_auctions.sh` deploys the house + NFT, opens one auction of each kind, then runs a full English auction between Anvil accounts (bid → outbid → warp past end → settle → withdraw) and verifies NFT ownership, seller proceeds, the outbid refund, and that the Dutch price decayed to its floor.

## How to test

```bash
forge test                          # 86 tests repo-wide, all passing

anvil                               # terminal 1
./utils/auctions/deploy_auctions.sh # terminal 2 — full English auction + 5 PASS checks
```

## Notes

- The invariant test runs ~2 minutes locally due to the call depth; it's the most valuable test here, so it's kept at full strength.
- Stretch goals from the issue (ERC20-denominated bids, sealed-bid Vickrey via commit-reveal) are left as follow-ups.

author: barrycosta
body:
Fixes #108.

## Problem
Clicking a numbered map marker no longer scrolled to / highlighted its card — broken on both the Explore page and the Nearby section (both use the shared `Map`).

## Cause
`ScrollWheelToggle` (the "click map to enable scroll" overlay, #31) rendered a full-map transparent `<div>` at `z-index: 400` with `pointer-events: auto` while scroll-zoom was inactive (the default; resets on mouseout). It sat above the markers and ate the click, so `onMarkerClick` → scroll-to-card + highlight never fired.

## Fix
Enable scroll-wheel zoom via Leaflet **map events** (`click` enables, `mouseout` disables) instead of a click-catching overlay. In Leaflet a marker click does not propagate to the map `click`, so numbered-marker clicks reach their handler again while clicking the empty map still activates scroll zoom. The hover hint is kept but is now `pointer-events: none` so it can never block clicks.

## Verified
Marker click → scroll-to-card + highlight works on Explore and the Nearby section; scroll-wheel zoom still activates on map click; page scroll resumes on mouse-out.

author: michaelsaucier
body:
## Summary

Closes transpara-ai/hive#250.

This PR adds a fail-closed review-capacity throttle before issue-scan work-start. The guard reads open PRs for the scoped Transpara-AI repos, treats open PRs as conservative unproven exact-head review load, and refuses new issue-scan work when the count is at or above the configured threshold.

## Implementation

- Adds operator-facing defaults of `3` for `factory scan-issues --review-queue-threshold` and daemon `--issue-scan-review-queue-threshold`.
- Runs the throttle before GitHub issue listing and before `QueueIssueScanRunLaunch`.
- Fails closed when the PR queue cannot be read or returns malformed state.
- Records at-capacity refusals as `hive.issuescan.review.capacity.throttled` in the configured Hive store context.
- Adds the design/evidence contract at `docs/designs/review-capacity-throttle-v0.1.0.md` and links it from `docs/OPERATOR.md`.

## Conservative Queue Semantics

The implementation counts all open PRs in the scoped repos. This intentionally over-approximates agent-authored PRs awaiting exact-head human review because `gh pr list` proves open PR existence but does not prove the current exact head has accepted human approval. Over-throttling is the safe direction because the guard can only prevent new work-start.

## Validation

- `gh pr list --repo transpara-ai/hive --state open --limit 1 --json number,title,url,headRefOid,isDraft,reviewDecision,mergeStateStatus,author`
- `go test ./cmd/hive -run 'ReviewCapacity|ReviewQueue|GHReviewQueue|ParseGitHubReviewQueue|FactoryScanIssuesRejectsNonPRReady|RunIssueScanScannerCycle' -count=1`
- `go test ./cmd/hive ./pkg/hive -count=1`
- `go test ./... -count=1`
- `go vet ./...`
- `git diff --check`
- GitHub CI `Build & Test`: passed

## Governance Status

- IADA: passed, PR comment `4907060644`
- CFADA: passed, PR comment `4907059142`
- IAR: passed, PR comment `4907086507`
- Draft-state CFAR: passed, PR comment `4907087893`
- Ready-state CFAR: passed, PR comment `4907110620`
- `cross-family-adversarial-review` status: success on exact head `a88a6a8a2935226bc94cd7a529ab33ae1259be1e`
- Human exact-head merge approval: not yet provided

## Non-Authorizations

This PR does not authorize RuntimeBroker execution, external adapter invocation, production EventGraph writes, Hive wake/start/action API use, label mutation, issue mutation outside normal PR closing semantics after merge, PR approval, PR merge, deploy, service restart, private fetch, protected settings changes, Test 001 GREEN, production go-live, value allocation, autonomy increase, or wiki work.

author: oaleffemanuel
body:
## Escopo por sede (unidade) na Saída de Alunos

Coordenação passa a ver e atuar **apenas na própria sede**:
- `infantil_coordination` → só **Sede Infantil**
- `fundamental_coordination` → só **Sede Fundamental**
- **Recepção, suporte e admin** continuam vendo **todas** as sedes (a porta de entrada única).

### Servidor (`scripts/checkout-pg-server.js`) — a fronteira real
- `COORD_SEGMENT` mapeia papel → segment.
- `/api/checkout/board` e `/api/checkout/classes` filtram por `segment` para papéis de coordenação.
- `/api/checkout/transition` retorna **403** se a coordenação tentar agir em aluno de **outra** sede (vale até via API direta).

### Segurança / propriedade-chave
- Aluno **sem `segment` (NULL)** fica **visível a todos** e continua acionável — uma etiqueta de sede faltando **nunca esconde uma criança** do painel.
- Pré-check em produção: 209 Infantil, 176 Fundamental, **0 sem etiqueta**.

### Cliente (`src/pages/StudentCheckoutPage.jsx`)
- `campus` travado na sede do papel + selo somente-leitura "Sede: …".

### Não alterado
Máquina de estados, regras papel-por-status, logs, reset — intactos. 2 arquivos, +37/−3.

### Rollout
`git pull` → `npm run build` → `pm2 restart veritus-checkout` + `veritus-web`. Verificação por papel + teste de 403 cross-sede via API.

author: guillaume-flambard
body:
## Prod hotfix — strayeye.com down after rebuild

Every `/weave-api/*` call 500s after rebuilding the web image. The freshly-pulled, stricter undici rejects the forwarded `connection` header:

```
Error [InvalidArgumentError]: invalid connection header (UND_ERR_INVALID_ARG)
  at proxy (app/weave-api/[...path]/route.ts)
```

The `HOP_BY_HOP` set was only applied to *response* headers. This applies it to the *forwarded request* headers too, so hop-by-hop headers (`connection`, `keep-alive`, `transfer-encoding`, …) are stripped before `fetch`.

Site loads (200); API proxy was 500 on all paths. One-line fix, no behavior change beyond RFC-correct header handling.

author: mfazekas
body:
Setting an optional RiveView prop back to `undefined` (e.g. `artboardName` from a string to no value) threw `Exception in HostFunction: RiveView.artboardName: Value is null, expected a String` during React commit. Fabric's prop diff sends `null` (not `undefined`) when a prop is removed, and Nitro's `JSIConverter<std::optional<T>>` only maps `undefined` to `nullopt`, so the inner converter throws. This affects all seven optional props (`artboardName`, `stateMachineName`, `autoPlay`, `alignment`, `fit`, `layoutScaleFactor`, `dataBind`) and both Android backends — the generated prop parser is shared C++, so iOS is affected the same way.

The fix extends `scripts/nitrogen-postprocess.ts` to patch the generated `HybridRiveViewComponent.cpp`, treating `null` like `undefined` at the optional-prop parse sites. This is a workaround until it's fixed upstream in Nitro (mrousavy/nitro#1184, open fix PR mrousavy/nitro#1189); the postprocess step already runs as part of `yarn nitrogen`, so regeneration keeps the fix.

Includes a reproducer page (`example/src/reproducers/OptionalPropClear.tsx`) that sets each optional prop and then clears it: it failed 7/7 before the fix and passes 7/7 after, verified on the Android emulator with both the new and the legacy (`USE_RIVE_LEGACY=true`) backend.

author: mkoek213
body:
## Summary

Daily mBank notification emails only carry transfers, so card and shop purchases (Żabka, Biedronka, Lidl, Orlen, restaurants, online) never reached the app - spending looked like transfers only. mBank sends a monthly "elektroniczne zestawienie operacji" PDF that lists every operation. This parses those statements and makes them the authoritative source of truth for their period, and classifies every imported transaction with the local LLM.

## What changed

- **Statement PDF parser** (`src/domain/imports/mbank-statement-parser.ts`): opens the password-protected attachment (`MBANK_STATEMENT_PDF_PASSWORD`), reads the operations table by text geometry, and extracts booking date, card transaction date (`DATA TRANSAKCJI`, used as the operation date), type, merchant, amount and running balance. It validates every statement against its own summary (credit/debit counts and totals) and the full opening-to-closing balance chain, and refuses to import anything that does not reconcile to the grosz.
- **Gmail adapter** can now fetch PDF attachments through the read-only Gmail API.
- **Pipeline**: sync detects statement emails and routes them to the PDF parser. A confirmed statement owns its whole month and replaces any transactions already booked in that period (daily-notification imports or a re-imported copy of the statement), deduplicated deterministically by booking date. Daily notifications for a period an imported statement already covers are skipped rather than queued.
- **LLM categorization** (`src/domain/imports/llm-categorizer.ts`): during import each parsed transaction is classified by the local model (gemma3 via Ollama), batched to keep prompts inside the small context window and constrained to the existing category taxonomy. Answers are validated against the taxonomy (key or Polish label); the deterministic keyword parser's category is kept as the per-row fallback whenever the model is unavailable, returns invalid JSON, or omits a row - so categorization never fails an import. Suggestions appear in the review UI before the user confirms. The categorizer is injected into `syncMbankGmail` so tests stay offline.
- **UI**: transactions carry a `STATEMENT` source and are labeled accordingly; import cards show the statement period; category keywords broadened (grocery chains, fuel, fast food, transit, insurance) with person-vs-company transfer detection for statement rows, used as the fallback.

Adds a Prisma migration (statement provider/source, batch period range), an anonymized statement-rows fixture (no raw data in the repo), and tests for parsing, summary validation, the supersede/skip dedupe, and LLM categorization (answer applied, label mapping, deterministic fallback).

## Notes and limitations

- The current month shows transfers only until its statement arrives (early the next month); mBank only puts card operations in the monthly PDF. Every closed month is complete once its statement is imported.
- LLM categorization runs on the local CPU model, so a full statement (~90 transactions) adds roughly a few minutes to the Sync it belongs to; a smaller/faster or hosted model would cut that down. gemma3:4b gets grocery/fuel/subscription merchants right after prompt tuning but still makes occasional mistakes (e.g. an incoming personal transfer read as income), which the review UI lets you correct before confirming.

## Test plan

- `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm test` (28 tests), `npm run build` all pass.
- Verified end to end against the real mailbox: imported the April, May and June statements. June's 11 daily transfers were superseded with no double-counting; card purchases now appear categorized; the Overview cashflow chart populates for April-June; redundant daily batches are marked "Covered by an imported monthly statement". LLM categorization verified against the real gemma3:4b on a statement sample (correctly reclassifying e.g. Prime Video and Apple to subscriptions, Koleo to transport).

author: mathpirate
body: Deno's coverage emits one record per module **instance** — the same file appears plain and as `?testRun=` once per importing test file — and `parseLcov` keyed records on the raw `SF:` path. The same physical line therefore counted as debt once per instance that didn't execute it, which made the coverage-debt ratchet structurally noisy: - the metric **flapped ±1–5 lines** run-to-run on unchanged code (baselines carry n=2 samples after main moves, so one flap trips the gate); - changes that move execution timing (e.g. eager→lazy deferral) **reshuffled the count with zero real coverage change** — verified from CI's own lcov artifacts, line-shift-adjusted against base runs, on both #4557 and #4560; - **adding a test file could *increase* "uncovered lines"** — its fresh instances carry red lines for whatever they don't execute (observed +3 from adding a test whose target module measured 100% covered). CT-1861 carries the full three-PR evidence trail from 2026-07-06/07. **Fix:** strip the query suffix before keying, so instances of the same physical file merge and a line counts covered when **any** instance executed it — the metric measures real per-file coverage. Unit test pins the merge semantics (three instances, hits summed, only the line no instance executed counts uncovered). **Transition:** no flag day. This PR's own gate computes merged (lower) values against old-style baselines — large apparent reductions — and post-merge main runs re-baseline downward once; subsequent PRs compare consistently. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes coverage-debt noise by merging Deno’s per-instance LCOV records into a single per-file profile, preventing flapping and false increases when adding tests. Addresses CT-1861. - **Bug Fixes** - Normalize instance suffixes at LCOV generation via `normalizeLcovInstancePaths` in `write-coverage-lcov.ts`, applied in both the CI artifact writer and local `lcovFromCoverageProfile`; all consumers (e.g. IDE report) now see one record per physical file, and `parseLcov` simply accumulates duplicate `SF:` sections. - Add a unit test that exercises normalize → parse and pins uncovered-line calculation. - **Migration** - No action needed. The gate already compares merged values to old baselines; main will re-baseline lower once after merge. Written for commit d2b74a693034e7c9ed6c6591a7576e8ec4fdeb87. Summary will update on new commits.

### Motivation
- Fornecer uma visão final segura e automatizada da prontidão NFC-e antes de ativar clientes reais, centralizando checks de configuração, homologação e segurança.
- Evitar exposição de segredos e garantir que o diagnóstico use exclusivamente `actor.storeId` em vez de aceitar `storeId` do frontend.
- Complementar a tela Focus/Fiscal com um bloco visual de Go-Live que não altera regras fiscais nem fluxos de pedido.

### Description
- Adiciona endpoint seguro `GET /api/fiscal/go-live-checklist` protegido por autenticação, `requireRole("max_control")`, `requireStoreFeature("fiscal")` e escopo via `actor.storeId`, retornando somente flags, status e mensagens seguras (não retorna tokens, CSC, certificado, senha ou payload fiscal completo). (arquivo: `artifacts/api-server/src/routes/fiscal-focus.ts`)
- Implementa checks mínimos solicitados (FISCAL_FEATURE_ACTIVE, FISCAL_CONFIG_READY, FOCUS_CONFIG_READY, CERTIFICATE_READY, CSC_READY, HOMOLOGATION_AUTHORIZED_DOCUMENT_EXISTS, PRODUCTION_READY_OR_BLOCKED_SAFELY, SIMPLE_ORDER_PAYLOAD_READY, MULTISABOR_PAYLOAD_READY, DELIVERY_FEE_PAYLOAD_READY, EXTERNAL_PAYMENT_PAYLOAD_READY, CANCELLATION_AVAILABLE, INUTILIZATION_AVAILABLE, SECRETS_NOT_EXPOSED, STORE_SCOPE_ENFORCED) e produz resumo/arrays `checks`, `blockingIssues` e `warnings`.
- Adiciona bloco visual "Go-Live Fiscal" em Focus/Fiscal com cartões de checks, indicadores coloridos, bloqueios críticos, avisos e botão "Atualizar checklist" sem substituir o checklist fiscal atual (arquivo: `artifacts/restaurant-pdv/src/pages/fiscal-focus.tsx`).
- Acrescenta testes contratuais para garantir proteção do endpoint, escopo de loja, não exposição de segredos, existência de documentação de homologação autorizada e renderização frontend (arquivo: `artifacts/api-server/src/routes/__tests__/fiscal-go-live-checklist.test.ts`).
- Inclui documentação operacional `docs/fiscal-go-live.md` com passo a passo de homologação controlada, cenários de teste e checklist de segurança.
- Não foram criadas migrations neste PR e nenhuma regra fiscal, criação de pedido, cálculo de preço, fluxos de caixa/pagamento, cozinha, Multisabor, taxa de entrega ou integrações externas foram alterados.

Points at the **dev** environment: `api_token: GARNET_API_TOKEN_DEV`, `api_url: https://dev-api.garnet.ai`. 2. **`.github/workflows/garnet-openclaw-ci.yml`** — new lightweight companion workflow that runs on `pull_request` + `workflow_dispatch`, checks out, invokes `garnet-org/action@v2`, does a `pnpm install --ignore-scripts` + `pnpm list`, and emits a 30s heartbeat so Jibril's post-step gets a meaningful profile even if heavier jobs skip. ### Why the companion workflow The Mantis smoke workflow depends on many external secrets (Crabbox, Convex, OpenAI, Mantis App private key) that are not present in this fork. Those runs will halt at the "require secrets" step, but Garnet will still have instrumented the runner up to that point. The companion workflow guarantees at least one fully green, signal-rich Garnet profile from this PR so we have a clean e2e verification target. ### Expected Garnet touchpoints - [ ] `garnet-openclaw-ci.yml` fires automatically on this PR - [ ] Job logs contain: `Created agent with ID: ` - [ ] Job logs contain: `stopping jibril service` - [ ] Job logs contain: `profiler markdown written to job summary` - [ ] Run Profile URL appears on [dev-api.garnet.ai](https://dev-api.garnet.ai) keyed by `GITHUB_RUN_ID` - [ ] `garnet-platform-dev[bot]` posts a "Garnet Runtime Review" tree-format comment on this PR - [ ] No duplicate comment from `github-actions[bot]` (dedup working) ### Not in scope - No modifications to Mantis harness logic beyond the Garnet step. - No new secrets pushed to the repo. - No cross-fork or upstream mutations. ---

author: hydrahive
body:
## Warum
Ein frischer Core-Clone (ohne das separate `hydrahive2-modules`-Repo) bricht bei der normalen Installation (`npm run build`) mit:
```
src/features/themetemplates/registry.tsx:17:29 - error TS2307:
Cannot find module '@/modules/atelier/AtelierPage'
```

## Ursache
`themetemplates/registry.tsx` importierte `AtelierPage` **hart statisch** aus dem Atelier-**Modul** und umging damit den optionalen Modul-Mechanismus (`gen-modules`). Der Core konnte so nie ohne Module bauen.

Tückisch: **`tsc --noEmit` (CI) tolerierte** den fehlenden Import, **`tsc -b` (Installer via `npm run build`) nicht** → CI war grün, die echte Installation rot. Deshalb fiel es erst beim Aufsetzen eines Testservers auf.

## Fix (nutzt das bestehende optionale Muster wie `buddyWidgets`/`workspaceTabs`)
- `gen-modules.mjs`: sammelt zusätzlich `moduleSlotBlocks` aus den installierten Modulen.
- `registry.tsx`: harter `AtelierPage`-Import entfernt; stattdessen `...(moduleSlotBlocks as SlotBlock[])` an die `SLOT_BLOCKS`-Liste angehängt.
- Der Atelier-Slotblock wird jetzt vom **Modul selbst** exportiert (`slotBlocks` in `hydrahive2-modules/atelier`, bereits gepusht).

## Verhalten
- **Ohne Module**: `moduleSlotBlocks = []` → Build grün (Bug behoben).
- **Mit Modul**: Atelier-Baustein voll vorhanden — **es fällt nichts weg**.

## Verifiziert
- `npm run build` mit **0 Modulen** → `✓ built`, exit 0 (exakte Repro von Tills Fehler).
- `npm run build`/`tsc -b` **mit** Atelier-Modul → exit 0, Atelier-Baustein funktioniert.

## Nicht in Scope
Kein Verhalten geändert außer der Modul-Entkopplung. Der Fix gehört zusammen mit dem Modul-Commit `atelier: slotBlocks-Export` (modules-Repo, main).

author: sds
body:
## Summary

This PR contains a fix for the validator config inconsistencies observed after running `tempo regenesis` with a different validator set than the cached block-0 database was initialized with.

- Changes `tempo regenesis --sync-validator-config-v2` from a hashed-storage-only overlay to a full synced-account block-0 state replacement.
- Rebuilds synced genesis account replacements from the new chain spec allocation.
- Rewrites `HashedAccounts` and wipes `HashedStorages` for the synced accounts.
- Updates RocksDB account/storage history for the synced accounts and removes stale storage history for old slots.
- Rebuilds block-0 static account/storage change-set segments while preserving unrelated bloat entries.
- Supports growing or shrinking ValidatorConfigV2 regardless of the initial validator config used to create the cached database.
- Logs when the recomputed synced state root differs from the `--chain` genesis root, preserving existing bloat-aware regenesis header behavior.

>[!NOTE]
>We switched from an entirely in-memory implementation to a streaming implementation since 100GiB bloat files would OOM. See [specific commit for details](https://github.com/tempoxyz/tempo/pull/6745/commits/7833b9133dec8b3373f213be9ce07056fc2a227d).

### Why does the issue occur?
The issue with the previous regenesis implementation is it:
- Does not fully replace the account’s block-0 footprint.
- Does not rebuild block-0 static account/storage changesets.
- Does not update RocksDB account/storage history indexes for newly added slots.
- Does not clean stale history when shrinking.

This leads to a non-deterministic crash because different code paths read state differently:
- “latest” reads could see the new ValidatorConfigV2 slots.
- finalized/block-hash/historical reads could classify some new slots as never written and return zero/default records.
- validatorByPublicKey for validators beyond the original 5 could therefore return ValidatorNotFound.

The crash happens when consensus peer resolution reconstructs DKG peers from ValidatorConfigV2:
- the DKG peer set contains a validator public key.
- the historical/block-hash ValidatorConfigV2 read cannot find that validator.
- consensus hits the invariant: DKG peers must exist in the validator config contract.
- node shuts down with ValidatorNotFound.

## Appendix

**Old Behavior**
Before this branch, regenesis did roughly this for synced accounts:

1. Read the target account storage from the new `--chain` genesis alloc.
2. Hash the storage slots.
3. Replace entries in `HashedStorages`.
4. Recompute/write trie updates.

That old implementation is visible in `origin/main`: it only built `overlay_storages`, called `replace_hashed_storage`, and wrote trie updates.

That was enough for some “latest state” paths, but not enough for historical reads. Historical/block-hash state in Reth does not depend only on `HashedStorages`; it also relies on account/storage history indexes and block changesets.

So after changing from, say, 5 validators to more validators:

1. New ValidatorConfigV2 slots might exist in current hashed storage.
2. But block-0 history might not say those slots were created at block 0.
3. Historical reads at the genesis/block hash could treat those slots as never written.
4. `validator_by_public_key` reads `pubkey_to_index[pubkey]`; if that historical slot comes back zero, it returns `ValidatorNotFound`.
5. Consensus then hits the invariant in [crates/consensus/src/peer_manager/actor.rs](crates/consensus/src/peer_manager/actor.rs:421): DKG peers must be present in ValidatorConfigV2.

That matches the PR description.

**What This PR Changes**
The new path starts in [bin/tempo/src/regenesis.rs](bin/tempo/src/regenesis.rs:199). Instead of “sync storage,” it now does “sync account state.”

Step by step:

1. It selects synced accounts.
   `--sync-validator-config-v2` adds `VALIDATOR_CONFIG_V2_ADDRESS` to the sync set. This part was already conceptually present, but now the replacement is fuller.

2. It rebuilds each synced account from the new chain spec allocation.
   `genesis_account_replacement` pulls account nonce, balance, bytecode, raw storage, hashed address, and hashed storage from the new genesis alloc.

3. It recomputes the post-state overlay using both account info and storage.
   The old code only overlaid storage. The new code includes `HashedAccounts` too, so the account’s full genesis footprint is represented.

4. It writes current-state tables.
   It updates `Bytecodes`, `HashedAccounts`, wipes old `HashedStorages` for the account, and inserts only the new nonzero slots. This handles both growing and shrinking ValidatorConfigV2.

5. It writes trie updates.
   This keeps the trie consistent with the replaced account/storage state.

6. It rebuilds block-0 static account/storage changesets.
   This is the key historical-read fix. The code deletes and recreates the account/storage changeset static-file segments, preserving unrelated entries while replacing entries for synced accounts. See [regenesis.rs](/Users/x/src/tempo/tempo/bin/tempo/src/regenesis.rs:406).

7. It updates RocksDB history indexes.
   [regenesis.rs](/Users/x/src/tempo/tempo/bin/tempo/src/regenesis.rs:366) rewrites `AccountsHistory`, deletes stale `StoragesHistory` keys for old slots, and writes history entries for the new slots at block 0.

8. It streams old static changesets instead of loading them all.
   That is the second commit’s point: preserve unrelated bloat entries without OOMing on huge bloat files.

**Why That Solves It**
Consensus reads ValidatorConfigV2 at a block hash through [read_validator_config_at_block_hash](crates/consensus/src/validators.rs:143). That path uses historical state, not just latest state.

After this PR, the synced ValidatorConfigV2 account is coherent in:

- current hashed account/storage tables
- trie updates
- block-0 account changesets
- block-0 storage changesets
- account history indexes
- storage history indexes

That means when consensus asks historical state for `pubkey_to_index`, validator records, active validator indexes, ingress, and egress, those reads should see the same genesis ValidatorConfigV2 layout that latest reads see. Validators added beyond the original cached DB size now have block-0 history, and validators removed from the new config do not leave stale storage/history behind.

Caveat: this does not recreate a DKG outcome. It assumes the new chain spec/header DKG outcome and the new ValidatorConfigV2 genesis storage are already consistent. The branch fixes the DB representation so historical reads can find the validators that should already be there.

author: bniladridas
body:
## Problem

`mac_alias` v2.2.3 uses 32-bit `I` format for CNID path entries. APFS on macOS 15 uses 64-bit inode numbers, causing `struct.pack` to fail during `.DS_Store` alias generation.

## Fix

- Patch `alias.py` in `package.sh` after pip install: replace `I` with `Q` format and `length // 4` with `length // 8`
- Clear `__pycache__` after patching to avoid stale bytecode

Previously patched manually in dev venv; this makes CI work too.

<!-- PhenoSage PR template. Keep PRs small and bounded. -->

## Outcome

Full 8-category audit of the repo; app code came back clean, so this PR fixes the concentrated findings: `pnpm run validate` was red on main (unpinned `supabase/setup-cli`), CI ran only 3 of the 8 canonical guardrail checks (the gap that let the unpin merge), the next CI run would have gone red on `pip-audit` (three 2026 CVEs on `python-multipart`), and `pnpm audit` now reports **zero advisories** tree-wide.

## Scope

- [x] Single concern; no drive-by refactors
- [x] Affected paths listed below

Affected paths:

```
.github/workflows/db-migrations.yml
.github/workflows/ci.yml
apps/analysis/requirements.txt
package.json
apps/web/package.json
pnpm-lock.yaml
turbo.json
WORKLOG.md
```

## Validation

- [x] `pnpm run validate` — PASS (all 8 checks; was FAILING on `check:action-pins` before this PR)
- [x] `pnpm turbo run type-check lint test` — PASS (1,049 web + 7 shared tests; the two `no output files found` turbo warnings are also gone)
- [x] `pnpm turbo run build` — PASS via `pnpm --filter web build` (12/12 pages)
- [x] `pnpm run security:routes` — PASS (29 routes)
- [x] `ruff check .` + `python -m mypy app/` (0 issues) + `pytest` 149/149 + `pip-audit -r requirements.txt` clean

Also: `pnpm run security:audit` — every step ✓ including `pnpm audit --prod --audit-level=high` (previously ✗).

## Test evidence

No behavior changes, so no new tests; the full existing suites pin the upgrades:

- web: 1,049 tests / 99 files green on the new lockfile (ws 8.21.0, @opentelemetry/core 2.8.x, vite 6.4.3)
- analysis: 149 tests green on python-multipart 0.0.31 + pydantic-settings 2.14.2
- `pip-audit`: "No known vulnerabilities found"
- `pnpm audit`: "No known vulnerabilities found" (prod and dev)

## Observability impact

No impact — no log lines, Sentry categories, or SLIs change. The `@opentelemetry/core` patch bump is within `@vercel/otel`'s supported range; trace propagation behavior is unchanged.

## Architecture & Forbidden Changes

Confirm none of the following were introduced (see `.github/copilot-instructions.md`):

- [x] No browser code calls the analysis service or Supabase service-role APIs directly
- [x] No server-only secrets (`SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `ANALYSIS_SERVICE_*`) leaked to client modules or `NEXT_PUBLIC_*`
- [x] No client component imports from `apps/web/src/lib/server/**`
- [x] No `middleware.ts` or `proxy.ts` added to act as a backend proxy
- [x] No public Supabase Storage bucket for user content
- [x] No edits to previously-committed `supabase/migrations/**` files
- [x] No SQLite, second database, or new microservice introduced

## Affected Boundaries

Tick all that apply:

- [ ] Shared types (`packages/shared`)
- [ ] Supabase migration (`supabase/migrations/**`)
- [ ] Web Route Handler (`apps/web/src/app/api/**`)
- [ ] Server-only module (`apps/web/src/lib/server/**`)
- [ ] Analysis service contract (`apps/analysis/app/models/**`)
- [ ] Env vars / `.env.example`

No contract boundary is touched; `apps/analysis/requirements.txt` changes are patch-level dependency bumps with the pydantic model surface unchanged (mypy + 149 tests green).

## Rollback

How do we revert this safely?

- [x] Pure `git revert` is sufficient
- [ ] Requires migration rollback (describe below)
- [ ] Requires env var rollback (describe below)

```
Each finding is its own commit, so any single fix can be reverted
independently. Note that reverting the requirements.txt commit will
re-break the pip-audit CI gate, and reverting the setup-cli pin will
re-break check:action-pins.
```

## Details per commit

1. **`fix(ci)` — restore SHA pin on `supabase/setup-cli`** (High). Dependabot #213 replaced the pinned SHA with the bare `@v2` tag in `db-migrations.yml`, a workflow holding `SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN`/`SUPABASE_DB_PASSWORD`. Pinned to the v2.1.1 commit (`3c2f5e2...`), matching the repo's pin style.
2. **`fix(analysis)` — Python CVE patches** (High). `python-multipart` 0.0.29→0.0.31 (CVE-2026-53538/53539/53540) and `pydantic-settings` 2.14.1→2.14.2 (GHSA-4xgf-cpjx-pc3j). `pip-audit` is a blocking CI step, so main's next run would have failed; python-multipart also parses inbound request bodies at runtime.
3. **`fix(deps)` — npm advisories to zero** (High/Medium). Overrides: `ws>=8.21.0` (high DoS, **prod** via `openai`), `@opentelemetry/core>=2.8.0` (unbounded memory in W3C tracecontext parsing — reachable, since the app propagates inbound `traceparent` per #248), plus dev-chain `vite>=6.4.3`, `js-yaml>=4.2.0`, `brace-expansion>=5.0.6`, `@babel/core>=7.29.6`. `vite` also became an explicit web devDependency: vitest 4 declares vite as a peer, and pnpm 9 auto-installed peers don't re-resolve from overrides, which kept 6.4.2 stuck in the lockfile.
4. **`ci` — run the canonical `pnpm run validate` in the guardrails job** (High). The job ran a hand-picked 3-of-8 subset, so `check:action-pins`, `check:code-scanning`, `check:budgets`, `check:server-actions`, and `check:smoke-script` never ran in CI — exactly how finding 1 merged green. One step running the package.json script means the gates can't drift again.
5. **`chore(turbo)`** (Low). `test` task declared `coverage/**` outputs that `vitest run` never writes; now `[]`, killing the two perpetual CI warnings.
6. **`docs(worklog)`** — session handoff entry.

## Held for approval (auth-adjacent, not included)

Six internal routes compare static bearer tokens with plain `!==` while the repo's HMAC verifiers correctly use `timingSafeEqual`: `webhooks/storage/image-uploaded`, `webhooks/auth/user-created`, `internal/diag`, `internal/ready`, `cron/daily-summary`, `cron/reconcile-onboarding`. Proposed fix: a shared `verifyStaticBearer(header, secret)` helper in `apps/web/src/lib/server/` using `timingSafeEqual`, adopted by all six routes (accept/reject semantics unchanged, existing route tests cover both paths). Severity Low — say the word and it lands as a follow-up commit here or a separate PR.

## Follow-ups

- Adopt a timingSafeEqual-based shared helper for static bearer checks on the six internal routes (held for approval — auth-adjacent)

author: rt-rtos
body:
#### Feedback wanted: Long term drift not measured on HW. Do we want a 24h+ A/B drift test as verification?

## Summary

`amy_sysclock()` computes milliseconds-since-start through single-precision
float. That has two correctness problems that show up on long uptimes, plus
avoidable per-callback cost in the sequencer timer path on 32-bit targets.
This PR makes the clock exact integer math and tightens the sequencer's
tick-deadline check. Behavior is otherwise unchanged; the sequencer tick
*rate* is identical.

## Bug 1: the clock wraps at ~24.9 hours at 48 kHz, not 49.7 days

```c
return (uint32_t)((amy_global.total_blocks * AMY_BLOCK_SIZE / (float)AMY_SAMPLE_RATE) * 1000);
```

`total_blocks` is `uint32_t` and `AMY_BLOCK_SIZE` is an int constant, so
`total_blocks * AMY_BLOCK_SIZE` is computed in 32-bit integer arithmetic and
wraps at 2^32 *samples* - 89478 s (24.85 h) at 48 kHz, ~27 h at 44.1 kHz -
before the float conversion ever sees it. The comment ("uint32_t rollover is
49.7 days") describes the intended ms-domain wrap; the actual wrap comes ~48x
sooner. When it hits, the clock jumps back to near zero, and the sequencer's
1-second catch-up guard re-anchors: pending absolute-tick events are
re-evaluated against a clock that went backwards.

## Bug 2: float precision quantizes the clock as uptime grows

The sample count passes through `float` (24-bit mantissa). Once total samples
exceed 2^24 (~6 min at 48 kHz) the conversion is no longer exact, and the
error grows with uptime. Measured with the test program below (48 kHz,
256-sample blocks): by 12 h of uptime the returned clock advances in 8 ms
jumps, while the true per-block step is 5.33 ms. Everything slaved to
`amy_sysclock()` - most importantly the sequencer, i.e. every scheduled
event - inherits that granularity.

## Fix

```c
uint32_t amy_sysclock() {
    // Time is returned in integer milliseconds; wraps at 2^32 ms = 49.7 days.
    // Integer math: computing this through float quantizes the clock once
    // total samples exceed the 24-bit mantissa (~6 min at 48 kHz), and the
    // u32 samples-domain multiply wrapped after 2^32 samples (~25 h).
    return (uint32_t)(((uint64_t)amy_global.total_blocks * (AMY_BLOCK_SIZE * 1000u)) / AMY_SAMPLE_RATE);
}
```

Exact for the full `total_blocks` range (verified against 128-bit reference
math: zero mismatches over the sampled u32 range including the wrap
boundary), monotonic, and the u32 result now genuinely wraps at 2^32 ms =
49.7 days as the original comment intended.

## Sequencer: compare tick deadlines in the us domain

`sequencer_check_and_fill()` ran, per check:

```c
while(amy_sysclock() >= (uint32_t)(amy_global.next_amy_tick_us / 1000L)) {
```

That is a second `amy_sysclock()` call plus a 64-bit divide per loop-condition
evaluation. GCC cannot strength-reduce a 64-bit divide by a constant on
32-bit targets, so on ESP32/RP2040/RP2350 the divide is a real `__udivdi3`
libcall executed on every 500 us timer callback. The function already
computes `now_us` at the top; comparing in the us domain removes both:

```c
while(now_us >= amy_global.next_amy_tick_us) {
```

Behavior note: the old compare rounded the tick deadline down to a ms
boundary, so a tick could fire up to 1 ms *early* relative to its us
deadline; now it fires at the first 500 us callback at-or-after the deadline
(up to 1 ms later than before). `next_amy_tick_us` accumulates exactly as
before, so the long-term tick rate is bit-identical. Not re-sampling the
clock inside the catch-up loop is also safe: the existing 1-second skip-ahead
guard already bounds how much catch-up a single callback performs.

## Sequencer: keep tempo math in single precision

`sequencer_recompute()` used unsuffixed double literals:

```c
amy_global.us_per_tick = (uint32_t) (1000000.0 / ((amy_global.tempo/60.0) * (float)AMY_SEQUENCER_PPQ));
```

which promotes the whole expression to double - software-emulated on these
targets (`__extendsfdf2` / `__divdf3` / `__muldf3` / `__fixunsdfsi` in the
disassembly). Algebraically identical single-divide float form:

```c
amy_global.us_per_tick = (uint32_t) (60000000.0f / (amy_global.tempo * (float)AMY_SEQUENCER_PPQ));
```

Cold path (tempo changes only); included for hygiene since it is the same
clock code.

## Measured effect (ESP32-S3, gcc 15.2, -O2 + LTO)

The 2 kHz sequencer timer callback goes from 77 instructions with `__divsf3`
(float divide inside the inlined `amy_sysclock()`) plus `__udivdi3` per
deadline check, to 53 instructions with a single `__udivdi3` (the new
sysclock's divide-by-constant) and no float conversion traffic. Small in

### Motivation
- Prevent unsafe or malformed user-supplied strings from being stored or used in logs and templates by normalizing encoding and stripping HTML/unsafe content.
- Tighten authorization around changes to the `silence_emails` (marketing email suppression) flag to prevent improper toggles by non-privileged actors.
- Avoid unintended external re-invites on email change and ensure external auth/session state is invalidated when a member's email changes.

### Description
- Add a new `SanitizesUserInput` concern that normalizes encoding, strips HTML, and unescapes entities, and include it into `Member`, `Rental`, `RentalSpot`, `SlackUser`, `ToolCheckoutRequest`, `VolunteerEvent`, and `VolunteerTask` to scrub string fields before validation via `before_validation`.
- Add log-scrubbing helpers to `ApplicationController` (`scrub_log_value` and `normalize_log_value`) and use `sanitize` for unsafe `params` logging to avoid logging malformed or unsafe bytes.
- Sanitize Google Drive/HTML email template replacement values in `Service::EmailTemplate` using normalized UTF-8 and `ActionView::Helpers::SanitizeHelper` to avoid injecting raw HTML or broken byte sequences into rendered templates.
- Add and enforce `authorize_silence_emails_change!` logic in `Admin::MembersController` and `MembersController` to restrict who can set/clear `silence_emails` across admin/board/resource_manager/own-account scenarios and to forbid admins from changing this flag for revoked members.
- Prevent reinvites on member email changes by removing `email_changed` subscriber reinvite behavior and add `Member#handle_successful_email_change` to clear `firebase_uid` and rotate `session_token` when an email was changed; update `publish_update` accordingly.

- Update many specs and add new specs for sanitizer behavior, `Service::EmailTemplate` sanitization, `silence_emails` authorization across roles, mailtrap optional tests, and related model/controller behavior.

- Ran the RSpec suite covering updated controller, model, and lib specs including `spec/controllers/*`, `spec/models/*`, and new `spec/lib/service/email_template_spec.rb` and the optional mailtrap specs guarded by `RUN_OPTIONAL_MAILTRAP_SPECS`; all tests passed locally.

author: tmartin2113
body:
MEDIUM finding (M5) from the pre-legal-review attack-vector pass. SQLCipher protects only the SQLite path; in **Postgres/k8s mode — the school/FERPA deploy** — a child's `name` and `birthdate` were cleartext columns at rest.

## Fix
App-layer encryption (deploy-independent), mirroring the `encrypted_email` pattern:
- **`core/profile_manager/field_crypto.py`** — encrypt/decrypt name + birthdate via `encryption_manager` (Fernet); `name_hash` (SHA-256) for the within-family duplicate-name lookup (the plaintext `name` column can no longer be queried); `col()`, a dict/Row/tuple-safe accessor.
- **Schema + migration `0004`** — add `encrypted_name` / `name_hash` / `encrypted_birthdate`; backfill existing rows; redact the plaintext columns (`name` → `"[encrypted]"` placeholder, `birthdate` → NULL). Idempotent.
- **Writes** — `create_profile`, the profile-create route, `update_profile`, **and the admin roster path** (`create_student` / `bulk_import_students` / `admin_update_profile`) encrypt on write; dup-check uses `name_hash`.
- **Reads** — `get_profile`/list decrypt into `ChildProfile`; age-verification decrypts birthdate; **admin lists, the parent crisis-alert path (`escalation.py` / `safety_monitor.py`), and the GDPR data-subject export** decrypt. All fall back to the plaintext column for un-migrated rows during rollout.

## The review earned its keep
This shipped in two commits: the core change, then fixes for sites a dedicated adversarial completeness review found — most importantly the **admin/school-roster writers** (which would have re-introduced plaintext names in the exact deploy M5 targets) and **safety-alert reads** (a parent crisis email would have said "[encrypted] mentioned content related to self-harm").

## Tests
Migration backfills + leaves NO cleartext PII + is idempotent; create→encrypt→decrypt round-trip; dup-name via hash; age-verification tuple-row path. **967 profile/admin/safety/migration/incident tests pass; mypy clean** on all touched files.

author: stan-stani
body: ## What this PR does Adds **Claude Fable** as a first-class usage metric, everywhere Claude Design already appears: the menu-bar pin (short label `F`, pink accent), all three popover layouts, the WidgetKit widget, notifications (Surface + a Settings toggle), the Display and Notifications settings, EN + FR localization, and unit tests. It also updates how per-model weekly quotas are read from the usage API (see **Why**), so Fable — and Sonnet/Opus/Design — resolve on the current API response shape. ## Why Fable deserves parity with the other model satellites. But while wiring it up I found the assumed `seven_day_fable` bucket **doesn't exist** on migrated accounts. Anthropic has moved per-model weekly quotas out of the flat `seven_day_*` keys into the `limits` array, as `weekly_scoped` entries tagged with `scope.model.display_name`: ```json { "kind": "weekly_scoped", "group": "weekly", "percent": 23, "resets_at": "2026-07-08T07:00:00Z", "scope": { "model": { "display_name": "Fable" } }, "is_active": true } ``` On the account I tested, every top-level `seven_day_sonnet` / `seven_day_opus` / `seven_day_cowork` / `seven_day_omelette` bucket was `null`, while the real data lived in `limits[]`. So `UsageResponse` now reads the dedicated `seven_day_*` key **first** and falls back to the matching `limits[]` entry. Old-shape accounts (populated `seven_day_*`, no `limits`) decode exactly as before — the top-level value always wins, so this can only *add* data, never change existing behavior. Like the other satellites, Fable is opt-in: the dashboard tile appears automatically when the bucket is present; the popover ring and the menu-bar pin are toggles. ## How to test 1. `xcodegen generate` 2. Unit tests: `xcodebuild -project TokenEater.xcodeproj -scheme TokenEaterTests -destination 'platform=macOS' -derivedDataPath build CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY="" CODE_SIGNING_REQUIRED=NO test` — **499 tests pass** (incl. new Fable + `limits[]` fallback cases in `FableTests`). 3. Build + run a Release build of `TokenEaterApp`. With an account that has Fable usage, the dashboard shows a **Fable** tile; enable **Show Fable ring** to get the popover ring, and pin **Fable** under Settings → Display to get the menu-bar `F` chip. 4. Verified end-to-end against a live `/api/oauth/usage` response — Fable decoded to **23%** through the real `UsageResponse` model (was `nil` before this change). ## Screenshots / recordings ## Checklist - [x] Tests pass locally - [x] If you changed SwiftUI or the widget, you tested it manually in a Release build - [x] Branch is rebased on the latest `main` --- **Worth flagging:** - The `limits[]` fallback matches on exact (case-insensitive) `scope.model.display_name`. I could verify it against live data **only for Fable** — at capture time Sonnet/Opus/Design had no active `weekly_scoped` entry, so their fallback path is structurally identical but unobserved with real data. Exact match keeps it conservative: it only ever adds a bucket and never misattributes one model's quota to another. - I kept `seven_day_fable` as the primary read for forward-compatibility, even though I never observed it populated in the wild. - New `UsageLimit` model + `weeklyScopedBucket(in:modelNamed:)` are covered by the added `FableTests` cases using the exact live JSON shape.

author: stein155
body:
Security/bug sweep of the LAN web API, the network clients, and the on-device update path. Threat model: anyone on the LAN can hit the (by-design unauthenticated) web API, radio stream URLs and the MQTT broker are attacker-influenced, and the OTA path runs as root.

## Fixed

**High-value**
- **Reflected XSS via the logo/TuneIn proxy** (`internal/web/web.go`): `relay` echoed the upstream `Content-Type` verbatim. A crafted `/api/logo?u=<evil>` where the remote host returns `text/html` + script executed **on the speaker's own origin**, which passes the same-origin CSRF guard and can drive every mutating API (settings, update, presets, volume, grouping). Now the upstream type is kept only when it stays within the expected family (`image/*`, `application/json`), otherwise the safe fallback is used, plus `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`.

**Hardening / correctness**
- **SSRF consistency** (`internal/web/web.go`): the ICY stream client now uses `publicOnlyTransport()` like every other outbound client, so a station URL resolving to loopback/RFC1918 can't be fetched.
- **MQTT handshake could hang forever** (`internal/mqtt/mqtt.go`): the CONNACK read was only bounded when the caller's ctx had a deadline — habridge passes the app-lifetime ctx (none), so a broker that accepts TCP but never replies wedged the bridge until process restart. Now always bounded by a hard deadline.
- **Unbounded goroutine spawn** (`internal/habridge/habridge.go`): every inbound PUBLISH spawned a goroutine + payload copy; a misbehaving broker could OOM the ARMv7 speaker. Concurrent handlers are now capped (excess dropped with a log).
- **IPv6 broker hosts** (`internal/habridge/habridge.go`): use `net.JoinHostPort` instead of string concat.
- **Ignored request-build error** (`internal/speaker/speaker.go`): `get`/`post` discarded the `http.NewRequestWithContext` error, risking a nil-deref in `Do`.
- **Masked scanner error** (`internal/tunein/tunein.go`): `Resolve` now surfaces `bufio.Scanner` errors instead of reporting "no streams".
- **Update path defense-in-depth** (`install/netinstall.sh`): re-validate `RETOUCH_RELEASE_BASE` / `RETOUCH_TARGET_TAG` charset on the device before splicing them into the root download URLs.

## Testing
- `go vet ./...` and `go test ./...` pass (in Docker `golang:1.22-alpine`).
- ARMv7 + amd64 cross-builds succeed.
- `sh -n` on the install scripts passes.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR — larger scope)
The OTA trust chain (install.sh → netinstall.sh → GitHub release) currently rests on TLS-to-GitHub plus a same-origin checksum; ed25519 signing is scaffolded in `release.yml` but dormant. The `beta.yml` workflow builds fork-PR code in a privileged job with a write token. Both are worth hardening separately.

This commit introduces a "Color Family" categorization system to the style simulation pipeline. Instead of selecting individual inventory items as anchors, users now select perceptual color buckets (e.g., "Navy", "Burgundy"), which are automatically mapped from hex codes using CIELAB distance quantization.

- **Perceptual Color System**:
    - Introduced the `ColorFamily` enum defining standard color buckets with associated hex values and display names.
    - Implemented `ColorQuantizer` utility using CIELAB ΔE distance to accurately snap raw hex colors to the nearest `ColorFamily`.
    - Added `ColorFamily` support to `ClothingItem` and `CosmeticItem` domain models and Room entities.
- **Inventory & Repository Updates**:
    - Updated `WardrobeRepository` and `CosmeticInventoryRepository` to automatically quantize and bucket colors during the save/update process.
    - Added Room `TypeConverters` for `ColorFamily` in `FashionConverters`.
- **Simulator UX Refinement**:
    - Redesigned the anchoring UI in `StyleSimulatorScreen` to use `ColorFamilySwatch` components, replacing the individual item horizontal scroll.
    - Updated `StyleSimulatorViewModel` to group inventory by color family and manage family-based constraints for the simulation engine.
    - Enhanced UI components with refined shadows, borders, and polished layouts for the "Visual Identity" and "Anchor" sections.
- **Infrastructure**:

## What this does

Adds an **admin-editable site message** system: a slot registry (`messages.py`) with admin-authored **raw HTML** bodies rendered verbatim, backed by a `site_messages` table in the internal DB.

Slots currently surface in two places:
- **Homepage** — a signed-out sign-in prompt.
- **Login page** — help text.

Also includes the **root bootstrap prompt** (nudges the freshly-installed instance's `root` to set things up), a Svelte **Messages** editor page, and tests.

## Notes for review

- **Raw HTML is intentional and admin-only.** Bodies are authored by admins and rendered verbatim — the trust boundary is "admin can already do anything," so this is not an XSS regression against untrusted input. Worth a look during review to confirm no non-admin path can write a slot.
- New `site_messages` table via internal migration; slot registry keeps the set of valid slots server-side.
- 226 lines of new tests in `tests/test_messages.py`.
- Screenshots: `docs/screenshots/messages.png`, `homepage-message.png`, updated `login.png`.

Closes #5025

## Summary
Implemented the native Z.ai hosted provider adapter for issue #5025. The work adds the `z_ai` provider family, accepted aliases `zai` and `zhipu`, profile `z_ai:glm-5`, provider setup CLI support, runtime adapter routing, provider substrate identity/capability inference, HTTP-family execution, tests, documentation, and a tracked proof note. author: janellycedenoaquino
body:
### What this feature does
Adds a watchlist to CineLog — a list of films a user wants to watch later, separate from their collection of already-watched films. Users can add a film to their watchlist (`POST /watchlist/<user_id>/add`) and view it (`GET /watchlist/<user_id>`). Adding the same film twice is rejected instead of creating a duplicate entry.

### Design decisions
- **Default visibility (`public`):** Changed the default from `True` to `False`. There's currently no way for a user to set this field themselves, so whatever the default is applies to every entry with no user input at all — it should be the option that doesn't expose anything a user didn't choose to share. See Comment 4 above for the full reasoning.
- **Sort order:** Watchlists are now sorted by `date_added` descending (newest first), matching how `get_collection()` already sorts the collection view. See Comment 5 above for the full reasoning.

### How to manually test
1. Seed a user and film via a Python shell (no API endpoint exists for this yet):
   ```python
   from app import create_app, db
   from models import User, Film
   app = create_app()
   with app.app_context():
       user = User(username="testuser", email="test@example.com")
       film = Film(title="Paddington 2", year=2017)
       db.session.add_all([user, film])
       db.session.commit()
       print(user.id, film.id)
   ```
2. With `python app.py` running, add the film to the watchlist:
   ```bash
   curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:5000/watchlist/<user_id>/add \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"film_id": "<film_id>"}'
   ```
3. Repeat the same request — it should be rejected as a duplicate instead of creating a second entry.
4. Run `pytest tests/ -v` to confirm the same behavior automatically.

author: salmartinez-design
body:
Sal: "on the tab the qleno logo is not showing up."

Root cause: the boot readiness gate (#deploy-healthcheck fix, 2026-06-24) 503s **every** path until migrations finish — but the frontend static mount sits *below* it in the middleware chain, so during each deploy's warm-up window `/favicon.svg`, `/assets/*.js`, and `index.html` all return `warming_up` JSON. Chrome caches the failed favicon for the tab, and with seven deploys today a tab was bound to load inside a warm-up window. (Confirmed live: `curl /favicon.svg` during the #940 warm-up returned the warming_up JSON body.)

Static files don't touch the DB, so they're safe during migrations. The gate now passes through anything that isn't `/api/*`; API routes stay held at 503 with Retry-After exactly as before, and `/api/health` + `/api/healthz` remain exempt for Railway's probe.

Verification: boot-readiness suite 8/8 (gate ordering + exemptions asserted there); will probe `/favicon.svg` during this PR's own deploy warm-up to confirm it serves the SVG instead of JSON.

author: alexkroman
body:
## What
Adds `verify_signer()` to `release-lib.sh` and calls it in `release-build.sh` after signing the app bundle and the DMG. It asserts each produced artifact is signed by **exactly** the expected leaf-cert SHA-1 (`640A…`) and Team ID (`Y54ZB9JF63`) — extracting the leaf certificate and fingerprinting it — and `die`s otherwise.

## Why
`codesign --sign <hash>` already selects the cert, but nothing verified the *finished* artifact. A release built or signed on a machine holding any **other** (even otherwise-valid, notarized) Developer ID would previously sail through. This is the "wrong-key release from your own machine" gate: it fails the build closed rather than publishing. `release-publish.sh`'s existing checksum match carries the guarantee through to the uploaded DMG.

Note: this does **not** protect a first-time downloader (that needs a consumer-side verifier / out-of-band trust anchor) — it protects the maintainer's own pipeline from shipping a wrong-key build.

## Verification
`verify_signer` tested against a real signed bundle:
- correct leaf SHA-1 + team → passes
- wrong leaf SHA-1 → fails closed
- wrong team → fails closed

`shellcheck -x` clean; helper is side-effect-free at source time (safe for `release.test.sh`).

body:
## What
Adds a convention to CLAUDE.md: design specs and implementation plans (e.g. `docs/superpowers/specs/`) are local working artifacts. They live on the working branch while work is in flight, get deleted once the work ships, and never reach `main` or a publish commit.

## Why
These docs describe drafting/planning process. Merging or publishing them would expose exactly the kind of work-in-progress the repo's draft-privacy rule keeps private, and they add no value once the work is done.

## Rollback
Revert the commit; docs-only, no CI/deploy impact.

author: polrk
body:
## What

Rewrites **both** the `@ydbjs/topic` writer and reader as deterministic finite-state machines on `@ydbjs/fsm` — each a domain FSM (writer / reader) + a transport FSM wired via `ingest` — consolidates the three writer implementations into one, and deletes the old imperative reader. Both are exported as classes (`TopicWriter` / `TopicReader`, no `Impl` suffix / interface), matching how `coordination` / `query` expose their domain objects. The `topic()` client uses them.

## Why

The writer had two divergent implementations (`writer1` callback-based, `writer2` xstate) plus an experimental `writer3`, each carrying real bugs (uncompressed non-RAW codecs, silent data loss on close, seqNo-renumber-on-reconnect). The reader was a callback-based stream handler that **rejected pending commits on every reconnect**, crashing naive `read()` + `commit()` consumers. A single explicit, testable FSM per side — no framework magic — fixes those and standardizes on `@ydbjs/fsm`. The reader mirrors the writer, so the two are symmetric and share one reconnect policy.

## Changes

**Writer** (`src/writer/`): pure `writerTransition` + `transportTransition`, effect handlers, facade `TopicWriter` class, `ydb:topic.writer.*` diagnostics. Removed `src/writer2/`, the old `writer1`, the `xstate` dependency, and the `./writer2` / `./writer3` subpath exports.

**Reader** (`src/reader/`): pure `readerTransition` + `transportTransition`, effect handlers, facade `TopicReader` class, `ydb:topic.reader.*` diagnostics + a `tracing:ydb:topic.reader.commit` span. Removed the old imperative reader (~19 `_*.ts` modules).

- `commit()` is **never rejected by a transparent reconnect**: pending commits are held per stable `partitionId` and re-sent on the new partition session (confirmed against a live server — YDB accepts a re-sent commit for offsets not read on that session).
- The reader FSM is **tx-agnostic**: read-offset tracking and the `UpdateOffsetsInTransaction` commit live in the facade; send effects carry domain data and the runtime builds the protobuf frames (as the writer already did).

**Shared reconnect policy (writer + reader)**

- Transparent reconnect is **unbounded by default** (waits for the server / topic to come back), matching every other YDB SDK. The new `recoveryWindowMs` option re-imposes a finite terminal deadline; `retryOnSchemeError` (off by default) retries `SCHEME_ERROR` so a client can wait for a not-yet-created topic. The arm/don't-arm decision lives in the FSM, not the runtime effect handler.

**`@ydbjs/fsm` fixes**: a `dispatch()` inside a transition is processed after the state change; `close()` drains events queued during an in-flight drain before sealing; internal-fault propagation to the terminal path.

### Breaking changes (`@ydbjs/topic`, major)

- Writer: `write()` returns `void` (get the last acked seqNo via `flush()` / `onAck`); `flush()` returns `bigint`; removed the `retryConfig` option; removed the `@ydbjs/topic/writer2` subpath; `flushIntervalMs` default 10ms → 1000ms; `close()` now rejects when the graceful drain fails (instead of resolving silently) — important for tx commit integrity.
- Reader `read()` option `waitMs` → **`batchWindowMs`** (`waitMs` kept as a deprecated alias); on an unrecoverable terminal error `read()` now **throws** instead of ending like a clean stream.

### Additions / fixes

- Non-RAW codecs (GZIP/ZSTD) are now actually compressed on the wire.
- New options: `recoveryWindowMs` + `retryOnSchemeError` (reader + writer), `gracefulShutdownTimeoutMs`, `partitionId` / `messageGroupId`; `producer` auto-generated when omitted.
- Structured `node:diagnostics_channel` lifecycle events for both reader and writer; `TopicTxReader` is `Disposable`.

## Testing

- Pure transition unit tests (writer + reader + transport), fake-driver contract tests, an 800-run property model (reader), real-YDB protocol / lifecycle integration tests (incl. the `SCHEME_ERROR` / `retryOnSchemeError` and commit-across-reconnect cases), and the e2e read/write + transaction suites.
- Validated end-to-end under a local SLO chaos stack (graceful-stop / instant-restart / SIGKILL): both writer and reader recover transparently with **0 loss, 0 duplicates**.
- Memory-leak coverage (heap snapshot + FinalizationRegistry) and a `@ydbjs/fsm` re-entrancy/close regression test. Full monorepo build + lint clean; all unit tests green (816).

## Checklist

- [x] Changesets added (`@ydbjs/topic` major writer + reader migration, `@ydbjs/fsm` patches)
- [x] README / docs / examples updated (EN + RU)
- [x] Tests added/updated

author: mhenrixon
body:
## Summary

The final issue in the 0.11 "part-2" API-simplification wave (#181–#185 merged). Four independent public-API edges honed, one instrumentation contract frozen — each a small, sharp knife, none entangled with the others.

| # | Change | Breaking? |
|---|--------|-----------|
| 1 | `reactive_filter` speaks **fields**, not selectors | yes (guided error) |
| 2 | `reply.append`/`prepend` accept **row kwargs** | no (additive) |
| 3 | `transition:` takes **named legs** (Hash) | yes (guided error) |
| 4 | **One registry reader** — the plural frozen hash replaces 7 fetch-one getters | yes (guided errors) |
| 5 | `defer.phlex_reactive` joins the **frozen instrumentation contract** | no (additive) |

### 1. `reactive_filter` speaks fields, not selectors

```ruby
# before                                    # after
reactive_filter(input: "#search",           reactive_filter(:q)   # :q -> [name="q"], scope-aware
  option: "[role=option]")                   #                       option: defaults to [role=option]
```

`reactive_filter(:q)` names the FIELD that drives the filter and compiles it to `[name="q"]` — scope-aware, exactly like `reactive_field` from #184. `option:` now defaults to `[role=option]`; `group:`/`empty:` stay opt-in (emit only when passed). The old selector form raises a guided error. **The client wire is byte-identical** (it still receives selectors) — a server-only compile, no client change.

### 2. Collection rows accept kwargs (non-breaking)

```ruby
reply.append(item, to: :items, autofocus: true)   # autofocus: reaches ItemRow.new(item:, autofocus: true)
```

Extra kwargs thread through to the row component's initializer. Additive — no-kwarg calls are unchanged; `prepend` threads identically.

### 3. `transition:` takes named legs

```ruby
# before                                          # after
js.toggle("#x", transition:                       js.toggle("#x", transition:
  ["fade", "fade-from", "fade-to"])                 { during: "fade", from: "fade-from", to: "fade-to" })
```

Compiles to the same `[during, from, to]` wire array (zero client change). The Array form raises with the caller's values slotted into the named form, so the error teaches the fix.

### 4. One registry reader — the plural frozen hash IS the fetch-one

Seven singular getters removed, each raising a guided error naming the hash form:

| removed | use instead |
|---------|-------------|
| `reactive_action(:x)` | `reactive_actions[:x]` |
| `reactive_action?(:x)` | `reactive_actions.key?(:x)` |
| `reactive_collection_def(:x)` | `reactive_collections[:x]` |
| `reactive_collection?(:x)` | `reactive_collections.key?(:x)` |
| `reactive_compute_def(:x)` | `reactive_computes[:x]` |
| `reactive_compute?(:x)` | `reactive_computes.key?(:x)` |
| `reactive_compute(:x)` (bare GETTER) | `reactive_computes[:x]` |

The resolved registries now come back **FROZEN** — they are the memoized dispatch table, so mutation raises `FrozenError` and can never corrupt default-deny. The `reactive_compute :name, inputs:, outputs:` **SETTER is unchanged** (only the bare-getter overload died). Internal callers (endpoint, deferred-render job, test helpers) migrated to the hash form; the `respond_to?(:reactive_action?)`/`reactive_compute?` reflection guards migrated to `respond_to?(:reactive_actions)`.

### 5. `defer.phlex_reactive` joins the frozen instrumentation contract

A request-spec now drives **all five** defer outcomes (`ok`/`no_content`/`invalid_token`/`not_found`/`unauthorized`), freezing the `{ component:, outcome: }` payload shape — a rename fails CI, the same guarantee `action`/`render`/`broadcast` already have. Documented in the README instrumentation table and the observability section of the performance docs page. The payload carries only the component NAME and the outcome — never the token, params, or state (asserted).

## Test Coverage

- `spec/phlex/reactive/registry_readers_spec.rb` (new, 13) — frozen plural hashes, the 7 guided errors, the compute SETTER stays
- `spec/requests/defer_instrumentation_spec.rb` (new, 6) — all 5 defer outcomes end-to-end, no secrets in the payload
- `spec/dummy/app/components/defer_auth_component.rb` (new) — a defer target that authorizes-on-render, driving the `:unauthorized` outcome
- `component_spec` `#reactive_filter (field-driven)` — compile, scope-awareness, overrides, guided error
- `js_spec` — transition named-legs compile + Array-form guided error
- `collection_streams_spec` — append/prepend row kwargs thread through
- migrated `component_spec` / `component_registry_inheritance_spec` / `collection_spec` / `param_schema_registry_spec` to the hash form

## Verification

- `bundle exec rubocop` — 237 files, 0 offenses
- `bundle exec rspec spec/phlex spec/requests` — 1153 examples, 0 failures
- `bundle exec rake spec:system_servers` — 70 examples, 0 failures under **Puma AND Falcon**
- pgbus optionality untouched (no broadcast-path change)

## Deviations & judgment calls

- **Change 1 — `group:`/`empty:` stay opt-in.** The plan floated convention defaults (`[data-filter-group]`/`[data-filter-empty]`) for all four selectors. But `group:`/`empty:` are OPT-IN today (they emit only when truthy), and always-emitting them would be a wire change that breaks the byte-stable-wire spec and the "omits group/empty" spec. Decision: only `option:` gets a convention default (`[role=option]`, always emitted — it's required); `group:`/`empty:` keep a nil default and emit only when passed. `reactive_filter(:q)` therefore emits `input=[name="q"]` + `option=[role=option]` and nothing else.
- **Change 4 — the `respond_to?` reflection guards had to migrate too.** `reactive_action?`/`reactive_compute?` were used not just as predicates but as `respond_to?(...)` reflection guards (`deferred_render_job.rb`, `actions_controller.rb`) — removing the methods breaks those guards silently. Migrated them to `respond_to?(:reactive_actions)`. `reactive_compute` is a getter/SETTER overload; only the bare-getter path was killed, and `reactive_compute_def` (a documented alias asserted by the inheritance spec) went with the getter — the inheritance-spec alias-equality test was rewritten to the hash form.
- **Change 4 — froze the *merged* result, not just the own-hash.** `Registry#resolve_hash` returned an unfrozen `(inherited).merge(own)`; the freeze goes on the memoized merged value so a subclass's resolved registry is frozen too (inheritance-aware).
- **Consumer migration caught two live stragglers.** The both-server system run surfaced `client_tabs_component.rb` (dummy AND docs) still passing the array `transition:`, and the README carried the old `reactive_filter(input:)` sample + `transition: [...]` prose — all migrated. The docs observability section (in `performance.rb`, not the tooling page) gained the `defer.phlex_reactive` row + a `[reactive] defer …` log-line sample.
- **No client edit.** Every change compiles server-side to the existing wire, so the minified client and its vendored copy are untouched (the two build-drift guards stay green without a rebuild).

Closes #186.

author: jiyuuchc
body:
Closes item **B** of #277 (see the [refreshed analysis](https://github.com/biopb/biopb/issues/277#issuecomment-4908121903)).

## Problem
Format detection lived in two places that had to be kept in lockstep by hand: the adapter `claim()` protocol (the intended single home) and a parallel set of hardcoded tables in `config.py` (`detect_source_type`, `scan_directory_for_sources`, `_discover_by_type`). They had already drifted.

## What changed
- **Deleted `scan_directory_for_sources` and `_discover_by_type` — both were dead code.** `SourceConfig.__post_init__` always auto-fills `source_id`, so the `discover_sources` Case 3 branch that reached `_discover_by_type` (`type and not source_id`) is unreachable; `scan_directory_for_sources` had no caller but its own recursion. Neither had any test.
- **Narrowed `detect_source_type` to remote URL-scheme routing** (`grpc(+tls)://` → `tensor-server`), its one non-duplicative and only test-pinned job. Its filesystem-format tables duplicated adapter knowledge and had gone stale — e.g. it mapped plain non-OME `.tif` → `"ome-tiff"`, but the adapters route those to bioio/`TiffSequenceAdapter` and `OmeTiffAdapter` *declines* them. Every local path now returns `None`.
- **Removed the legacy fallback in `discover_sources`:** a typeless local file that no adapter claims is now a hard error (fail-loud) rather than a guessed, often-wrong type.

The adapters are now the single source of truth for format detection.

## Testing
- Full `biopb-tensor-server` suite: **1090 passed, 1 skipped** (no regressions).
- **+2 tests** pinning the narrowed contract: local paths return `None` from `detect_source_type`; an unclaimed file raises instead of guessing.

Net **−292 / +19** in `config.py`.
